title: Commanders to sign Van Jefferson to practice squad
summary: Wide receiver Van Jefferson did not make the cut to the 53-man roster in Washington, but he's rejoining the Commanders ahead of their season opener.
full_text: Wide receiver Van Jefferson did not make the cut to the 53-man roster in Washington, but he's rejoining the Commanders ahead of their season opener. According to multiple reports, Jefferson will sign with the team's practice squad. Jefferson initially signed with the team in March and was let go at the end of August. Jefferson had 29 catches for 350 yards and a touchdown while with the Titans last season. He opened his career with the Rams and spent three-plus seasons with the team before a midseason trade to the Falcons in 2023. He played for the Steelers in 2024. Terry McLaurin, Stefon Diggs, third-round pick Antonio Williams, Dyami Brown, Luke McCaffrey, Treylon Burks, and Jaylin Lane are the wideouts on the active roster for the Commanders.
author: Josh Alper

title: Broncos to bring Taylor Rapp back to practice squad
summary: Veteran safety Taylor Rapp is heading back to Denver.
full_text: Veteran safety Taylor Rapp is heading back to Denver. Rapp signed with the Broncos last month, but left the team to attend to personal matters. Head coach Sean Payton said at the time that there was a strong chance Rapp would return to the organization and Rapp worked out last week with an eye on coming back to action. According to multiple reports, his return will come via the practice squad. Rapp can resume working out with the team right away and will be eligible to be elevated to the active roster for games. Rapp played in 36 games for the Bills over the last three seasons and he made 57 appearances for the Rams over his first four years in the NFL. He has 488 tackles, 12 interceptions, two sacks, two forced fumbles and four fumble recoveries for his career.
author: Josh Alper

title: Nico Collins: CJ Stroud is built for everything
summary: Texans quarterback CJ Stroud is entering a critical fourth season, particularly after his four-interception performance in the divisional round that helped end the club's 2025 postseason.
full_text: Texans quarterback CJ Stroud is entering a critical fourth season, particularly after his four-interception performance in the divisional round that helped end the club's 2025 postseason. Houston General Manager Nick Caserio said last week that if the club and Stroud don’t work out a contract extension before the season begins on Sunday, then it won’t be addressed until the offseason. That would give the team more time to evaluate Stroud. But it would also give Stroud the opportunity to set himself up for a bigger payday with a strong 2026. One of Stroud’s top weapons, receiver Nico Collins, said recently that he feels the quarterback is prepared to execute well in the coming season. " He’s built for everything ," Collins said, via DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN. "We believe in him, we love him. This is the best position he can be in right now. I feel like he is about to go out and show the whole world what he's made of, and I can't wait. We got his back 100 percent, all the way." Stroud, the No. 2 overall pick of the 2023 draft, completed 64.5 percent of his passes for 3,041 yards with 19 touchdowns and eight interceptions in 14 regular-season games last year. He completed 51.9 percent of his throws for 462 yards with two TDs and five picks in the postseason.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Michael Penix will be inactive in Week 1
summary: The Falcons will be starting Tua Tagovailoa in Week 1 against the Steelers and they won't be turning to Michael Penix if they decide to make a change during the game.
full_text: The Falcons will be starting Tua Tagovailoa in Week 1 against the Steelers and they won't be turning to Michael Penix if they decide to make a change during the game. Head coach Kevin Stefanski said at a Monday press conference that Penix will be inactive for the season opener. Cooper Rush will be the backup to Tagovailoa. Penix was cleared for full football activities in late August and did not play in the preseason, but Stefanski said that he has been pleased with the quarterback's progress as he returns from a torn ACL. "We're all on the same page , and feel good about where he is heading," Stefanski said, via Tori McElhaney of the team's website. Stefanski did not say when he thinks Penix will be ready for game action or what the quarterback depth chart will look like once that's the case, which should make updates on the plans for the position a regular part of life in Atlanta for the near future.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mike Evans: None of my injuries this summer were significant
summary: 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans did not practice much at training camp this summer due to injuries, but he's not concerned about his health heading into Thursday's opener against the Rams.
full_text: '' 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans did not practice much at training camp this summer due to injuries, but he's not concerned about his health heading into Thursday's opener against the Rams. Evans missed time with groin and quad issues and he has a history of hamstring injuries that have cost him time, but he told reporters at a press conference in Australia that this summer's time off was more about precaution than any limitations he was feeling. “The training staff, they did a great job working with me ," Evans said. "I know I'm an older player. I've had probably over a thousand practices, football practices in my life now, so I know what I'm doing out there. They know what they're doing. They did a good job taking care of me. None of my injuries were significant. If it was a game week, I wouldn't have missed any time.” Evans was always set to play a big role in the 49ers' offense, but injuries to Ricky Pearsall and Christian Kirk have made him an even more significant piece of the offensive puzzle. That makes it good news that he's feeling well heading into Week 1 and will make keeping him on the field vital to the team's hopes for the whole season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Greg Newsome: Past battles with George Pickens will make Sunday a little more special
summary: Sunday night's game between the Giants and the Cowboys will provide a chance for Greg Newsome and George Pickens to renew their relationship.
full_text: Sunday night's game between the Giants and the Cowboys will provide a chance for Greg Newsome and George Pickens to renew their relationship. The two men last faced off when Newsome was a Browns cornerback and Pickens was a Steelers wide receiver during the 2024 season. On a Hail Mary attempt at the end of a 24-19 Browns win in Week 12, Newsome and Pickens wrestled with each other and then continued their scuffle after the ball fell incomplete. The physical interaction morphed into a battle of words , but Pickens missed the second game between the AFC North teams with a hamstring injury and the two players never met last season. They'll be back on the same field this week and Newsome downplayed the idea of having unfinished business while acknowledging the history between the players adds to the matchup. “I wouldn’t say that ,” Newsome said, via Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News . “I would just say every receiver I go against there’s technically unfinished business. My job is to shut them out no matter what. Obviously I’ve had a lot of battles with him, so it’s gonna be a little more special. But my job is to shut them out.” Newsome praised Pickens as being "great at the catch point" and also noted how good CeeDee Lamb is before adding that "I like our chances" of winning the game. That would be just the start to the John Harbaugh era that the Giants are looking for in Week 1.
author: Josh Alper

title: Michael Irvin defends Jed York after recent arrest
summary: On Thursday night, the 49ers and Rams will play in Australia — and the game will be streamed by Netflix.
full_text: On Thursday night, the 49ers and Rams will play in Australia — and the game will be streamed by Netflix. One of the Netflix pregame analysts has already shared some strong feelings about a recent issue involving the owner of the 49ers. Hall of Famer Michael Irvin has publicly defended Jed York for his recent arrest, and no-contest plea, on misdemeanor charges arising from a prostitution sting in East Palestine, Ohio. “He got divorced five, six months ago, so I’m like, ‘Man, come on. Is that really a crime? ’ Let that man go. Leave it alone,” Irvin told N3on on a Twitch stream, via Qwame Skinner of Awful Announcing . “Like, imagine if . . . you’re going through a divorce and some, and some young girl, some pretty girl come up to you hitting on you, you know, and she’s undercover. You don’t know. And I don’t know how that happened or what happened with him.” What happened with York wasn't that. He actively sought someone out on a website that was part of the sting operation. After his third attempt to make contact was successful, the meeting — and the trap — were set. Irvin still has no problem with the situation. “Everybody’s paying for it," Irvin said. "You take [a girlfriend] out to eat, you’re paying for it. Everybody’s paying for it. So what are we doing? Why we gotta embarrass this man for 140 dollars? People think, ‘You’re a billionaire. Why didn’t you go to high-end places?’ The high-end places get you in trouble all the time.” No one is embarrassing York. He created the situation on his own. And, obviously, his risk-reward calculation surely included the theoretical possibility that he'd end up in handcuffs for reasons other than the way handcuffs possibly would be utilized during such encounters. Making Irvin's comments more relevant is the fact that he'll be on the 49ers-Rams pregame broadcast. Will Netflix embrace the subject and give Irvin a chance to repeat his viewpoint to a much larger live audience? Will Netflix steer clear of it? There's also a third possibility: Netflix doesn't add the subject to the planned topics to address, and Irvin finds a way to bring it up. However it goes, it's all the more reason to tune in on Thursday night to hear what Irvin has to say about it, if anything. And if he says anything, there's a good chance he'll say everything .
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean McVay expects Puka Nacua, Alaric Jackson to be available Thursday
summary: Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua and left tackle Alaric Jackson are both on the team's active roster on Monday and the team isn't expecting that to change ahead of their opener against the 49ers.
full_text: Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua and left tackle Alaric Jackson are both on the team's active roster on Monday and the team isn't expecting that to change ahead of their opener against the 49ers. Nacua and Jackson's off-field issues led to questions about potential league discipline this offseason, but they have not been suspended or put on paid leave at this point. On Sunday, Rams head coach Sean McVay said that he has no reason to believe that will change in the next couple of days. "Yeah, absolutely," McVay said when asked if he expected the pair to be available, via Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com. "That's what I’ve heard . I haven't heard anything different." The status of the two players could change at some point in the future, but the status quo looks like it will remain in place for at least another week.
author: Josh Alper

title: Patriots OC Josh McDaniels: I have to do a better job of limiting Seahawks opportunities
summary: The Patriots will kick off the 2026 season against the same team that dashed their hopes of winning the Super Bowl and that will lead to some reflection on what went wrong against the Seahawks at Levi's Stadium in February.
full_text: ' The Patriots will kick off the 2026 season against the same team that dashed their hopes of winning the Super Bowl and that will lead to some reflection on what went wrong against the Seahawks at Levi's Stadium in February. Seattle's overwhelming defensive performance is at the top of that list. The Seahawks had six sacks and three takeaways during their 29-13 win and the New England offense's inability to handle pressure throughout the game swung things in Seattle's direction. During a Sunday press conference, Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels pointed the finger squarely at himself for those shortcomings. “Whether it’s the rush concepts that they had when they didn’t blitz or the the pressures that they used, they created some opportunities for themselves ," McDaniels said. "I didn't do a good enough job. Point it at me. They did a great job. They 'out-everythinged' us in the game. Start with coaching and that comes back to me. We have a lot of things we learned, but I think this will be a different game, I think it will be a new game. It's a new year. We have some different players. They have a few guys that are new. We’ll see how different it is as the complexion of the game unfolds. They certainly found some opportunities last year, and hopefully we've done a good job trying to limit those as we go into Wednesday night." While McDaniels is looking inward, others pointed to left tackle Will Campbell's rough outing as a leading piece of what went wrong for the Patriots. Campbell dealt with a knee injury leading into the game and McDaniels said he's confident that the 2025 first-rounder is on the right track heading into Wednesday night. “I don’t look at it as a rebound. I look at it as the progression of a second-year player. . . . He's had a really good mindset all year," McDaniels said. "Locked in, good spring, good camp trying to work on the things he knows at his position are important and critical to his improvement." Whatever the mix of coaching and execution, all of the pieces will need to come together for the Patriots to pull off a road win this week.
author: Josh Alper

title: All 2026 quarterback competitions went to the older players
summary: Training camp opened with four, and potentially five, NFL quarterback competitions.
full_text: ' Training camp opened with four, and potentially five, NFL quarterback competitions. In the end, all five jobs went to the older of the two primary contenders. The first decision came in Minnesota, where Kyler Murray prevailed over 2024 top-10 selection J.J. McCarthy in the first competition to be resolved, before the first preseason game. The backup job there also has apparently gone to the older player, with Carson Wentz seemingly leapfrogging McCarthy. (The Vikings have yet to release their Week 1 depth chart.) Minnesota will enter the season with three former high first-round picks in their quarterback room. Murray was No. 1 overall in 2019, and Wentz was the second overall pick in 2016. The next decision was made by the Browns, where Deshaun Watson was made the starter (at least for Week 1 and likely Week 2) two weeks ago today, over 2025 fifth-rounder Shedeur Sanders. Watson was the 12th overall pick in 2017. Last week, the Raiders finally declared that Kirk Cousins, who entered the league as a fourth-round pick in 2012, would start Week 1 over Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in 2026. And now the Falcons have gone with Tua Tagovailoa, pick No. 5 in 2020, over Michael Penix Jr., the eighth overall selection in 2024. That one feels even more tenuous than Watson in Cleveland; the Falcons were hoping Penix would be ready to go. Ultimately, they decided he wasn't — and Tua got the nod over Cooper Rush (who's technically older than Tua). The fifth competition never became one, because Jacoby Brissett got a new deal done before a hold in gave Gardner Minshew or Carson Beck a chance to learn the new offense and potentially supplant Brissett. In many situations, winning the starting job to start the season means securing the privilege of eventually being benched. That's a very real possibility for Watson, Cousins, and Tagovailoa. The safest of them all is Murray, who was likely signed to be the starter — and who is playing for a team that wants to have the same quarterback in place for all 17 regular-season games.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Giants to sign DL Dean Lowry to practice squad
summary: The Giants are expected to make a veteran addition to their defensive line group ahead of their Week 1 game against the Cowboys.
full_text: The Giants are expected to make a veteran addition to their defensive line group ahead of their Week 1 game against the Cowboys. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that they plan to sign Dean Lowry to their practice squad. Once signed, Lowry would be available to be one of the two players elevated to the active roster on gamedays. Lowry played for the Steelers the last two seasons, but did not play in 2025 due to a torn ACL and he was released as part of their final cuts this summer. He had five tackles and a sack in 12 games for the team in 2024 and has 271 tackles, 16.5 sacks, an interception, a forced fumble and five fumble recoveries in 132 career games for Pittsburgh, Minnesota and Green Bay. The Giants overhauled their defensive line this offseason. Shelby Harris, DJ Reader, C.J. Okoye, and sixth-rounder Bobby Jamison-Travis are all in their first season with the club.
author: Josh Alper

title: Falcons pick Tua Tagovailoa as their Week 1 starting quarterback
summary: Six days before the season opener, the Falcons have finally made their choice.
full_text: ' Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa will start on Sunday against the Steelers. The Falcons finally made the choice today, just six days before the start of the regular season, according to multiple reports. Tagovailoa was the favorite all along, but Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski declined to make the choice official. Tagovailoa was seemingly competing with Michael Penix for the job, but Penix is coming off a torn ACL last season and wasn't healthy enough to make it a real competition. The Falcons kept four quarterbacks on the 53-player roster, with Cooper Rush and Jack Strand in the quarterback room along with Tagovailoa and Penix. It's unknown at this point who will be No. 2 on Sunday. Sunday's game will mark Tagovailoa's second straight game in Pittsburgh, as it was also the site of his last game with the Dolphins, a 28-15 loss after which he was benched for the rest of the season. Tagovailoa will hope he has more job stability as the starting quarterback in Atlanta, but he might not: Given how long it took Stefanski to make Tagovailoa the starter, he might decide quickly to move on if Tagovailoa isn't working out.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Trent Williams is a captain for the 14th time as 49ers choose same captains as last year
summary: The 49ers have a stable group of veteran leaders, and as a result they're a rare NFL team that will have all the same captains two years in a row. 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed that the players elected the same eight team captains that they elected for the 2025 season: defensive lineman Nick Bosa, fullback Kyle Juszczyk, tight end George Kittle, defensive back Deommodore Lenoir, running back Christian McCaffrey, quarterback Brock Purdy, linebacker Fred Warner and offensive tackle Trent Williams.
full_text: '' The 49ers have a stable group of veteran leaders, and as a result they're a rare NFL team that will have all the same captains two years in a row. 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed that the players elected the same eight team captains that they elected for the 2025 season: defensive lineman Nick Bosa, fullback Kyle Juszczyk, tight end George Kittle, defensive back Deommodore Lenoir, running back Christian McCaffrey, quarterback Brock Purdy, linebacker Fred Warner and offensive tackle Trent Williams. Williams has a distinct honor in NFL history: He is a 49ers captain for the seventh time, and he was previously a team captain in Washington for seven seasons. The NFL doesn't keep official records of team captaincies, but Williams is believed to be the only player in NFL history who has been a team captain for at least seven seasons on two different teams. Kittle has now been a 49ers team captain for nine seasons, with his teammates choosing him every year but his rookie year. Warner is in his seventh season as a 49ers captain. Kittle, Warner and Williams will all wear the gold "C" on their jerseys that denote they've been captains for at least five seasons. Purdy and Bosa are both captains for the fourth time. Juszczyk is a 49ers captain for the third time, and so is McCaffrey, who was previously a Panthers captain for four seasons. This is Lenoir's second season as captain.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss passes for 336 yards, runs for 60 in 41-38 win in opener
summary: Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who may prove to be among the most polarizing prospects in the 2027 NFL draft, is off to a good start to his final season of college football.
full_text: Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who may prove to be among the most polarizing prospects in the 2027 NFL draft, is off to a good start to his final season of college football. Chambliss completed 21 of 36 passes for 336 yards, with three touchdowns and one interception, and also added nine carries for 60 yards and a rushing touchdown, as No. 9 Ole Miss beat No. 24 Louisville 41-38. A year ago, Chambliss was a little-known transfer from Division II Ferris State who wasn't even expected to start at Ole Miss, but he became more than just a starter. He became one of the best players in the country, leading Ole Miss to the College Football Playoff. So why is Chambliss polarizing as a prospect? He's on the smaller side (listed at 6-foot-1, possibly shorter) and is already 24 years old and in his sixth year of college football, so he may have less less upside and room for growth than some of the younger, less experienced quarterback projects. Will Chambliss be a first-round pick? A Day Three pick? There's a wide range of potential outcomes, but he can help his case by continuing to play like he did against Louisville.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Kyle Shanahan "a little confused" playing Friday in Australia, which is Thursday in America
summary: "I feel like I'm in the future," Shanahan said on Sunday. "I call today Tuesday. No, wait, sorry, I call today Wednesday."
full_text: For the American TV audience, the 49ers and Rams play on Thursday night. But they'll be playing in Australia, where it will already be Friday. And 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said in Australia on Monday (which was Sunday in the US) that he's trying to keep his team on a normal routine as if they were playing on a Sunday — which for Australians is a Monday. Confused? So is Shanahan. "We're a little confused with — when I look at my clock and it says a time and then I try to see my family's time and then it says the time, but it says yesterday. I don't even get how that's possible," Shanahan said. "So I feel like I'm in the future. And then also when we play on Friday, which I think is a Thursday in the US, we're such creatures of habit. So I call today Tuesday. No, wait, sorry, I call today Wednesday. Which is the first day we put in a game plan. But I think it's Monday. However, though, it's Sunday in the present. So, like I'm gonna mess that up all week if you guys ask me. But today is just our first day of the game plan, which is a Wednesday, and we'll put in some on a Thursday. Friday's the final part of the game plan. Saturday, we walk through and we play on Sunday, which is a Friday in Australia and a Thursday in the US. So, don't ever make me do that again." Shanahan said he's adhering to the same schedule as the Rams, who are still in the US, and that the 49ers won't be putting out an injury report until the Rams do. "Because we're technically in the future, from where we're from, and the Rams are in the present, I don't have to talk about injuries until tomorrow," Shanahan said on Monday in Australia, or Sunday in the US. Despite flying 16 hours to a place with a 17-hour time difference, Shanahan said he's suffering no ill effects from the travel and will be ready to coach his team on Thursday Night Football on Friday. "It's taken a couple days to adjust but I'm feeling real good today," Shanahan said on Monday — or Sunday.
author: Michael David Smith

title: 49ers' Sam Okuayinonu has "bad injury" to his foot, hopes to play by end of season
summary: When 49ers defensive lineman Sam Okuayinonu hurt his foot in the final practice before the team flight to Australia, there was hope that he could make a later flight and still play in the opener.
full_text: When 49ers defensive lineman Sam Okuayinonu hurt his foot in the final practice before the team flight to Australia, there was hope that he could make a later flight and still play in the opener. The injury proved to be a lot worse than that. 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said Okuayinonu injured the same foot that already had a plate in it from a previous injury, and the hope now is just that he can get on the field at some point this season. "He had a plate in his foot a while ago, and on our bonus practice the day we came, just stepped on it and it broke," Shanahan said. "He's going to have to get surgery. It's a bad injury. Hopefully we can get him back later in the year, but it was a real tough loss. Hurt for Sam O, hurt for our team, but hopefully we can take care of business and he can come back later in the year." Okuayinonu was expected to have a big role in the 49ers' defensive line rotation this year after starting 12 regular-season games and both playoff games for them last year. Losing him just before the start of the season will be a challenge for the 49ers' defense.
author: Michael David Smith

title: NFL's new three-strike system doesn't apply until the 2026 regular season
summary: The NFL and the NFL Players Association have agreed to a new three-strike formula that will trigger automatic suspensions for repeated violations of five specific safety rules: hip-drop tackles, horse-collar tackles, launching, hits on defenseless players, and blindside blocks.
full_text: '' The NFL and the NFL Players Association have agreed to a new three-strike formula that will trigger automatic suspensions for repeated violations of five specific safety rules: hip-drop tackles, horse-collar tackles, launching, hits on defenseless players, and blindside blocks. Per the NFLPA, the new procedure doesn't commence until the 2026 regular season. Which means that players who were fined for any of the five specific rules won't carry them into the games that count. That's good news for any of the various players who were dinged for the infractions that otherwise would have counted toward a potential suspension. It applies to Cardinals safety Dadrion Taylor-Demerson, who was fined $7,148 for a hit on a defenseless player in Week 2 of the preseason. And to Cardinals safety Wydett Williams, who was fined $4,935 for a hit on a defenseless player in the same game. And to Bengals linebacker Shaka Heyward, who was fined $5,972 for a hip-drop tackle in Week 2 of the preseason. (He's currently on Cincinnati's practice squad.) And to Chiefs tight end Jake Briningstool, who was fined $4,972 in Week 2 of the preseason for a blindside block. And to Rams linebacker Darryl Peterson III, who was fined $4,935 in Week 1 of the preseason for a horse-collar tackle. (He's currently on the L.A. practice squad.) And to Buccaneers linebacker David Walker, who was fined $6,254 in Week 1 of the preseason for a blindside block. None of them will be on strike two when the regular season begins. Which means that all of them will still be three violations of each specific rule away from a suspension. Again, a one-game suspension happens only if a player violates the same rule three times. A player can, in theory, violate each of the rules twice and still not be suspended.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyle Shanahan expects Aaron Donald to play on Thursday night
summary: Aaron Donald is back.
full_text: Aaron Donald is back. And the coach of the first team on the Rams' docket expects to see No. 99 on Thursday night in Melbourne. Via Sarah Barshop of ESPN, 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters on Sunday that he " definitely " anticipates Donald playing in the Week 1 showdown down under. Shanahan explained that he "wasn't crushed" when Donald announced his return after two years of retirement, "because I decided a month ago it was happening." "So I prepared for that the right way, and it is what it is," Shanahan added. "He's a hell of a player and we'll have our work cut out for him." Donald's unexpected retirement after the 2023 season prompted cheering in the 49ers' facility. "I was like, 'What the hell's going on?'" Shanahan said. "And then I got it on my phone and it was probably the most we've celebrated in the offseason ever. . . . And then it was the exact opposite this year." Although 49ers left tackle Trent Williams has a good chance to hold his own against new Rams defensive end Myles Garrett, rookie left guard Carver Willis could be forced to contend with Donald, in the ultimate "welcome to the NFL" moment — as Aaron Donald welcomes himself back to the league he dominated for a decade before deciding he was "full." Donald is hungry again. And the first of 17 courses is the 49ers. If Donald plays. Shanahan is bracing for it.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyle Shanahan expects 49ers fan takeover vs. Rams in Melbourne
summary: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan has been salty about the Rams' desire to export a home game to Australia, in order to avoid yet another San Francisco-fan takeover of SoFi Stadium.
full_text: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan has been salty about the Rams' desire to export a home game to Australia, in order to avoid yet another San Francisco-fan takeover of SoFi Stadium. Now that Shanahan and the 49ers have hunkered down in Melbourne, Shanahan feels differently. Via David Lombardi of the San Francisco Standard , Shanahan explained in a Sunday press conference that he has a different outlook on the situation. Shanahan reiterated his belief that the league " let the Rams off the hook " by allowing them to hand-pick the annual showdown against the 49ers as the game to be sent overseas. Shanahan currently believes "it won't be much different" in Austrialia — and he expects the so-called Faithful to take over the 100,000-seat Melbourne Cricket Ground on Thursday night. It really is a consequential game, given the impact of the outcome on the tiebreakers within the division. Arguably, a game like that shouldn't be part of the international series. But if the Rams gave up their supposed home-field advantage against the 49ers in order to avoid the embarrassment of having red far outnumber blue in the L.A. venue, it apparently won't be much different for the NFL's first-ever game in Australia.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean McVay confirms Rams will fly Tuesday night for Thursday night game in Australia
summary: The Rams are dealing with the short straw of a long trip to Australia by making the stay as short as possible.
full_text: The Rams are dealing with the short straw of a long trip to Australia by making the stay as short as possible. On Sunday, coach Sean McVay addressed the very different approach to playing in Melbourne, treating it as a quick-in, quick-out business trip at a time when the 49ers have basically moved there. “The guys had an idea, but I tell them, ‘Hey, let's take it a day at a time, but for your guys' understanding we'll leave on what would be equivalent — I look at it as Friday evening," McVay said. "It’s Tuesday night for you guys, but it would be the equivalent of Friday evening. Sleep through the night and then we'll get there and we have kind of a rhythm. But I believe everything that we do, I think our guys, and I would hope — the most important thing to me is they know that, hey, everything we do is what we think is best. "It doesn't mean that we think we're right and a different approach is wrong. It's just what we think is best based on the things that we've done and what we've learned over our time here. That's what will always consistently drive our decision-making processes is with the players first and foremost at the forefront of our minds in every decision that we make and keeping guys in their normal rhythm and routine. Then some of the different things that we've done behind the scenes of people that have done this whether it's different sports or people that have made these types of trips. We've tested it out with some guys and we feel like it's been positive, but that's what went into the approach." The goal is to minimize the time in Melbourne. "What gives me confidence is I'm not going to really make it a big deal," McVay said. "It's, ‘Hey, this is what the reality is. We've got a long way to go, but let's be ready to rock when that three-hour window that we're allotted comes.’ That's what it is. To spend a bunch of time talking about it — I get it with you guys, too, like I understand your questions but for me, I've told you guys what our approach is. Our expectation is our guys will be ready to go and I'm not worried about it because I know what our plans are. We're going to follow that plan and then we're going to focus on our preparation and try to go be at our best and go swing when we get a chance to play against a great team." While San Francisco decided to go early to Australia in order to fully acclimate, the first game of the season isn't the only game of the season. The 49ers will have to re-acclimate to America when they return from Melbourne, for a Week 2 trap game against the Dolphins. The Rams, by minimizing their time in the land down under, may be less under the gun to get ready for a Week 2 Monday night visit from the Giants. Either way, the league doesn't care. The goal is to globalize the game. The inconveniences imposed upon two high-end NFC contenders don't matter. The short-term impact on their prospects for the season is taking a back seat to the obsession with making a billion-dollar domestic business into a trillion-dollar international enterprise.
author: Mike Florio

title: Mike Macdonald on Terrion Arnold: He's in the building and learning
summary: Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold starts the 2026 season on paid leave, due to eight felony charges arising from an alleged armed robbery and kidnapping.
full_text: Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold starts the 2026 season on paid leave, due to eight felony charges arising from an alleged armed robbery and kidnapping. And while he can't practice or play, Arnold is with the team. “He’s in the building and being part of our program and learning the heck out of our defense," coach Mike Macdonald told reporters on Saturday regarding Arnold. "Keep training and stay ready for when there’s an opportunity." It's still unknown when an opportunity will arise. In general, players on the Commissioner Exempt list due to criminal charges remain there until the case is over and discipline, if any, is imposed by the league. But the NFL has deviated from that approach in the past; in 2024, then-Patriots safety Jabrill Peppers spent seven games on paid leave, returning before his case went to trial. (He was acquitted of domestic battery in January 2025.) Arnold's next court date happens on October 5. A trial hasn't been scheduled. Barring a plea deal, it's unlikely Arnold's case will end before the conclusion of the 2026 season. The overriding question is whether the league will stick to its general approach that players will remain on paid leave until the case ends, or whether the league will allow Arnold to return at some point later in the season.
author: Mike Florio

title: With opener looming, Rams DE Myles Garrett returns to practice
summary: Knee injury had kept 2025 defensive player of the year out for a while.
full_text: One of the biggest acquisitions by any team of the 2026 offseason has been out of practice throughout most of the preseason. But Rams defensive end Myles Garrett returned to practice on Sunday, after missing plenty of time with a knee issue. “Yep, he's going to do some stuff," coach Sean McVay told reporters on Sunday regarding Garrett's anticipated participation. The Rams will issue their first injury report for Week 1 on Monday. That will contain some information, but not much, regarding Garrett's specific injury and his level of participation. Our guess? He'll be listed as limited (knee). And he'll likely end up being described on Wednesday as questionable (knee). And then the 49ers will find out, along with the rest of us, whether and to what extent Garrett will be available on Thursday night in Australia.
author: Mike Florio

title: Brian Fleury embraces his first opportunity as an offensive coordinator
summary: Brian Fleury's moment has arrived.
full_text: '' Brian Fleury's moment has arrived. After more than 20 years of coaching at the college and pro level, Fleury will soon embark on his biggest job yet — offensive coordinator of an NFL franchise. And not just any franchise. He's running the offense for the Seattle Seahawks. "I didn’t think that grandly," Fleury told reporters on Sunday regarding his career goals. "As a kid, I always wanted to be a part of the National Football League, so that part of it has always been there. I’ve always had a lot of respect and admiration for the people that play football in this league and the people that have helped build it from the ground up, but it was really more about teaching for me early on, like taking what I knew from the knowledge standpoint and being able to help people get better.” But it can be a lonely existence, when it comes to seeking input from others. Said Fleury on that subject, “Unfortunately, the people I would seek advice from aren't interested in seeing us do well, so not many.” That's a direct byproduct of Fleury taking the Seattle job after seven seasons as an assistant coach on Kyle Shanahan's staff in San Francisco. Fleury arrived as a low-level defensive quality control coach before flipping to the offensive side of the ball the next year. From there, he was promoted to tight ends coach before adding in 2025 the title of run game coordinator. He's now stepping into the shoes of Klint Kubiak, who did enough in one year in the position to become a head coach. It increases the degree of difficult for Fleury, especially since head coach Mike Macdonald is a defensive specialist. Fleury's preferred system may yield in large part to the things the Seahawks did well enough in 2025 to win a Super Bowl. Last year, for example, the promotion of John Morton to replace Bears coach Ben Johnson as the Lions' offensive coordinator didn't go well — and Morton had been in the building. Fleury is a newcomer to an offense that wasn't broken. And so while it's a great opportunity for Fleury to take the next step, it's also a high wire. One false move, and his first year as an offensive coordinator could be his last, for now or possibly for good. Regardless, Fleury is embracing the moment. “I'm looking forward to it," Fleury said. "I've had more fun out here at practice these last two days than any of the last seven years, so I'm excited to continue this journey and get out there for the first time on Wednesday." When he does, he'll watch his former employer's arch rival hang a banner, minutes before Fleury is charged with the task of leading the offense to another one.
author: Mike Florio

title: Giants extend guard Jon Runyan Jr. by two years
summary: The Giants are using the last Sunday before the start of the 2026 regular season to take care of some internal business.
full_text: ' The Giants are using the last Sunday before the start of the 2026 regular season to take care of some internal business. After extending quarterback Jameis Winston by two years, the Giants signed guard Jon Runyan Jr. to a two-year, $22 million extension. The contract was announced by Runyan's agent, Drew Rosenhaus. Jon Runyan Jr. is now under contract through 2028. The son of former NFL offensive lineman Jon Runyan, Jon Jr. was a sixth-round pick of the Packers in 2020. After four years with the Packers (three as a full-time starter), Runyan Jr. signed with the Giants. He has been a full-time starter for the Giants since 2024, and he obviously has done enough to persuade coach John Harbaugh that Runyan Jr. is part of the solution for a team that has been sufficiently problematic to have six head coaches since 2011, the last year in which the team won a Super Bowl. In his six-year career, Runyan Jr. has 96 regular-season appearances, with 79 starts. He is expected to be the starting left guard next Sunday night, when the Giants host the Cowboys on the first Sunday night of the new year.
author: Mike Florio

title: Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (ankle) was limited in practice on Sunday
summary: The Seahawks have been saying very little about safety Nick Emmanwori's recovery from offseason ankle surgery that happened in July.
full_text: The Seahawks have been saying very little about safety Nick Emmanwori's recovery from offseason ankle surgery that happened in July. On Sunday, they were required to say one specific thing — whether and to what extent he practiced. On the first official injury report of the season, Emmanwori was listed as a limited participant, due to the ankle. The report comes one day after coach Mike Macdonald was asked whether he could characterize Emmanwori's progress over the last month and said, "Not really." Macdonald nevertheless praised Emmanwori's handling of the overall process. “Nick’s been fantastic," Macdonald said. "Our training staff has been fantastic, and it wasn’t an easy situation for him. He’s done a great job to work through all of that.” Not practicing on Sunday was safety Ty Okada (hamstring). Limited were guard Anthony Bradford (knee), receiver Tory Horton (hamstring), tackle Josh Jones (quadricep). Full participants were tight end A.J. Barner (oblique), cornerback Julian Neal (quadricep), and running back Emmanuel Wilson (hamstring).

title: RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) misses practice, three days before Week 1
summary: Henderson injured ankle nearly two weeks ago.
full_text: In their first official injury report of the 2026 season, the Patriots don't have many names. One stands out. Running back TreVeyon Henderson did not practice, due to an ankle injury. It happened nearly two weeks ago, when Henderson slipped on the turf at practice . He hasn't practiced since then. If Henderson, a second-round pick in 2025, can't go, it will mean more work for Rhamondre Stevenson. Corey Kiner is the only other tailback on the 53-man roster; Hassan Haskins and Lan Larison (that's a lot of alliteration from anxious anchors placed in powerful posts) are on the practice squad. Also not practicing on Sunday were defensive tackle Christian Barmore (knee) and offensive lineman Ben Brown (knee). The Patriots will issue another report on Monday. The Tuesday report will include the official designation for the injured players — questionable, doubtful, or out.

title: Giants, QB Jameis Winston agree to two-year extension
summary: No. 1 overall pick in 2015 embraces his status as No. 2 on the depth chart.
full_text: The No. 1 overall pick in the 2015 draft continues to embrace his status as a No. 2 quarterback. Per multiple reports, the Giants and Jameis Winston have agreed to terms on a two-year, $13 million extension. The move puts Winston under contract through 2028, as the clear backup to Jaxson Dart. Winston became the Week 1 starter as a rookie in Tampa. After five seasons with the Buccaneers, he spent four years with the Saints (starting 10 games), one with the Browns (starting seven), and one with the Giants (starting two). In lieu of finishing his current deal and becoming a free agent in March 2027 (where he could have potentially found a spot to compete for a starting role), Winston decided to stay put, with a total commitment of three years. It doesn't hurt Winston to be in New York, given that he seems to be destined to become a star in the media space, once his playing career ends.

title: Inside Harrison Smith's eleventh-hour deal to return to the Vikings
summary: Vikings legend Harrison Smith is back for a fifteenth season in Minnesota.
full_text: Vikings legend Harrison Smith is back for a fifteenth season in Minnesota. The initial reports regarding the contract ($12.25 million base, up to $16.25 million max) were surprising to some. An executive from another team was skeptical of the reported value, based on Smith's performance in 2025 and the fact that he had been available to anyone, with no takers, throughout the offseason, training camp, and preseason. The contract indeed carries a $12.25 million base package, technically. Here's the breakdown: 1. Signing bonus: $6.95 million. 2. 2026 base salary: $1.3 million. 3. 2026 per-game active roster bonus: $235,294 per game ($4 million total). The $4 million in incentives are based on $1 million for earning a playoff berth (wild-card or bye), $1.5 million for winning in the divisional round, $2 million for winning the NFC Championship, or $4 million for winning the Super Bowl. Basically, if the Vikings end up paying Smith $16.25 million, it will be the best money the franchise has ever spent. The very high per-game roster bonuses reduce Smith's guarantee to $8.25 million. If he plays all year, he gets to $12.25 million. Smith arguably has greater value to the Vikings than he would have to a new team. As one source put it, Smith is a "glue guy," whose mere presence makes the Minnesota defense and the rest of the team better. As to his late availability, we're told that when other teams inquired about him, Smith made it clear that he wasn't going to attend training camp. Which made a return to Minnesota even more likely, if he decided to play for another season. It may have been inevitable. Either way, Smith returns for one more run with the team that made him a first-round pick in 2012. The defense is more than good enough to compete, and to contend. If the offense carries its weight, they could make the playoffs and win their first postseason game since 2019.
author: Mike Florio

title: Falcons name Tua Tagovailoa starting QB: What to expect from former Dolphins Pro Bowler
summary: Tagovailoa will become Atlanta's sixth different Week 1 starting quarterback in as many seasons when the Falcons face the Steelers
full_text:
The Falcons named Tua Tagovailoa their starting quarterback Monday. He beat out Michael Penix Jr . in a stop-and-start, injury-impacted quarterback battle and will make his official Atlanta debut Sunday against the Steelers .
Tagovailoa will be Atlanta's sixth consecutive different Week 1 starting quarterback.
The Dolphins released Tagovailoa, 28, last year, and he subsequently signed a one-year deal with the Falcons. Expected to go head-to-head with Penix for the starting nod, he essentially won the job de facto. Penix, recovering from yet another knee injury, wasn't able to participate in full-team drills until after the team's second preseason game , and he did not play in the third preseason game either.
Penix "did not believe that he was ready" for Week 1, according to ESPN . Shortly after naming Tagovailoa the starter, coach Kevin Stefanski said Penix Jr. won't even be active in Week 1. Cooper Rush will be the backup quarterback.
Tagovailoa, on the other hand, had almost a full training camp and played in two preseason games, though the results were mixed at best. He struggled mightily in Week 1 of the preseason, did not play in Week 2 and then looked better in Week 3 -- though that game was against the Dolphins' backups. He had trouble handling snaps in both appearances, an issue that sometimes plagued him in Miami as well. Overall, he went 10-for-13 for 117 yards across the two cameos.
Tagovailoa reached some impressive highs -- a top-10 MVP finish in 2022 and a Pro Bowl and passing yards crown in 2023 -- in Miami, but he struggled last season, throwing 15 interceptions and eventually getting benched. With the Dolphins undergoing a major rebuild, they moved on from Tagovailoa despite record cap penalties .
He'll now hope to resurrect his career surrounded by superstar running back Bijan Robinson , standout wide receiver Drake London and a solid offensive line. Health will be a key, as he has played all 17 games just once in his career, but for now, he'll get the first shot to prove he can be the answer to Atlanta's quarterback woes.
If the last two seasons and this preseason are any indicators, this will be a bumpy ride. Tagovailoa admitted his first preseason performance "wasn't up to standard" after the Falcons got throttled by the Broncos . He was better in preseason Week 3, but again, that was against several Dolphins backups -- and many of Miami's starters are backup-quality players, so really, it was against guys simply hoping to make a roster or practice squad
Tagovailoa's propensity for getting rid of the ball as soon as possible -- and often accurately -- could technically fit, though his weak arm, limited mobility and turnover issues make the margins for error slim to none. Expect a heavy, heavy dose of Robinson, London and Kyle Pitts on quick-hitting throws. In the preseason, Tagovailoa's average pass went 2.0 yards downfield, a preposterously low number that will obviously rise when his games actually count. Still, throws like these will be commonplace, with YAC doing much of the work.
Tua finds Kyle Pitts Sr. for a 37-yard gain! Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/se0K7iEgFs
Last year, Tagovailoa's average release time was 2.59 seconds, the fastest in the NFL . His 6.8 air yards per attempt ranked 28th out of 33 qualifying quarterbacks. Those numbers will rise in part because Stefanski prefers more under-center play action, but still, there's a clear picture with Tagovailoa.
Tagovailoa won this quarterback battle simply by being available (and not being a complete disaster when available). Penix's extended recovery from injury meant he didn't really get a shot.
He will almost certainly get his shot this season, though. Tagovailoa's injury history is well-documented, ranging from several concussions to thumb, rib, finger, back and hip ailments ... and that's just in his NFL career. His dislocated hip while at Alabama also made him a completely different player.
Penix simply needs more time to get into the swing of things, and when he is physically ready, a quarterback change could be quickly in the offing.
The biggest beneficiary of a potential change down the road would be London, who has thrived in his short time sharing the field with Penix.
Michael Penix Jr. on field
Michael Penix Jr. not on field
Regardless of which quarterback plays the most this year, Atlanta will very likely be in the quarterback market next offseason. Stop me if you've heard this before. Here's the list of Week 1 starters since 2021:
The Falcons did the right (and easy) thing this summer by extending several members of the offensive core , but finding an answer at quarterback will be the biggest task for the new front office led by Matt Ryan and Ian Cunningham.

title: Defining success for NFL's seven biggest Super Bowl longshots, including Raiders, Jets and Titans
summary: For the NFL's biggest longshots, success could mean developing a franchise quarterback, evaluating a new coaching staff or positioning the roster for a pivotal 2027 offseason
full_text:
What does a successful season look like for these Super Bowl longshots? Las Vegas has been handicapping the upcoming season since the prior concluded in February and, through Super Bowl odds, expressed how it perceives each team. Seven teams held +10000 odds or worse. Unfortunately, four of those teams were on last year's list, too. The following is in order from shortest to longest odds:
Tennessee enters the second year with quarterback Cam Ward and the first year with coach Robert Saleh. At the bare minimum, the objective should be not to be on this list next year. A success would be feeling good about the Ward-Saleh pairing heading into 2027.
The Titans spent heavily, particularly on the defensive side of the ball ($125 million total guaranteed). It may take some time for that group to come together, but the hope is that they adopt Saleh's hard-nosed demeanor. If all goes as planned, the franchise will be tasked with replacing pieces of the operation next offseason rather than the operation itself, positioning them to take a big leap within the AFC South.
The vibes around the Falcons are not great, but few can boast the collection of elite offensive skill talent -- wide receiver Drake London , running back Bijan Robinson and tight end Kyle Pitts -- assembled in Atlanta.
The best possible outcome would be having clarity on Michael Penix Jr. , one way or another, entering the offseason. If Penix is fully healthy and establishes himself as an investment-caliber quarterback, it would allow them to funnel resources elsewhere. Alternatively, if neither Tua Tagovailoa nor Penix inspires confidence, it would open the door for the team to go in another direction at the position.
In either scenario, the Falcons would be staring down a full season from edge rushers James Pearce Jr . and Jalon Walker , as well as the hope that a new quarterback brings.  Atlanta will have the most salary cap space by a wide margin this offseason, according to Spotrac.
Las Vegas' best possible outlook boils down to the success of No. 1 overall selection Fernando Mendoza and first-year coach Klint Kubiak. Despite Kirk Cousins being named the Week 1 starter, Mendoza must see the field this season and showcase the skill set that enabled him to be drafted so early, which in turn creates optimism as the 2027 campaign begins.
Beyond Mendoza, the Raiders bringing in another supreme talent with an early draft pick as part of the long-term vision would be another step in the right direction.
Las Vegas ranks among the top-10 in projected salary cap space as well.
The Browns had arguably the best rookie class a year ago, and the early returns on the 2026 draft class have been promising as well. The limitations at quarterback have capped the potential of this season, but they have positioned themselves well to bring in that player next offseason through the trade of Myles Garrett .
In an ideal world, Cleveland would be feeling good about the collection of offensive rookie talent -- offensive tackle Spencer Fano and wide receivers Denzel Boston , KC Concepcion -- after the season, while simultaneously being in position to draft its quarterback of choice in 2027. In each of the past two years, the franchise has been in the top six overall of a one-quarterback draft, but failed to secure that player.
It is important to note that the 2027 season would be the first without quarterback Deshaun Watson on the roster since 2021.
New York is the most difficult to project because what is best for the franchise is not what is best for the coaching staff. Aaron Glenn knows his job is on the line and will be desperate for wins. Too many wins, however, could conceivably put a potential franchise quarterback outside of the organization's reach. They have three first-round picks to move up if another team is willing to deal, but what if it is like the 2024 NFL Draft, where every team in the top three overall selected a quarterback, and there was no other option? Could they thread the needle of being bad enough to draft a quarterback without trading all of their assets while also showing enough progress to retain the coaching staff? The proposition seems unlikely, but not impossible.
Additionally, if the organization can identify pieces of the future. Can D'Angelo Ponds hold up at cornerback? Is David Bailey the elite talent he was billed as during the pre-draft process? Will either Omar Cooper Jr . or Kenyon Sadiq emerge as essential outlets in the offense?
If one were to ask two Dolphins fans their ideal outcome for the upcoming season, each would likely give a different answer. The first may desire free agent acquisition Malik Willis to have a good season, and for the franchise to invest in Willis' supporting cast. Miami has a projected $104 million in salary cap space, fifth-most in the NFL . The second may wish for the team to bottom out and be in a position to draft a quarterback No. 1 overall next April.
The team drafted 13 players in the 2026 NFL Draft. If they can identify four or five starters among that group, then that would be a great outcome for the Dolphins. As it stands, running back De'Von Achane and potentially edge rusher Chop Robinson are the only impact performers on the roster.
Arizona has a lot of young talent on defense. If either defensive tackle Walter Nolen II or cornerback Will Johnson Jr. emerges as a blue-chip talent within that defense, then it greatly raises the ceiling of that unit. Cornerbacks Denzel Burke , Max Melton and Garrett Williams have all had positive moments in their respective careers as well. If defensive lineman Darius Robinson gives them anything, it will be icing on the cake.
Offensively, a positive outcome would be having confidence in coach Mike LaFleur's scheme and the way running back Jeremiyah Love , tight end Trey McBride, and wide receivers Michael Wilson Jr. and Marvin Harrison Jr . are deployed.
Having said all of that, next season will be a wash if they do not identify a sustainable quarterback situation. Jacoby Brissett may be fine in the short-term, and Carson Beck is capable of stringing together some decent performances, but the outlook for either becoming a long-term option is bleak.

title: Winners, losers, grades from Week 1 in college football; NFL season predictions produce shocker
summary: Plus it was a big weekend for the Americans at the US Open and FIBA Women's World Cup
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
For most teams in Week 1, the goal was simple: Beat a team you are supposed to beat. The opening slate was light on marquee matchups and heavy on contests between heavy favorites and massive underdogs. But even in an era where the powerhouses have all the resources in the world at their disposal, college football is college football. Surprises happen.
Look no further than No. 2 Oregon , which only narrowly escaped a very real upset bid from Boise State . The Ducks won in the end, but their defensive line was one of the nation's biggest losers of Week 1 . It was supposed to be an elite, impenetrable unit but instead looked vulnerable against a Group of Six squad. And that wasn't Oregon's only shortcoming in a game it trailed by double digits.
On the flip side, other national championship hopefuls took care of business and left no doubt. No. 7 Miami , for one, might have the best offense in the country. Is that an overreaction ? It sure won't be if Malachi Toney keeps playing like a Heisman Trophy contender .
And how about No. 13 Alabama ? The Crimson Tide was a touch underwhelming in the early years of the Kalen DeBoer era, but it did everything it was supposed to do in a 48-10 thumping of East Carolina . We'll give the team as a whole a "B" grade for turning in a mostly great but still imperfect effort. As for new starting quarterback Keelon Russell , our Brad Crawford graded his debut .
WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert announced her retirement on Friday . The league's first commissioner, who took office in 2019, will step away from the role at the end of the year.
Over more than seven years, Engelbert oversaw the league's most dramatic period of growth. With the introduction of three expansion teams (plus three more on the way by 2030), the signing of a massive $3.1 billion media rights deal, multiple collective bargaining agreements and numerous other achievements on her résumé, she leaves her post as an immensely successful commissioner.
But players and fans alike are not exactly sad to see her go. Our Lindsay Gibbs explains the other side of the equation.
Engelbert said there are already internal and external candidates for her replacement. She will remain on board until early 2027 if the league does not find a successor by Dec. 31. Who is worthy and capable of stepping into what is a more highly scrutinized role than ever? We have a few ideas:

title: 2026 NFL Week 1 early odds: Cowboys road favorites vs. Giants, while Panthers in familiar position vs. Bears
summary: Here's a look at the lines for Week 1 in the NFL as we open up the 2026 season
full_text:
After what feels like a blink of an eye and two decades all jumbled up into one, the NFL is finally back. In just a couple of days, the 2026 regular season will kick off in Seattle, where we'll see a rematch of Super Bowl LX between the Patriots and Seahawks . From there, we're off to the races and heading down to Australia for an early international matchup as the 49ers and Rams will kick off from Melbourne Cricket Ground. It'll be all gas, no brakes, until we get to Los Angeles for Super Bowl LXI.
As we shake off the rust and prepare to wager on the opening slate of the NFL season, let's remember that this is one of the trickiest times to bet on the league calendar. Need a refresher? Let's take a quick look back at the start of the 2025 season, where Week 1 offers a clear-cut example of its obscurity. Last year, the Raiders went into Foxborough and defeated the Patriots, 20-13, in the season opener. After that, New England went on to win the AFC and reach the Super Bowl, while Las Vegas earned the No. 1 overall pick following a league-worst 3-14 record.
With that in mind, it's important to have your head on a swivel in Week 1 because some funky results are bound to occur. Below, we'll take an early look at the Week 1 odds, highlighting the spread, total, and moneyline as we gear up for the new season.
All lines via DraftKings ; all games on Sunday unless noted)
Patriots at Seahawks (Wednesday)
Patriots +150, Seahawks -180
49ers at Rams (Thursday, in Australia)
Falcons +154, Steelers -185
Buccaneers +170, Bengals -205
Cardinals +410, Chargers -549
Packers +102, Vikings -122
Dolphins +160, Raiders -192
Commanders +180, Eagles -218
Broncos at Chiefs (Monday)
The defending champion Seahawks come into Week 1 after not only hoisting the Lombardi Trophy, but also covering a league-best 75% of their games in 2025 (including playoffs). However, they are a bit of a different club than the one that found itself in the winner's circle a year ago, most notably losing offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak and Super Bowl MVP running back Kenneth Walker III . They were also 6-4 ATS (60%) at Lumen Field last year. As for New England, they were quite stellar against the spread as well, notching a 13-7-1 ATS record over the course of the regular season and playoffs. That included a 7-2 ATS road record. This offseason, they added the likes of A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs on offense. One X-factor for this game that could certainly swing these odds is the status of All-Pro corner Christian Gonzalez , who is in the midst of a contract dispute with the team, raising questions about his availability for the opener.
We're heading Down Under for the second game of the 2026 season, as the Niners and Rams will duke it out from Melbourne. What's fascinating about this matchup (beyond it being a key NFC West head-to-head) is how both clubs are dealing with international travel. San Francisco has already flown down to Australia, giving itself a week to best acclimate to the 17-hour time difference. As for L.A., they'll be in Australia for just over 24 hours, opting to arrive the day before the game . This aligns with how the Rams have handled international travel in the past, and it seems to have worked quite well for them. Under McVay, Los Angeles is a perfect 3-0 (SU and ATS) in international games, while outscoring their opponents 92-17.
Jacksonville was one of the best teams to back in 2025, owning a 12-6 ATS record (regular season and postseason). That included an NFL-best 7-2 ATS record at home, where they boasted a 13.7-point average margin of victory. Meanwhile, the Browns -- who will start Deshaun Watson after the veteran beat out Shedeur Sanders this summer for the Week 1 job -- are looking to improve a dreadful road record in 2025. Last year, they were 2-6 (SU and ATS) on the road and lost by an average of 12.5 points.
The Colts enter 2025 with Daniel Jones back under center as he looks to return to his first-half form from last year before going down with a torn Achilles. Even after their free fall down the stretch, Indy was still 8-7-2 ATS last year. The offense will look a bit different, however, with Michael Pittman Jr. traded to Pittsburgh this offseason, meaning Jones will need to lean on the likes of Alec Pierce , Josh Downs , and Keenan Allen in the passing game at receiver. As for the Ravens, they are beginning the Jessie Minter era after the former Chargers defensive coordinator was hired as head coach this offseason. Minter will look to get Baltimore's defense back into shape. If he does, they'll certainly improve upon the 6-11 ATS record from 2025, which was tied for the second-lowest in the NFL.
Both of these teams made the playoffs a season ago but are looking to take another step towards contention. They were roughly in the same tier in terms of the gambling sphere in 2025, with the Texans going 10-9 ATS (including playoffs) and the Bills going 9-10 ATS. This will be an opportunity for new Buffalo head coach Joe Brady to flex his offensive prowess against a top-flight Texans defense, and for the Josh Allen- D.J. Moore connection to take shape. Meanwhile, all eyes will be on C.J. Stroud as the Texans' QB looks to rebound from a disastrous playoff run. Last year, the Texans were 5-4 ATS at home, while the Bills were 5-5 ATS on the road.
Who doesn't love a little revenge narrative? Robert Saleh will begin his head coaching tenure with the Titans when he hosts his former Jets squad in the opener. Neither Tennessee nor New York is expected to make much of a splash this season, so this is an opportunity for Saleh to start on a strong note, and he will do so as a slim 1.5-point favorite. Under the previous regime, Tennessee was 4-5 ATS at home in 2025. Meanwhile, the Jets still have Aaron Glenn pulling the strings as head coach, but they do have a new quarterback in Geno Smith . With Smith under center, New York will try to improve on the 3-4-1 ATS road record from last season.
Both of these NFC squads are coming off a 2025 season that saw them each reach the playoffs, but it'll be an uphill climb for them to get back there in 2026. Each faces a difficult schedule, but Chicago may be better equipped to handle it and come into this matchup as a 2.5-point road favorite. In their lone game as a road favorite in 2025, the Bears covered. As for the Panthers, this is a position they are quite comfortable being in. Last year, Carolina was an underdog at home eight times. They covered six of those games and won five of them outright.
At long last, the Falcons have named their starting quarterback . In Week 1, it'll be Tua Tagovailoa, who gets the nod from head coach Kevin Stefanski, but it comes after a less-than-inspiring showing this summer. Given that it seemed like Tagovailoa was earmarked for the job over Michael Penix Jr., the line appears to have baked in this result as it continues to sit at Steelers -3.5. In 2025, Atlanta was 4-4 ATS on the road. Looking at the Steelers, they are beginning the Mike McCarthy era after he was hired as the head coach this offseason. Of course, McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers have a long history together from their days in Green Bay, so this should be pretty seamless for the duo. McCarthy will try to get the Steelers playing better ball in Pittsburgh, where they were 5-4 ATS in 2025.
If you're looking for a shootout, this might be your best bet, with this matchup between Tampa Bay and Cincinnati having the highest total on the board in Week 1. Before jumping in on the Over, however, it'd be wise to monitor the status of Bucs wideout Emeka Egbuka . The second-year receiver -- who is expected to take over as the No. 1 option following Mike Evans ' departure in free agency -- has been battling a toe injury that has had him sidelined for portions of the summer. If he can't go, that'd drastically cap Tampa Bay's offense. Last season, the Buccaneers were 4-5 ATS on the road, while Cincinnati was 4-5 ATS at home, so something will need to give…

title: 2026 NFL predictions: Final record for all 32 teams, Super Bowl LXI pick, playoff matchups and MVP winner
summary: We just went through and predicted the entire 2026 NFL season
full_text:
Welcome to football's greatest Labor Day tradition: The release of my annual NFL predictions.
After spending the past three days locked in a windowless room trying to figure out who's going to win the Super Bowl this year, I am ready to share my predictions with the world. Will you hate them? Probably. Will you hate me? Maybe.
If I've noticed one thing over the years, it's that people love to throw the wrong predictions back in my face at the end of the year, but that won't be an issue this year, because I don't plan on getting anything wrong.
That being said, if I do end up getting some (or all) of my predictions wrong, feel free to rub it in my face on social media (You can send hate messages to me on X , and I also started a TikTok because my Gen Z nephews told me that no one uses X anymore, so feel free to make fun of me there).
Anyway, before we get to my predictions, let me explain how things will work here: I'll go through each division and predict each team's final record. After that, I'll be making one bold prediction for each division.
Once you roll through the divisional portion of these predictions, you'll see my playoff picks and eventually the team I'm picking to win the Super Bowl. In two of the past 10 years, my preseason Super Bowl pick has ended up winning it all, so if you want to skip everything and scroll straight down to my Super Bowl pick to see if I'm taking your team, I won't be offended.
Finally, if you're wondering how I did last season , I predicted the exact record for 13 different teams or came within one game of it. According to the guys at Stadium Rant , I had the second-most accurate preseason predictions among the media members they tracked. Does that mean I was good, or does it mean that I was just less worse than everyone else? I'm still trying to figure that out.
Even though my predictions were pretty solid for most teams, there was one team that I absolutely whiffed on last year, and that was the Seahawks . I had them missing the playoffs, and if you watched any football in 2025, then you already know that the Seahawks did NOT miss the playoffs.
The largest and most technologically advanced Super Bowl ring ever created for the SBLX Champions. pic.twitter.com/2M2ANGEBgT
That ring is worth more than my car, and the irony is that I could have bought a new car if I had picked the Seahawks to win the Super Bowl last year and made a big bet on it. I definitely will not be underestimating the Seahawks this year. Does that mean I'll be picking them to pull off a Super Bowl repeat?
Let's get to the 2026 predictions and find out.
1. *Bills: 11-6 2. Patriots : 9-8 3. Jets : 6-11 4. Dolphins : 2-15
AFC East bold prediction: Patriots miss the playoffs
Before I explain myself here, I would like to start by saying that my AFC East bold prediction for 2025 was that the Patriots would win double-digit games and that Mike Vrabel would win Coach of the Year. Well, check and check. I also predicted that the Patriots would win the AFC title game by exactly three points over Denver and that they'd lose by two touchdowns to the Seahawks in the Super Bowl.
OK, now that we've established that I'm never wrong about the Patriots, we can get to this year and why I think they'll miss the playoffs. On defense, I'm worried about New England's pass-rush. Their sack leader from last year, Harold Landry , is going to miss at least the first four games of the season, and they don't really have any proven stars behind him. On the other side of the ball, I'm concerned about the offensive line. On paper, it's certainly better than it was last year -- and Will Campbell will be fully healthy -- but I'll believe they're better when I actually see it. This group is going to get two stiff tests in the first two weeks (The Seahawks defense in Week 1 and T.J. Watt in Week 2), and if they pass those, I'll probably be regretting this bold prediction by Week 3.
And let's not forget about the schedule. Last year, the Patriots took advantage of one of the easiest schedules in NFL history. This year, they have an absolute gauntlet coming out of the gate. Their first four opponents have a combined strength-of-schedule of .721, the highest SOS any team has faced in the first four weeks in 40 years. To make things worse, the Patriots will have to play three of their first four games on the road. They might start 1-3, and if that happens, I could see things getting ugly from there, but not too ugly, because I do have them finishing over .500.
1. *Ravens: 12-5 2. *Bengals: 11-6 3. *Steelers: 9-8 4. Browns : 5-12
AFC North bold prediction: Bengals second-round pick wins Defensive Rookie of the Year
Two years ago, I correctly predicted that Jared Verse would win defensive rookie of the year , and this year, I'm jumping on the Cashius Howell bandwagon. A front-seven player has won this award in eight of the past 10 years, and Howell will keep that trend going.
The easiest way for a defensive player to win this award is to rack up sacks, and Howell is in the perfect position to do it. With Dexter Lawrence now on the team, you can pretty much bet that every offense the Bengals play this year will be worried about slowing down Lawrence. That likely means Lawrence will regularly see double teams, which should open the door for someone on the defensive line to shine, and I think that someone will be Howell, who was taken with the 41st overall pick back in April.
And let's not forget, Howell is in a very sack-friendly division. He gets to face Aaron Rodgers , who has been sacked more times than any other QB in NFL history. He also gets to face a Browns offense that surrendered 51 sacks last season, which was the seventh-most in the NFL. As a matter of fact, there were only eight teams last year that gave up 49 sacks or more, and the Bengals will get to play four games against those eight teams, so Howell will be in a position to put up some impressive numbers.
1. *Texans: 11-6 2. Jaguars : 8-9 3. Colts : 7-10 4. Titans : 3-14
AFC South bold prediction: Trevor Lawrence leads the NFL in interceptions
The Jaguars won the AFC South last year, and they did that despite the fact that Lawrence threw 12 interceptions, which was tied for the fifth-most in the NFL. Lawrence's biggest struggles came early in the season with three interceptions in his first four games. The early season could be another struggle for Lawrence this year, and that's because the Jags will be facing two of the best defenses in the NFL in the first two weeks: The Browns (Week 1) and Broncos (Week 2). There were only three teams in the NFL that recorded more than 50 sacks last season, and those were two of them. Basically, Lawrence is likely going to be under a lot of pressure, which could lead to three or four interceptions in the first two weeks. And things won't be getting any easier after that.
Here's what the Jags schedule looks like from Week 2 through their Week 7 bye:
Week 2: at Broncos Week 3: Patriots Week 4: at Bengals Week 5: vs. Eagles (in London) Week 6: vs. Texans (in London)
That's brutal. Lawrence threw at least one interception in nine of Jacksonville's 17 games last season, and he did that even though he had Travis Etienne in his backfield, a player who was so good that he took a lot of pressure off the passing game. The Jags won't have Etienne this year, and although they do have two solid running backs in Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez, I don't think they'll be quite as good as Etienne. With the running game taking a step back, I think Lawrence will be asked to do more, which will lead to more interceptions.

title: Roger Goodell extended as NFL commissioner for four more years, through 2030 season
summary: Goodell is now under contract through what will be his 24th season as the league's commissioner
full_text:
The NFL's compensation committee approved a four-year contract extension for Roger Goodell, keeping him as the league's commissioner through the 2030 season. His new deal lines up with the NFL's current collective bargaining agreement. Goodell is now in line to work as the league's commissioner through the age of 71 years old.
New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft, the chair of the NFL's compensation committee, sent out the following statement to announce the new deal, via ESPN . The other NFL owners on the compensation committee are John Mara of the New York Giants , Shad Khan of the Jacksonville Jaguars , Jimmy Haslam of the Cleveland Browns , Michael Bidwill of the Arizona Cardinals and Greg Penner of the Denver Broncos .
"As members of the Compensation Committee, we're pleased to announce that we have reached agreement with Roger to remain as Commissioner through the 2030 League Season, ending on March 31, 2031. Throughout the negotiation process, the Committee worked closely with an independent third-party compensation consultant and outside counsel to structure a deal that aligns Roger's compensation with the League's long-term interests and success. To that end, the agreement is heavily performance based, with more than 95% of the total compensation tied to Roger's and the NFL's performance measured against various metrics and at the discretion of the Compensation Committee. "We believe we are very fortunate to have Roger at the helm for the next four years. If any of you has any questions, please reach out to any of us. Robert Kraft (Chairman) John Mara Shad Khan Jimmy Haslam Michael Bidwill Greg Penner."
This deal positions Goodell to be front and center for the NFL's next round of CBA negotiations with the NFL Players Association. The league's current media rights deals, which are worth just over $110 billion, are set to run through the 2032 season.
