title: 49ers player gets cut after flying 16 hours to Australia: Why he might be sent home and why they made the move
summary: San Francisco made room for long snapper Jon Weeks ahead of the opener in Melbourne, a move that could signal George Kittle is ready to return from an Achilles tear.
full_text:
The only thing worse than getting cut by an NFL team is getting cut after flying 16 hours to Australia, and that's exactly what happened to 49ers tight end Brayden Willis on Saturday.
Willis was released to make room for long snapper Jon Weeks , who was promoted to the active roster from the practice squad.
Weeks is the only long snapper on the team, but he wasn't on the active roster going into the weekend because the 49ers had to do some roster gymnastics before the cut deadline on Aug. 30. He ended up being released just before the deadline, which left the 49ers with exactly zero long snappers on their roster. Weeks was eventually added to the practice squad, and now, he's back on the active roster as the 49ers get ready to prepare for their opener against the Rams in Melbourne.
Although Weeks is the one being added to the roster, let's not forget about Willis, who might have to fly 16 hours home just days after landing in Australia. Willis has been in the NFL since 2023, when the 49ers made him a seventh-round pick, and with less than four years of NFL experience, he's now going to hit the waiver wire. If he gets claimed by another team, he'll immediately leave Australia to join his new team.
Of course, this might be the one situation where a player is hoping NOT to be claimed by anyone. As several 49ers beat writers noted on Saturday , if Weeks goes unclaimed, then he'll likely sign with San Francisco's practice squad, and if that happens, then he'll be able to stay in Australia with the 49ers
SUNDAY NIGHT UPDATE (9/6/26): Willis signed with the 49ers practice squad after going unclaimed on waivers, so he gets to STAY in Australia.
From a roster standpoint, the 49ers' decision to cut Willis is definitely an interesting one. Since Willis is a tight end, the move could signal that the team is extremely confident in George Kittle's chances of playing on Thursday night -- Friday morning in Melbourne -- against the Rams.
Kittle, who tore his Achilles tendon in January , made the trip to Australia, and it's increasingly looking like he'll be able to play.
That being said, now that Willis is on the practice squad, the 49ers could still promote him to the active roster on game day if they feel like Kittle isn't quite ready, so it will certainly be interesting to see how Kittle is listed when the 49ers release their first injury report of the year on Monday.
The 49ers also made one other roster move this week, and that was the signing of Khalid Kareem away from the Falcons ' practice squad. The move means Kareem will have to make the roughly 21-hour trip from Atlanta to Melbourne to join the 49ers for the start of practice this week.
As you can see, there are many logistical issues with playing in Australia. If you cut a player, there's a chance they might have to turn around and fly home immediately (if a player is released or waived while on an international trip, the franchise remains fully responsible for their return transportation, logistics, and getting them back to the United States), and if you sign a player, that person has to quickly figure out how to travel halfway around the world in a very short time.

title: 3 reasons to be excited, 3 reasons to be concerned about the Cardinals
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are in countdown mode. Think about Mike LaFleur, who has been hired to become the head coach of an NFL team. That has to be exciting, and super anxious at the same time. The preparation, the work, the roster decisions, and all the ideas that came from Moment 1 to the opening […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 12: Trey McBride #85, Michael Wilson #14 and James Conner #6 of the Arizona Cardinals celebrate after a play during the second half in the game against the Atlanta Falcons at State Farm Stadium on November 12, 2023 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Mike Christy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals are in countdown mode. Think about Mike LaFleur, who has been hired to become the head coach of an NFL team. That has to be exciting, and super anxious at the same time. The preparation, the work, the roster decisions, and all the ideas that came from Moment 1 to the opening kickoff against the Los Angeles Chargers. RELATED: CARDINALS OFFENSIVE WEAPONS RANKED #6 And now, the excitement of the season. Everything is new. Every team in the NFL has the same record at 0-0-0 with the same goals: division crown, playoff bid, conference championship game appearance, and play in the Super Bowl. For Cardinals fans, there is hope, but also the realization that this team broke a 127-year franchise record for the most losses in a single season with 14. That doesn’t simply cure itself overnight. It is easy to be excited about the new year, the new schedule, new players, and yes, a new coaching staff. But this franchise has been down so many times and kicked off the year with high hopes, only to realize that the new boss is just like the old boss. Here is what we, as Arizona fans, can be excited about and also concerned about. Excited: Offensive weapons are everywhere As training camp approached, ESPN ran an article and rated the best offenses for the upcoming season. The Cardinals were ranked #6. We agree. Every NFL team that has a high-powered offensive group has either a stud at quarterback, a receiver that is uncoverable, or a stallion in the backfield. With Arizona, however, it is their tight end, Trey McBride. What a sensational guy this is, and he is just getting started. He had the most targets on the team last year (169), most receptions (126), most first-down conversions (63), most yards (1,239), and the most touchdowns (11). Those numbers could explode this year with this new offense, which has multiple tight ends on the field for most every offensive play. Backup TE Elijah Higgins will get more targets than you think. Michael Wilson has assumed the WR1 position. The key element of this offense is whether Marv Harrison can rebound and finally become that “generational” player he was advertised to become. And what about RB Jeremiyah Love, the #3 overall pick in the draft? These two are going to be the reasons why Arizona can win games or get bogged down. The receiver depth is very deep this year with Kendrick Bourne, Simi Fehoko, Jalen Brooks, and the rookie Reggie Virgil. With a veteran at quarterback in Jacoby Brissett and capable backups, the weapons that this offense has accumulated are going to surprise a lot of folks. Concerned: The offensive line The Wild Card to this offense? Without a shadow of a doubt: The offensive line. GM Monti Ossenfort did his best to fix this mess with multiple signings for starters and also quality depth. The big question seems to be whether his big splash during free agency, OG Isaac Semualo, can create stability and whether Isaiah Adams is really ready to take on the starting role at the other guard spot. These two men are critical to the offense’s success in running the ball, which is a significant portion of the offense. Not much has been mentioned about Elijah Wilkinson as the new right tackle, so that’s good news. The coaching staff believes he is doing what he is supposed to be doing, although in the past few years he has been known to collect laundry. Hopefully he doesn’t attract many penalties going forward. And center Hjalte Froholdt and LT Paris Johnson. Anyone worried about either one? This group has the potential of being really solid, or could fall apart if they don’t come out as one cohesive unit right out of the gate. The backups are a good group as well, with Jon Gaines and Josh Fryar leading the room. Excited: Up the gut run defense Getting Roy Lopez back with the defense is such a blessing. He has good gap responsibility and is stiff against the run. Now, can Walter Nolen remain healthy? Seemed like each week in training camp he was walking off the turf with some ailment. He is such a force when healthy. Great physical traits with good explosiveness. He is certainly a playmaker, but he has to stay on the field for Arizona. And Andrew Billings has been a big surprise this preseason. Seems like every year his body keeps getting bigger, but since he is a rotational player, his limited snaps shouldn’t be an issue. For some reason, he seems a bit quicker than last year when he was with the Chicago Bears. L.J. Collier has had his moments, but is a good run stopper and gives this defense inside-out flexibility. Concerned: Pass rush opposite Josh Sweat Ossenfort couldn’t fix every hole on this roster. Getting another pass rusher to bookend EDGE rusher Josh Sweat would have been ideal. The GM passed on several young pass-rushing studs early in the draft in order to take Love, which would have made this year’s defense one of the best pass-rushing teams in the division at least. Right now, that responsibility is resting on the shoulders of Darius Robinson and Zaven Collins. Both players were drafted high, and the one thing this defense is not getting from either is another high: production. Collins had just 1.5 sacks last year with 40 tackles and 10 QB hits. That does not scream “elite-level pass rusher.” Robinson has had two sacks total since signing his rookie deal. Most Cardinals fans were expecting him to be released after training camp, and yet, here we are in total mediocrity. And it’s not like Ossenfort can just reach out and sign a free agent for assistance. That list has been picked over to the bone. Excited: Elite defensive backfield One thing Ossenfort loves is cornerbacks and safeties. He is a former college quarterback and knows that competent guys in the back are critical. So, it’s his pet project. He didn’t draft S Budda Baker, but he realizes just how special this dude is. NFL All-Rookie Team, eight Pro Bowls, Art Rooney Award winner, two-time Second Team All-Pro, and two-time First Team All-Pro. All of that in just nine seasons. Six seasons with 100+ tackles, including 164 in 2024. In 2019, he made the most solo tackles in the league with 104. So, what does Ossenfort do? He takes care of Baker. He continues to nurture him and make him feel needed and happy. As Cardinals fans, thank you for doing this Mr. O. Then there is the cornerback room. Will Johnson is a league star waiting to explode. And his creative cast is doing a great job with Garrett Williams, Max Melton, and Denzel Burke, who showed last year he can ball out. Now, all of this is with an asterisk. Can each of these young men remain healthy? The collapse of the pass coverage last year due to multiple players getting hurt killed this defense. The lone backup is Kei’Trel Crawford. Ossenfort was able to nab a veteran safety that hardly anyone is talking about, and that is Andrew Wingard. He is as solid as he can be, and will hit his grandma if she catches a ball in his zone. The backups all show promise, with Dadrion Taylor-Demerson (who could actually start right now) and the new guy, Wydett Williams. This entire group will decide the season. The NFC West has exceptional receivers, pass-catching tight ends, and veteran quarterbacks who know how to find tight windows. Concerned: The friggin’ schedule Aren’t the fourth-place division teams from last year supposed to play each other and have the easiest schedules the next year? What happened to that plan? Because the Cardinals currently own the league’s fourth-most difficult schedule. Isn’t there somebody we can sue for misrepresentation? And about playing all the worst teams from the season before? From that list of last-place division finishers, Arizona…

summary: This past week, the Arizona Cardinals coaching staff had several difficult decisions to make in regards to the final 53-man roster. Then, scouring the waiver wire, followed by crafting this year’s practice squad. The new head coach, Mike LaFleur, had his own agenda as far as players he was looking for. RELATED: WHICH PRACTICE SQUAD […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - AUGUST 28: Kedon Slovis #12 of the Arizona Cardinals drops back during a preseason game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on August 28, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images This past week, the Arizona Cardinals coaching staff had several difficult decisions to make in regards to the final 53-man roster. Then, scouring the waiver wire, followed by crafting this year’s practice squad. The new head coach, Mike LaFleur, had his own agenda as far as players he was looking for. RELATED: WHICH PRACTICE SQUAD PLAYER HAS THE HIGHEST UPSIDE There were a few surprises among the final roster and a few expected cuts among the almost 40 guys who have since left the desert. Where did the athletes released end up? QB Kedon Slovis – Green Bay Packers Slovis had a pretty good camp and subsequent preseason. The issue is that most NFL clubs only keep three quarterbacks, and he was the odd man out. And once rookie Carson Beck balled out in the Hall of Fame Game, Slovis’ days were numbered. When Packers head coach Matt LaFleur saw Slovis in action during their joint practices, he was impressed and added the young signalcaller to their practice squad. Slovis may have an opportunity to be brought up to the main roster because the franchise only kept two quarterbacks: Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor. The good news for the Cardinals coaching staff is that if any of the three QBs they retained become injured, they are able to claim Slovis at any time as long as he remains on Green Bay’s practice squad. LB Owen Pappoe – Tennessee Titans Pappoe was impressive in training camp and had a few excellent games during the exhibition phase. He had four tackles with two batted passes against the Packers, led the team in tackles against the Cowboys with 10, three in the Raiders contest, and a single tackle in the Hall of Fame Game. The Cardinals had a logjam at linebacker, plus the rookie Karson Sharar and journeyman Eku Leona outplayed Pappoe. He is the only former Cardinal who ended up on the main roster of another club. CB Sean Murphy-Bunting – Tampa Bay Buccaneers This was a guy who restructured his deal to stay in Tempe, then was released. He didn’t impress in camp or in preseason games against the opponent’s second-string offense, so he ended up on the unemployment line. The Bucs signed him to their practice squad. The Cardinals had spent a valuable second-round draft pick back in 2019. He was productive early in his career with three picks his rookie year and 70 tackles in Year 2. But they cut bait with him after his rookie contract expired, and he hasn’t been the same player since he re-signed in 2024. He did not play at all last year, which hurt his status for this season unless he balled out during camp. Plus, CB Garrett Williams’ return gave the defensive backfield plenty of talent as it was. Practice squad OT Valentin Senn is Arizona’s international designation on the practice squad and was in the Cardinals’ camp this year. He was born and raised in Austria. Of the 17 players listed on the initial practice squad, 13 were in the Cardinals’ camp this year. The only ones who were in another camp were: TE Jared Harrison-Hunte (Panthers) OG Vershon Lee (Vikings) CB D’Shawn Jamison (Steelers) TE Shawn Bowman (Jaguars)

title: Tua Tagovailoa named Falcons’ starting QB for Week 1 vs. Steelers
summary: The biggest question facing the 2026 Atlanta Falcons has been answered. On Monday, the Falcons announced that Tua Tagovailoa, who signed with the Falcons this offseason after being released by the Miami Dolphins, has been named the starter for Week 1 against the Steelers in Pittsburgh. The Falcons’ quarterback situation has been a roller-coaster ride […]
full_text: Aug 28, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Atlanta Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa (1) reacts as he exits the field after the game against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The biggest question facing the 2026 Atlanta Falcons has been answered. On Monday, the Falcons announced that Tua Tagovailoa, who signed with the Falcons this offseason after being released by the Miami Dolphins, has been named the starter for Week 1 against the Steelers in Pittsburgh . The Falcons’ quarterback situation has been a roller-coaster ride since the first day of training camp — and not a particularly fun one. On Day 1 of camp, the team announced that Trevor Siemian had been released with an injury settlement; Tua Tagovailoa would not be participating in practice due to some lower back stiffness; and the team was signing QB Cooper Rush. Michael Penix Jr. wasn’t medically cleared until the final week of training camp, so that left Rush and rookie undrafted free agent Jack Strand to participate in that first practice. Stefanski declined to name a starter throughout the preseason, even though Penix’s medical clearance came so late in the process that he was unable to take any preseason game snaps. And Tua’s preseason performance didn’t necessarily enthuse fans. He completed 3 of 5 attempts for 22 yards, zero touchdowns, and zero picks in Week 1 of the preseason against the Broncos, sat out Week 2 (this was always Stefanski’s plan, to let the starters take most of the joint practice reps with the Colts and sit out that preseason game), and went 7 of 8 for 95 yards, no touchdowns, no picks, and one absurd botched snap that turned into a fumble and kind of overshadowed the rest of his performance. But I have concerns about whether or not Michael Penix is ready, after basically three days of full practice, to play an entire NFL game. I do believe, based on what Penix has said about it, he’s past the mental aspect of his recovery, and I trust that he’s physically healthy. I worry that his lack of contact leading up to Week 1 could lead to a different injury altogether, or that the lack of contact and full-speed practice or preseason action has him unprepared for the speed of the regular-game. And that’s not to suggest there aren’t injury concerns with Tua. His concussion history worries me — not because of football, but for the sake of his long-term health and well being. But he has gotten most of the meaningful work this preseason with the starters, he has participated fully in padded practices, joint practices, and the preseason, and it stands to reason that he is more prepared — through no fault of Penix’s, just because of the timing of his medical clearance — to be the Week 1 starter. Tua spent the first six seasons of his career with the Miami Dolphins, who drafted him with the fifth overall pick out of Alabama in the 2020 NFL Draft. He has a 68% completion percentage over his NFL career, throwing 120 touchdowns against 59 interceptions. He was released by the Dolphins in March 2026 after a 2025 season he finished with 2,660 yards, 20 touchdowns, 15 picks, and took 30 sacks. He was benched for the final three games of the season, and the Falcons took advantage of him being cut to sign him for an extremely affordable one-year deal. New head coach Kevin Stefanski and general manager Ian Cunningham saw him as competition and insurance for Penix, and now he is the starter. I don’t think this decision says anything about either Tua’s or Penix’s long-term future with the Falcons or as the starter. There’s a lot of football to be played before I’ll have an opinion about that. But I do think it’s Tua’s job to lose. If he goes out there and balls out, it would be silly to sit him. If he doesn’t, though, it likely won’t be long before Penix is ready to step in. Can the 2026 version of Tua Tagovailoa do that, and stay healthy? That’s now one of the biggest questions facing the 2026 Falcons now.

summary: Several new players make up the Falcons’ interior tackle rotation this season. They have gotten younger by trading for Gervon Dexter Sr. and Maason Smith. These look like well-calculated moves by Ian Cunningham […]
full_text: Several new players make up the Falcons’ interior tackle rotation this season. After struggling to stop the run last season, the team is optimistic that a personnel overhaul will help address a major flaw. They have gotten younger by trading for Gervon Dexter Sr. and Maason Smith. These look like well-calculated moves by Ian Cunningham to bolster a group that needs to carry the load early in the season. They will join Brandon Dorlus, who finished second on the team in sacks with 8.5. Dorlus may occasionally shift to the edge, but the coaching staff knows how prolific he can be as an interior pass rusher. That is why fans firmly believe he will play the most snaps out of all the defensive tackles. The question is who plays more between Dexter Sr. and Smith. The answer proved to be more definitive than expected. Despite falling out of favor in Chicago, Dexter Sr. is expected to take on a major role after recently joining the Falcons. His intriguing pass-rushing skills feature a quick first step and impressive bend to beat opposing guards. Combining his attributes with Dorlus could provide Jeff Ulbrich’s defense with the punch inside that compensates for the lack of viable edge-rushing options. title: Ravens discussion: who is flying under the radar heading into Week 1?
summary: This offseason, the Baltimore Ravens rebuilt the interior of their offensive line and retooled their pass rush – and turned over virtually their entire coaching staff. Over the past few months, those coaches have installed an entirely new offensive scheme while drilling down on the details on defense. Young playmakers like Ja’Kobi Lane and Mike Green […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 23: Travis Jones #98 of the Baltimore Ravens reacts as he takes the field prior to an NFL football game against the New York Jets at M&T Bank Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images This offseason, the Baltimore Ravens rebuilt the interior of their offensive line and retooled their pass rush – and turned over virtually their entire coaching staff. Over the past few months, those coaches have installed an entirely new offensive scheme while drilling down on the details on defense. Young playmakers like Ja’Kobi Lane and Mike Green turned heads in training camp, while undrafted gems Joe Fagnano and Ethan Burke impressed enough in the preseason to enter the roster spot. But with Week 1 right around the corner, it’s time to look away from the headlines and the highlights and talk about some Ravens who are flying under the radar heading into the regular season. Nikhil’s take: Over the course of the preseason, every player gets talked about at some point. But discussions regarding Baltimore’s backfield focused on future Hall of Famer Derrick Henry, owner Steve Bisciotti’s personal draft pick Adam Randall, and on-the-bubble youngster Rasheen Ali. Lost in the conversation was veteran Justice Hill, who has been an afterthought this year after missing the second half of the 2025 season with a neck injury. But Hill has quietly averaged 4.8 yards per carry and 8.3 yards per reception since 2023 and is poised to continue serving as the Ravens’ third-down back this year. Henry will no doubt get the lion’s share of the work on the ground, but offensive coordinator Declan Doyle will likely give Hill opportunities on screens and isolation routes against linebackers. If the 28-year-old can remain efficient with his touches, protect Jackson in the pocket, and make plays when his number is called, he will be a key cog in the 2026 offense. On the other side of the ball, defensive tackle Travis Jones is simply not getting enough love. He was the Ravens’ second-best defender last year behind Kyle Hamilton and singlehandedly held the defensive line together whenever he was on the field. But with the arrival of Trey Hendrickson and the return of Nnamdi Madubuike, Baltimore’s more athletic, stat-stuffing edge rushers have been the main talking points. But Jones stands to benefit from the focus on his new teammates. If opposing offenses are more worried about the bigger names, they might leave Jones in 1-on-1 situations more often and hope their blocker can lose slowly before being overwhelmed. But the 26-year-old refined his pass rush repertoire after a few years in the league and should be able to collapse pockets consistently. Having Calais Campbell and Broderick Washington back in the fold will also ease Jones’ workload, which skyrocketed to a 70% defensive snap share and 889 total snaps last year. Now, it’s your turn! title: Ravens news: DT Nnamdi Madubuike could be ready for Week 1
summary: Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of all the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens. In this week’s edition, we cover Nnamdi Madubuike’s return to full-team work in practice, landing spots for recent ex-Ravens, and media projections for the 2026 season. Let’s dive in! Nnamdi Madubuike nears return The Ravens were […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 7: Nnamdi Madubuike #92 of the Baltimore Ravens runs around the edge during an NFL football game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on September 07, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of all the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens. In this week’s edition, we cover Nnamdi Madubuike’s return to full-team work in practice, landing spots for recent ex-Ravens, and media projections for the 2026 season. Let’s dive in! Nnamdi Madubuike nears return The Ravens were extremely cautious with Nnamdi Madubuike’s ramp-up in training camp, holding him out of 11-on-11 work for the entire preseason. He did not even make contact with a sled until the week before the team’s last preseason game. But last week, the two-time Pro Bowler returned to full-team drills, a huge leap of progress that brings him one step closer to playing in a game. Ian Rapoport (Good Morning Football, NFL Network) I think it’s fair to say there was some doubt, especially heading into the offseason, on if he would play football again. Needed a procedure, needed it to go well, needed a lot of things to happen for him to be back on the field. And there he is, not only back on the field but doing individual drills and other such things for most of training camp. Now is in 11-on-11, a significant step, making you believe that Madubuike will be on the field when the season starts in Week 1 or shortly thereafter. It is impossible to overstate Madubuike’s potential impact on Baltimore’s defense. The defensive line virtually collapsed after he went down in 2025. His return, along with the addition of Trey Hendrickson, could vault the Ravens pass rush from the bottom of the league last year to the top this season. But his ability to stuff the run could be just as important in Jesse Minter’s new defense. 2026 NFL season X factors: Key players for all 32 teams – Ben Solak (ESPN) In 2023, Madubuike had 13 sacks at defensive tackle. Preposterous stuff. A comprehensive list of defensive tackles who had at least 13 sacks in a season over the past decade: Aaron Donald (twice) and Chris Jones (twice). That’s it… …Defensive tackle comes into even greater focus when you consider how often new head coach Jesse Minter runs light boxes (fifth-highest light-box rate in football last season). Strong defensive tackle play is a must for teams trying to fit the run from two-high shells, and next to Travis Jones, Madubuike can stuff early-down runs and get the defense to passing downs. There, a deeper bench of rushers can take some of the pressure off him. Former Ravens make career moves Linebacker Kyle Van Noy signs with Vikings on practice squad (ESPN) Van Noy, 35, played the past three seasons with the Baltimore Ravens. He followed up a career year in 2024 with one of his most disappointing seasons last year, struggling to generate consistent pressure. He finished his last campaign with just two sacks, ending a run of six straight seasons with at least five. But with the Vikings, he should provide some needed depth and experience at the edge rusher position, where Andrew Van Ginkel and Dallas Turner give Minnesota a dynamic set of starters, but the rest of the depth chart is largely unproven. Giants To Sign LB Malik Harrison – Adam La Rose (Pro Football Rumors) This deal will allow for a reunion between Harrison and head coach John Harbaugh after the two worked together in Baltimore from 2020-24. During that time, Harrison primarily contributed on special teams but he also logged 372 defensive snaps on defense during his final Ravens campaign. Upon arrival in Pittsburgh, the former third-rounder saw a career-high 40% defensive snap share while playing 11 games. Additionally, former Ravens tight end Qadir Ismail signed with the Bears’ practice squad. Evan Beerntsen, the team’s final draft pick this year (Round 7, No. 253 overall) worked out for the Raiders and the Seahawks, and kicker Justin Tucker had a tryout with the Jets. Media projections for the Ravens’ 2026 season AFC North Preview: Should You Believe in the Bengals? – Sheil Kapadia (The Ringer) The Super Bowl case here is straightforward: Jackson is healthy and thrives in the new offensive system. The offensive line overachieves. A young pass catcher like rookie Ja’Kobi Lane emerges as a quality second option. And Minter coaches the defense to a top-five level. I see a very good team, but the issues above give me pause. I see a team that can win in different ways. But I’m not sure I see an elite unit. I could get there with the offense if I trusted the offensive line or the pass catchers more. I could get there with the defense if I were confident in the pass rush. I like the Ravens as a wild-card team with a Super Bowl ceiling. But ultimately, I think that they probably need one more offseason to build up the roster. Projected record: 11-6 NFL team previews 2026: Predictions, rankings, depth charts – ESPN Best-case scenario for 2026, per FPI: 13-4 Worst-case scenario for 2026, per FPI: 8-9 This season is a success if … the Ravens advance to at least the AFC Championship Game. Baltimore fired coach John Harbaugh because of a lack of deep playoff runs. The Ravens need to avoid quick exits under Jesse Minter. — [Jamison] Hensley One key fantasy nugget: With Jackson’s electric dual-threat ability and a play-action-heavy system under new coordinator Declan Doyle, the Ravens quarterback is primed to produce big numbers. Jackson completed a league-best 80% of his play-action throws last season. — [Matt] Bowen Bold prediction for 2026: The Ravens’ defense will rank in the top four in EPA per play. That’s a pretty big jump from last season, when it finished 16th. But in Minter’s first season with the Chargers, he took a defense that ranked 29th and brought it to seventh best. And Minter probably has more talent to work with in Baltimore. — [Seth] Walder Who Will Have the NFL’s Best Offense in 2026? – Anthony Dabbundo (The Ringer) 7. Baltimore Ravens You used to be able to ink Baltimore into the top five of any preseason offensive rankings, but the Ravens are entering this season with more questions than usual. They scored 40 points in a thrilling Week 1 loss to Buffalo last year, but for the rest of the season, Baltimore ranked only 13th in EPA per drive. Quarterback Lamar Jackson missed four games with a hamstring injury and never looked as explosive as a runner after returning. His 2025 pressure-to-sack rate was the highest of his career and one of the highest in the entire league. Will a healthier Jackson resemble his pre-2025 self? Or was last season’s decline in his rushing efficiency the beginning of an age-related trend? That question will become increasingly prevalent this season and beyond. Jackson’s mobility has always helped Baltimore’s line perform better than the sum of its parts, but having a less explosive version of him would place more pressure on the offensive line in protection and on Jackson to operate the traditional passing game. The uncertainty does not end there. The Ravens have to replace longtime center Tyler Linderbaum, who departed for Las Vegas, while Declan Doyle takes over for Todd Monken as offensive coordinator. This will be Doyle’s first time calling plays after spending last year working as OC under Ben Johnson in Chicago—so this will also be the first test of Johnson’s coaching tentacles. The Ravens still have a solid rushing infrastructure with Derrick Henry and one of the league’s most uniquely talented quarterbacks. But for the first time in years, ranking Baltimore among the NFL’s elite offenses requires projecting a rebound rather than relying on recent evidence. Join the conversation! title: Buffalo Bills 2026 scouting report: defensive lineman Greg Gaines
summary: With a switch to an odd-man front on defense, the Buffalo Bills have been changing their defensive personnel throughout this offseason. In some ways, the team has had to be creative, asking players drafted for former head coach Sean McDermott’s four-man defensive line to change their roles and body types in preparation for a season […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 15: Greg Gaines #96 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers celebrate during an NFL football game against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on September 15, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images With a switch to an odd-man front on defense, the Buffalo Bills have been changing their defensive personnel throughout this offseason. In some ways, the team has had to be creative, asking players drafted for former head coach Sean McDermott’s four-man defensive line to change their roles and body types in preparation for a season under new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. In some cases, though, the Bills have gone outside of their usual comfort areas to find different player archetypes. One of the more oft-discussed positions in the new defense has been that of the nose tackle. Buffalo didn’t have a traditional nose tackle with McDermott given that they generally had two defensive tackles on the field at once, but players like DaQuan Jones and Star Lotulelei served roles similar to that which a nose tackle would traditionally fill in a three-man front. The Bills have an answer in the middle, but they definitely need depth at that spot. In today’s installment of our “91 players in 91 days” series, we discuss a veteran nose tackle ostensibly signed to provide said depth. _____________________________________________________________________________ Name: Greg Gaines Number: 97 Position: DL Height/Weight: 6’1” 312 lbs. Age: 29 (30 on 5/6/2027) Experience/Draft: 7; selected by the Los Angeles Rams in the fourth round (No. 134 overall) of the 2019 NFL Draft College: Washington Acquired: Signed with Buffalo on 8/18/2026 Financial situation (per Spotrac): Gaines signed a one-year deal at the veteran’s minimum. The total deal is worth $1,487,500, but thanks to the veteran’s salary benefit, his cap hit comes in lower at $1,262,500 for the season. If Gaines is on Buffalo’s Week One roster, his entire base salary ($1.3 million) becomes guaranteed thanks to his status as a fully vested veteran. If he’s released prior to the start of the first game, Buffalo will carry a dead cap charge of $137,500 for the season. 2025 Recap: Gaines once again served as a rotational nose tackle for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last season, appearing on 35% of the team’s defensive snaps across 17 games. Gaines offers little in the way of pass rush, so he mostly plays on early downs and in obvious run situations, acting as a gap-plugger and run-stuffer up front. He totaled 23 tackles, three tackles for loss, and two sacks last season. Positional outlook: Gaines is one of ten defensive linemen listed on the current roster. Ed Oliver, Deone Walker, Landon Jackson, Zane Durant, Phidarian Mathis, Zion Logue, DeWayne Carter, Travis Clayton, and T.J. Sanders are the others. 2026 Offseason: Gaines has been a free agent since his contract with Tampa Bay expired at the start of the new league year. He has participated in practice and preseason action since signing with Buffalo. 2026 Season outlook: While he fills a need as a potential nose tackle, as Skarekrow pointed out in his All-22 analysis after Gaines signed, the veteran can play multiple spots along a three-man line. Tampa Bay frequently used him off center, and while that might have been because they had Vita Vea to plug the middle, it bodes well for Gaines’ chances to come in and contribute along the line in Buffalo. Behind Deone Walker, Buffalo doesn’t have much going at nose tackle. Phidarian Mathis looked like a solid bet to make the team as the backup nose, but a three-game suspension for an alcohol-use issue while he was with the New York Jets means that he will begin the year unavailable. I guess being with the Jets could drive anyone to drink, but I digress. The Bills have also asked third-year man DeWayne Carter to bulk up and play the nose, and while he has done so, he hasn’t exactly separated himself this summer, and after a weak rookie season followed by a lost second year due to a torn Achilles, it’s not wise to assume that he can just come in and play at the level Buffalo needs. Gaines, then, not only has a good shot at making the roster based on his experience alone, but I would go so far as to say he has a strong chance to carve out an important role on defense. Whether he’s spelling Walker or playing alongside him on first down, in goal line situations, or on fourth-and-short, Gaines could easily see 35-45% of the snaps on defense as a run-down specialist. The Bills don’t have a ton of those along their defensive front, and given Leonhard’s stated desire to be significantly better against the run this season, it’s reasonable to assume that someone like Gaines is looked at as an acquisition who can help them in achieving that goal. August signings are often nothing more than camp bodies and tryout players, but with Greg Gaines, the Bills likely found a piece to their defense that they were missing.

title: The Optimist: Taxing depth early as a sign of progress
summary: The Carolina Panthers are entering the 2026 season in a weird place. On the surface, the wheels are falling off before the bus has even left the station. Their two starting offensive tackles, Taylor Moton and Ikem Ekwonu, are on various reserve lists, along with starting defensive tackle Tershawn Wharton, and all are expected to […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 15: Monroe Freeling #57 of the Carolina Panthers waits for the snap against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers are entering the 2026 season in a weird place. On the surface, the wheels are falling off before the bus has even left the station. Their two starting offensive tackles, Taylor Moton and Ikem Ekwonu, are on various reserve lists, along with starting defensive tackle Tershawn Wharton, and all are expected to miss the first four to six weeks. Their favorite play-all-five-spots utility lineman, Brady Christiansen is out for at least another month recovering from an injury suffered last season. Nic Scourton, a projected starting outside linebacker coming off a breakout rookie season, is out for the season. So too is their third round pick, wide receiver and human highlight reel Chris Brazzell II. They were so disappointed with the middle of the defense during the preseason that they found a free agent linebacker who stayed home during the whole offseason in Bobby Okereke and signed him into a starting role. In short, the offensive line never even got assembled before it started falling apart and the defense is shaky and untested at best. So why aren’t we all freaking out? Why are a lot of us looking around the division and thinking “we might be able to repeat”? Simply put, this is the deepest roster the Carolina Panthers have fielded in years. Injuries happen every year to every team. Depth, as often as anything, separates the teams that are ready to compete from the rest. Rasheed Walker and 2026 first round draft pick Monroe Freeling are maybe the most capable backups the Panthers have ever had at the same time. Both look capable of starting for a lot of teams. Here? They are just holding down the fort. Instead of an injury to a third round pick screwing over all of our hopes and dreams for the wide receivers corps, Brazzell’s injury just clarified the training camp battle for the deepest room we’ve seen in a minute. Instead of wondering who was going to step up as a number two receiver behind DJ Moore or Steve Smith, we spent training camp arguing over who would take the fifth and sixth roster spots. There was a large contingent of people, even after Brazzell went down, that thought the team might legitimately keep seven wide receivers. That kind of depth affords the Panthers the opportunity to be pleasantly surprised, instead of dependent upon, any signs of positive development from Xavier Legette. There are still a thousand questions to answer regarding the 2026 regular season. Not least among them is whether or not the team will get off to their near traditional slow start to September. An extra tally in the win column in the next few weeks could make all the difference for the team’s playoff hopes when their competition is the always fluky NFC South. A thousand more questions will arise when the Panthers actually start playing games on Sunday. The one thing we aren’t questioning is the ability of this team to roll with the first round of punches they received. Depth across the entire roster has improved dramatically since Dan Morgan and Dave Canales started working together. Where they go from here is simply the story of the season. That’s a big step up from the foregone conclusion it would have been even three years ago.

title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 6 Days Remaining
summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TN - NOVEMBER 15: Thomas Davis #58 of the Carolina Panthers looks over the offense before the snap during a game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on November 15, 2015 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Wesley Hitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #6. Thomas Davis Sr. Panthers stats: 176 games, 1,098 tackles, 87 tackles for loss, 28 sacks, 13 interceptions Career stats: 199 games, 1,216 tackles, 90 tackles for loss, 29 sacks, 13 interceptions Few players in NFL history, let alone Panthers history, have displayed the combination of excellence and resilience as Thomas Davis Sr. His brilliant 16-year NFL career only came about because of his dogged determination to return from three different ACL tears that would have ended most careers. He’s a living reminder of what it means to overcome the obstacles life throws at you, remain positive and optimistic, then work your rear end off to achieve your goals. Davis joined the Panthers in 2005 as a first round pick (No. 14 overall) after a stellar career at Georgia. The Panthers went 11-5 that year with a roster that featured a plethora of veteran linebackers like Will Witherspoon, Dan Morgan, Brandon Short, and Chris Draft. All four of those guys had at least 50 tackles in Davis’s rookie season, but even then he carved out a rotational role appearing in all 16 games with 40 tackles and 1.5 sacks. In 2006 he locked down a starting gig and in the three seasons between 2006 and 2008 he racked up 291 tackles and eight sacks. His 2009 campaign was off to a great start but then he tore his ACL seven games into the season. Back in 2009 returning from a torn ACL was much more of a dicey proposition than it is today. Davis put in the work to rehab and returned to minicamp in June 2010, just seven months after his initial injury. On the second day of minicamp he re-tore the same ACL in a noncontact drill and ended up missing the entire 2010 season while he rehabbed for a second time. He returned in 2011 and in the second game of the season, he tore the same ACL again. It was the third time that ACL had been torn in 23 months. At the time, no professional athlete had been known to return to their sport after tearing the same ACL three times. But there had also never been an athlete like Thomas Davis. In 2012 Davis managed to return to the Panthers for his age-29 season and miraculously began a streak of five consecutive seasons with at least 100 tackles. He made the Pro Bowl in three consecutive years between 2015 and 2017, and was All-Pro First Team in 2015 when the Panthers went 15-1 and reached the Super Bowl. He remained with the Panthers through 2018, his age-35 season, and was still productive with 79 tackles in 12 games. But by 2019 Carolina was ready for a full-scale rebuild and Davis took his veteran know-how to the Chargers for one season followed by his final campaign with Washington. Thomas Davis’s 1,098 tackles is a Panthers franchise record. The Panthers motto is “Keep Pounding”. That’s exactly what Thomas Davis Sr. did throughout his outstanding 14-year career in Carolina, making him one of the most legendary players in team history.

title: 2026 NFL Season Award Predictions: Offensive Rookie of the Year
summary: Some of the Windy City Gridiron staff made their picks for several 2026 individual season awards, and we’ll cap the predictions off by picking Super Bowl LXI. We’ve been running through all our picks the last couple of days, and next up is Offensive Rookie of the Year. MVPOffensive Player of the YearDefensive Player of […]
full_text: SOUTH BEND, IN - NOVEMBER 22: Notre Dame Fighting Irish RB Jadarian Price (24) celebrates a touchdown with Notre Dame Fighting Irish RB Jeremiyah Love (4) during a college football game between the Syracuse Orange and Notre Dame Fighting Irish on November 22, 2025 at Notre Dame Stadium in South Bend, IN. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Some of the Windy City Gridiron staff made their picks for several 2026 individual season awards, and we’ll cap the predictions off by picking Super Bowl LXI. We’ve been running through all our picks the last couple of days, and next up is Offensive Rookie of the Year. MVP Offensive Player of the Year Defensive Player of the Year Offensive Rookie of the Year Defensive Rookie of the Year Coach of the Year Protector of the Year Super Bowl LXI Bryan Orenchuk: For ORTY, I’m going with the Seattle Seahawks Jadarian Price. Becoming RB1 on the Super Bowl champs is as ideal as it gets. Having your main competition begin the year on PUP makes it even sweeter. I expect a fantastic year for the former Fighting Irish RB2. Josh Sunderbruch: I feel like this is Jadarian Price’s award to lose. Sam Householder: Jeremiyah Love is going to get tons of opportunities for the Arizona Cardinals. The team might not be good enough, but I think he’s electric enough to earn the votes. Donald Gooch: I don’t think fans or the NFL quite realize how good Jeremiyah Love truly is, and while the Cardinals won’t be good and his running opportunities will be limited accordingly, I expect Love to post a 1,300-yard season and 6-8 touchdowns, which will be sufficient to earn him rookie of the year accolades. TJ Starman: Jadarian Price is where I’ve landed for OROY. I think it’d be harder for a WR to take it than one of the talented RBs, and Love is in a crowded backfield, while Price will at least start the season for Seattle as the bell cow with Charbonnet on PUP. Mongo Peanut: KC Concepcion. He’s got talent, opportunities, and already looks like he might be the top dog for the Cleveland Browns. Lester A. Wiltfong Jr.: The Cardinals may not be able to create a lot of running room for Jeremiyah Love, but he might catch 50+ balls in that offense, so his all-purpose yards will be enough to get him this award. Gary Baugher Jr.: KC Concepcion is looking great, but I worry about the cast of QBs throwing him the ball. I’ll go with Carnell Tate from the Tennessee Titans, banking on a good year 2 jump from Cam Ward to help Tate’s numbers. Erik Duerrwaechter: Ja’Kobi Lane, WR, Baltimore Ravens. The youngster has been the talk amongst league circles when predicting who’ll be the next receiver to explode on the scene as a rookie. He’s already taken command of the Ravens receiving game despite having Zay Flowers signed long-term. Jeff Berckes: Nothing against Jeremiyah Love, but it’s going to be tough to shine in Arizona this year. On the other hand, Jadarian Price has a clear path to a lot of touches for the defending Super Bowl champions – a team that would love to let their defense and running game carry them back to the playoffs. So for me, the Price is Right Price is the pick. title: Matt Suhey, Popular 1985 Chicago Bears Super Bowl Champion, Passes Away
summary: Former Chicago Bears fullback Matt Suhey has passed away at the age of 68, according to NBC Chicago. Suhey was the starting fullback on the 1985 Super Bowl championship Bears team. He scored the first touchdown of Super Bowl XX, helping lead the way to the Bears’ eventual 46-10 victory over the New England Patriots. […]
full_text: Former Chicago Bears fullback Matt Suhey has passed away at the age of 68, according to NBC Chicago . Suhey was the starting fullback on the 1985 Super Bowl championship Bears team. He scored the first touchdown of Super Bowl XX, helping lead the way to the Bears’ eventual 46-10 victory over the New England Patriots. Suhey also served as the lead blocker for Hall of Fame running back Walter Payton for most of his career. The two famously developed a very close bond during those years. Suhey played college football for Penn State University, rushing for 2,818 yards and 26 touchdowns from 1976 to 1979. He was selected by the Bears in the second round of the 1980 NFL Draft. Suhey went on to play 10 seasons in the NFL, all of them spent in Chicago. He totaled 2,946 rushing yards and 20 rushing touchdowns during his NFL career. Suhey also had 2,113 receiving yards on 260 receptions over the course of his career, including five receiving touchdowns.

title: Bears Dillon Thieneman gets surprise nod as possible Defensive Rookie of the Year from ESPN
summary: We already know first-round safety Dillon Thieneman will have to play up to his billing early for the Chicago Bears following the loss of running mate Coby Bryant in training camp. Maybe that’s why one ESPN analyst is taking what she calls a “calculated long shot” on the 25th overall pick from the 2026 NFL […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 29: Dillon Thieneman #31 of the Chicago Bears walks off of the field during an NFL preseason game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images We already know first-round safety Dillon Thieneman will have to play up to his billing early for the Chicago Bears following the loss of running mate Coby Bryant in training camp. Maybe that’s why one ESPN analyst is taking what she calls a “calculated long shot” on the 25th overall pick from the 2026 NFL Draft as a possible Defensive Rookie of the Year candidate Pamela Maldonado made an interesting call in her preseason picks for the prestigious award , slotting Thieneman third on the list of DROY potentials behind Ohio State products Sonny Styles (Washington Commanders) and Arvell Reese (New York Giants)—both of whom were top-10 picks. DT Caleb Banks of the Minnesota Vikings and Chiefs rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane rounded out the five picks. “The first-round pick is already Chicago’s starting strong safety. He should be around the ball plenty after playing 40% of his snaps in the box last season. Thieneman recorded 94 tackles in his final college season, while missing just 7.8% of his attempts,” Maldonado writes. With his sub-4.4 speed and physicality in the box, Thieneman certainly has the tools to do a little bit of everything from the safety position, though his best usage might be as box safety with the versatility to cover multidimensional offensive players in the passing game rather than patrolling centerfield. Earning that award, especially over highly touted pass-rushers and linebackers, might be a tough task, though. According to Maldonado’s research, a safety hasn’t won DROY since 1990. (So, literally since I was born.) Coincidentally, though, the last safety to do it was the Bears’ own Mark Carrier, who went off for a league-leading 10 interceptions and earned a Pro Bowl nod as a rookie. If Thieneman plays even half that well, that Rookie of the Year talk will be very deserved. Now, a lot has to go right around Thieneman in order for him to make those impact plays. One can’t assume the Bears are going to notch 23 total interceptions again in 2026 with the defensive front looking as suspect as it currently does (though Thieneman might end up making a lot of tackles). But if he’s as good as the Bears hope, perhaps he can help elevate a Bears defense in dire need of some blue-chip production. And you never know: maybe one of his teammates, like cornerback Malik Muhammad or defensive tackle Jordan van den Berg, might sneak their way onto this watch list by the end of the year, too.

summary: With the NFL offseason officially in the rearview mirror and each team pushing to field as healthy a roster as possible, it got me thinking about which players the Chicago Bears could least afford to lose. Especially after news came out this week about WR1 Rome Odunze and RB1 D’Andre Swift leaving practice early. Thankfully, […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 08: Joe Thuney #62 of the Chicago Bears looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Minnesota Vikings at Solider Field on September 8, 2025 in Chicago, Illinois . (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the NFL offseason officially in the rearview mirror and each team pushing to field as healthy a roster as possible, it got me thinking about which players the Chicago Bears could least afford to lose. Especially after news came out this week about WR1 Rome Odunze and RB1 D’Andre Swift leaving practice early. Thankfully, those were nothing major, but the question remains: Which starter, outside of Caleb Williams, would be the biggest loss for Chicago? If Rome goes down, we still have Darth Burden, Loveland and Jahdae Walker to throw to. If Swift goes down, I’d be a bit more concerned, but only because our depth behind Kyle Monangai would be on deck. Mongai himself would be more than capable. If Montez Sweat goes down, our pass rush would hurt. But our defense is already going to struggle, so that is not too much of a difference in my eyes. But if Joe Thuney goes down, especially with our LT spot still in flux and especially with a new center in town, I think our offense is hindered more than any other player missing time not named Caleb Williams. The inaugural Protector of the Year earned the third best pass blocking grade through PFF among ALL offensive lineman and was the highest rated mark for all guards. He helped mitigate the shortcomings with the revolving door next to him and helped Drew Dalman reach his first ever Pro Bowl in his first ever season in Chicago. Not only that, but he slid out to Left Tackle for the playoffs and held his own against a daunting Rams pass rush. Joe Thuney is the man and rightfully earned his flowers with the leagues first ever award strictly for offensive linemen. And he would be my choice. What about you? Who can Chicago LEAST afford to lose outside of Caleb Williams in 2026?

title: Bengals News: Buccaneers Game Week
summary: We are actually here gearing up for Week 1. We are to the point the roster is as set as things can be, and speculation falls on how the Cincinnati Bengals will fair against their opponent each week, and not just broadly comparing them to last year’s team. Week 1 we will see the Tampa […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 10 - Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) leads his team onto the field before a game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on Saturday, August 10, 2024. (Photo by Jeff Moreland/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We are actually here gearing up for Week 1. We are to the point the roster is as set as things can be, and speculation falls on how the Cincinnati Bengals will fair against their opponent each week, and not just broadly comparing them to last year’s team. Week 1 we will see the Tampa Bay Buccaneers travel to Cincinnati. They are led by a familiar faces at quarterback, Baker Mayfield. He had a bit of a renaissance with the Bucs after hopping around the league a few seasons. He spent his first four seasons with the Cleveland Browns after being selected No. 1 overall. He is 6-2 against Cincinnati. One of those losses coming as a Carolina Panther. However, this is a vastly different defense than from the 2021 season and earlier. Even in 2021, they played the final week of the season, and the Bengals rested most of their starters for that game since they had won the AFC North already. It likely will come down to how fast Joe Burrow and company can get going. The offense has had some slow starts despite being together for so long. If they are able to get out to a quick lead, It may help this defense that has plenty of new faces playing a large amount of snaps a bit easier. Bengals News Bryan Cook Comes Home To A City He Never Left: ‘This Is My Heart’ Cook proves time and time again why he chose the Bengals, and why it was probably for the Bengals to commit to him at safety. He has been a fairly vocal leader for a youngish defense, and he has a winning pedigree to back up what he is talking about. Cincinnati Bengals Could Shock NFL World With Top Defense Across 2026 Season Yo back and wonder just how this team lost some of these games, and the answer was too commonly that the defense blew it. It wasn’t always their fault, but when you are asking an offense to score in the 40’s to have a chance to win, you are going to lose in frustrating fashion pretty often. If this defense makes a huge leap, it will be a pretty fun season. How former Bengals players did at NFL cuts, waiver wire Unsurprisingly, the castoffs from the past few seasons have had issues sticking to another 53-man roster. I don’t think a better illustration of that is former-offensive guard Cordell Volson getting cut by the Tennessee Titans this offseason after being pretty much an unchallenged starter for most of his time with Cincinnati. It is a frustrating process we see all to often. Here is to hoping the linebackers aren’t going to fall down that same road. NFL News Steelers’ Alex Highsmith: There’s ‘added motivation’ to send Aaron Rodgers out ‘the right way’ It is a bit ironic to see the Pittsburgh Steelers turn into the Bengals during the Andy Dalton era. The Steelers last won a playoff game in the 2016 season, which means if they do not win again this year, it will have been a decade since they won a playoff game. Last year they got shellacked 30-6 by the Houston Texans. That was their fifth straight postseason where they lost their first game. I am sure things will be so much better with Mike McCarthy as head coach. Bold predictions for 2026 NFL season: Brock Bowers to set NFL record; who wins receiving triple crown? The Bengals are going to let it fly more than any team in football, and Chase will be the focal point of that aerial attack. If Joe Burrow stays healthy for the full season, this old Bayou connection will bear its juiciest fruit to date. Chase breaks Calvin Johnson’s single-season record of 1,964 receiving yards, wins Offensive Player of the Year and makes his 2024 triple crown-winning campaign look like a walk in the park. It is certainly bold. Safe to say everyone involved would love to see a deep playoff run first, but is Ja’Marr Chase is doing this, it is hard to imagine the team won’t be doing very well. Top 25 NFL free agents in 2027: Puka Nacua, George Pickens headline way-too-early list DJ Turner and Chase Brown both make the list. Turner is only behind Joey Porter Jr. at cornerback, and Brown is the only running back to make the top 25. Both hopefully get long-term deals next offseason, but odds are Turner at least gets hit with the franchise tag. Was Mitchell Tinsley really the hardest cut? Let us know in the comments!

title: Browns fans look back at the team’s biggest roster surprise heading into the season
summary: It’s been a week since the Cleveland Browns made their final roster cuts and named their initial 53-man roster. When I compare that to my initial 53-man roster projection, I successfully predicted 47/53 players (88.6%). The players who I predicted to make it, but got wrong, were WR Luke Floriea, TE Joe Royer, OL KT […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 27: Luke Floriea #81, Shedeur Sanders #2 and KC Concepcion #1 of the Cleveland Browns stand for the National Anthem prior to a preseason game against the New England Patriots at Huntington Bank Field on August 27, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images It’s been a week since the Cleveland Browns made their final roster cuts and named their initial 53-man roster . When I compare that to my initial 53-man roster projection, I successfully predicted 47/53 players (88.6%). The players who I predicted to make it, but got wrong, were WR Luke Floriea , TE Joe Royer , OL KT Leveston , DT Sam Kamara , LB Nathaniel Watson , and CB Tre Avery . Since then, a few other changes have happened, including the waiving of DE Julian Okwara , CB Michael Coats , and placing DT Kalia Davis on injured reserve, as the team opted to add some other or veteran depth to the main roster with the lines of DE Sam Williams , CB Noah Igbinoghene , and CB Toriano Pride . For this week’s Reacts poll, I asked fans what the biggest roster surprise was for the Browns. The options focused on two of the team’s cuts, as well as the decisions made at the quarterback decision. Leading the way with 41% of the vote was the clear cut departure of Floriea, the local wide receiver who quickly became beloved by fans. More surprising than him not making the roster was the fact that the team opted to not even sign him to the practice squad. He did have a tryout with a team this past Friday, but he’s dangerously close to never getting a shot in the NFL again, despite an excellent training camp. Next up in the voting with 33% of the vote was the fact that QB Dillon Gabriel landed on injured reserve to begin the season. People were half-expecting the Browns to try to find a trade partner for Gabriel, but after a 3-touchdown first half in the final preseason game, the last thing people expected was for him to suddenly have a “back injury.” With 21% of the vote was Leveston getting outright cut. I don’t think fans had much emotional investment into this one, but heading into training camp, Leveston was locked up in a position battle at right guard with Teven Jenkins . Toward the end of camp, Austin Barber started getting reps at right guard and performing well, but the assumption was that the team was simply testing the rookie’s versatility and potential. In actuality, it helped make Leveston expendable in terms of depth, along with Zak Zinter performing better to win a reserve spot. Last, but not least, only 5% of fans voted for QB Taylen Green making the team as the biggest surprise. Even though he may not be ready to “quarterback,” his speed showed a huge asset that Cleveland could consider leveraging in packages this season, something the team didn’t want to let get away. One user noted that “none of the above” would have been appropriate, with Coats having been waived. That’s fair, although our poll was created prior to that transaction. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 350/1 odds to win the Super Bowl, which is a big drop since roster cuts were made.

full_text: BLOOMINGTON, IN - SEPTEMBER 05: Indiana Hoosiers quarterback Josh Hoover (10) takes a snap at the line of scrimmage with a bloody nose and bloody mouth guard against the North Texas Mean Green on September 5, 2026, at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Brian Spurlock/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images When it comes to football, both at the college and pro levels, the conversations start at the quarterback position as the offensive side of the ball gets the vast majority of attention. College Football’s Week 1 slate of games had some excitement and a lot of quality play from quarterbacks and wide receivers. While the 2027 NFL draft is a long way off, for many NFL teams it will end up being the most important part of this season, even as Week 1 of the NFL is a few days away. Quarterbacks continue to be vital, despite a downward turn in overall passing yards , so NFL teams without long-term certainty at the position, like the Cleveland Browns, New York Jets, and Arizona Cardinals, will be spending a lot of time looking at this year’s QB class. Before the first full week of college football, rankings had different orders for the top quarterbacks, but a similar list overall. The Athletic’s Top 5 were: Trinidad Chambliss, Ole Miss Dante Moore, Oregon CJ Carr, Notre Dame Darian Mensah, Miami Julian Sayin, Ohio State CBS Sports had Moore at the top and included Arch Manning: Dante Moore, Oregon Arch Manning, Texas Trinidad Chambliss, Ole Miss Darian Mensah, Miami Julian Sayin, Ohio State Digging deeper into the rankings gave us Drew Mestemaker, Jayden Maiava, Noah Fifita, LaNorris Sellers, and many others. With Chambliss and Carr yet to play (both play Sunday evening at 7:30 PM), in Week 1, many of those top quarterbacks did not disappoint. Mensah, Sayin, Moore, Manning, and Maiava all threw for over 300 yards with at least three touchdowns. The only interception from that group was a bad decision by Manning to try to force things into triple coverage. Beyond that group, Georgia’s Gunner Stockton went 15 of 16 for 202 yards and three touchdowns before sitting out most of the second half. Indiana’s Josh Hoover, taking over for Fernando Mendoza, had four touchdown passes and 231 yards, and this bloody imagery: Josh Hoover is profusely bleeding, he remains in the game for now #iufb #unt pic.twitter.com/JiCcM4UvSE — Carter Lowe 🦡 (@carterjlowe) September 5, 2026 Sellers attempted just 23 passes, completing 19 of them for 270 yards and three touchdowns as South Carolina trounced Kent State. Fifita completed 76% of his passes for 262 yards and two touchdowns and rushed for 24 yards for the Arizona Wildcats. Not everyone had a great game in Week 1. Mestemaker, making a big step up in competition from North Texas last year, where he threw for over 4,300 yards, completed just 59% of his passes for just 241 yards on 49 attempts. On top of that, the new Oklahoma State quarterback had just one touchdown and two interceptions as the Cowboys were knocked off by Tulsa, 24-10. There is a long way to go, starting with Chambliss and Carr on Sunday night to close out Week 1, before the 2027 NFL draft. So far so good for a quarterback class that many expect could rival some of the best in the last decade or two. Did you watch any of the potential 2027 NFL draft class of quarterbacks in Week 1? title: Browns: Can HC Todd Monken break this unbelievable streak in Week 1?
summary: The Cleveland Browns hired Todd Monken as the franchise’s 19th full-time head coach at the end of January.  It was a smart move, as the 60-year-old Monken has considerable experience running an offense and is familiar with the AFC North Division after spending the past three seasons as offensive coordinator with the Baltimore Ravens. It […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 27: Head coach Todd Monken of the Cleveland Browns looks on prior to a preseason game against the New England Patriots at Huntington Bank Field on August 27, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns hired Todd Monken as the franchise’s 19th full-time head coach at the end of January. It was a smart move, as the 60-year-old Monken has considerable experience running an offense and is familiar with the AFC North Division after spending the past three seasons as offensive coordinator with the Baltimore Ravens. It is not without its risks, of course, as this will be Monken’s first shot at being a head coach at the NFL level, with his only previous head coaching experience coming at Southern Mississippi from 2013 to 2015. The Browns interviewed a variety of interesting candidates, but Monken was the preferred choice of owner Jimmy Haslam , and everything has always worked out when ownership has gotten involved in football decisions. Monken will get his first taste of being the head man in a game that counts when the Browns open the 2026 season against the Jacksonville Jaguars on September 13. It has been three years since the Browns won their opening game, a 24-3 defeat of the Cincinnati Bengals that saw quarterback Deshaun Watson pass and run for a touchdown in the victory. That won’t be the only streak that Monken will be looking to break, as the recent fate of Cleveland head coaches in their first game has been bleak. Would anyone be surprised to learn that Bud Carson was the last full-time head coach to win his Cleveland debut? And that came in 1989 in a 51-0 beatdown of the Pittsburgh Steelers? Since then, 11 full-time head coaches have come and gone in Cleveland, and not a single one kicked off their tenure with a victory. While we wait to see what Monken has in store for the Jaguars, let’s take a run through how each of Cleveland’s 18 full-time head coaches fared in their first game on the sidelines. Paul Brown – 1950 The NFL thought it was being clever when it scheduled the Browns to open the 1950 season on the road against the defending champion Philadelphia Eagles. Cleveland was coming off four years of dominance in the All-America Football Conference, and the Eagles were going to teach the upstarts a lesson. The Browns did not get the memo, however, and rolled to 448 yards of offense in a 35-10 victory that announced to the rest of the NFL that a new top dog was in town. Final record: 10-2 and the NFL Championship. Blanton Collier – 1963 In the first game in franchise history without Paul Brown as head coach, it was another blowout in the debut of the Blanton Collier tenure. Cleveland had 543 yards of offense, with Jim Brown combining for 262 rushing and receiving yards, as the Browns took down Washington by a score of 37-14. Final record: 10-4 and a Playoff Bowl loss to the Green Bay Packers. Nick Skorich – 1971 Another new head coach, another victory as the Browns opened their campaign under head coach Nick Skorich with a 31-0 win against the Houston Oilers. Quarterback Bill Nelsen led an effective offense, but it was a day for the defense as Cleveland held the Oilers to 35 rushing yards and forced six turnovers, including five interceptions. Final record: 9-5 and a Divisional Playoff loss to the Baltimore Colts. Forrest Gregg – 1975 All good things must come to an end, a lesson that Forrest Gregg learned in his first game as head coach of the Browns. Trailing 24-3 midway through the third quarter against the Cincinnati Bengals, Cleveland rallied behind a Gregg Pruitt touchdown run and a recovered fumble in the end zone by linebacker Charlie Hall to pull within seven points heading into the fourth quarter. The Browns threatened to tie the score, but two drives inside Cincinnati’s two-yard line ended up with zero points as the Bengals held on for the victory. Final record: 3-11, fourth place in the AFC Central Division. Sam Rutigliano – 1978 Sam Rutigliano was on the sidelines when the Browns opened the 1978 season at home against the San Francisco 49ers. Cleveland broke open a close game in the fourth quarter thanks to a 69-yard touchdown pass from Brian Sipe to Reggie Rucker, then closed out the scoring with a 23-yard field goal by Don Cockroft. Final record: 8-8, third place in the AFC Central Division. Marty Schottenheimer – 1985 Marty Schottenheimer took over as interim head coach midway through the 1984 season after Sam Rutigliano was fired, so this game serves as Schottenheimer’s first as the full-time head coach. And the game gave Cleveland fans a taste of the excitement to come in the next few years. The Browns rallied with 21 points in the fourth quarter, highlighted by Ozzie Newsome’s 25-yard catch-and-run touchdown to give Cleveland a seven-point lead with 38 seconds remaining against the St. Louis Cardinals. But the Cardinals used a 43-yard screen pass to Ottis Anderson to set up a game-tying touchdown to force overtime. St Louis won the toss in overtime, and then the game, as Neil O’Donoghue converted a 35-yard field goal. Final record: 8-8 and a Divisional Playoff loss to the Miami Dolphins. Bud Carson – 1989 In what was arguably the highlight of the Bud Carson era as a head coach, the Browns went into Pittsburgh in Week 1 and steamrolled the Steelers by a score of 51-0. Cleveland’s defense held Pittsburgh to 53 yards of total offense, sacked Pittsburgh quarterback Bubby Brister six times, and forced eight turnovers, three of which they turned into defensive scores. Final record: 9-6-1, with a loss in the AFC Championship Game to the Denver Broncos. Bill Belichick – 1991 It was a dreary start for the Browns under head coach Bill Belichick, as the offense managed only 32 rushing yards as Cleveland lost to the Dallas Cowboys by a score of 26-14. The Browns were trailing 13 points at halftime, but quickly cut into the deficit when Bernie Kosar hit Webster Slaughter on a 62-yard touchdown pass on the first play of the second half. The offense went cold from there, however, and the Cowboys closed out the scoring with a pair of field goals in the fourth quarter. Final record: 6-10, third place in the AFC Central Division. Chris Palmer – 1999 After three years without football, the Browns returned to the NFL to open the 1999 season at home on national television against the Pittsburgh Steelers in the first game under head coach Chris Palmer. There was no Hollywood ending, however, as the Browns managed just 40 yards of total offense, nine rushing yards, and two first downs in a 43-0 defeat. Final record: 2-14, sixth place in the AFC Central Division. Butch Davis – 2001 Points were hard to find in the first game under head coach Butch Davis. The game turned into a battle of field goals, with Phil Dawson’s 22-yarder tying the score at 6 with two minutes remaining. But a 49-yard kickoff return set up Seattle on the ensuing possession, and Rian Lindell converted a 52-yard field goal with three seconds remaining to leave the Browns on the wrong end of a 9-6 final score. Final record: 7-9, third place in the AFC Central Division. Romeo Crennel – 2005 It was another ugly day for the Browns in the debut of head coach Romeo Crennel, as the defense allowed 420 yards of total offense, and penalties wiped out a punt return touchdown and an interception return for a touchdown in what would be a 27-13 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. While Frisman Jackson posted the only 100-yard receiving game of his career, three turnovers from quarterback Trent Dilfer kept the offense from putting up a stronger fight. Final record: 6-10, fourth place in the AFC North Division. Eric Mangini – 2009 Cleveland took a three-point lead into halftime against the Minnesota Vikings thanks to a 67-yard punt return for a touchdown by Josh Cribbs, but it was all Vikings in the second half of a 34-20 loss in Eric Mangini’s first game as head coach. Cleveland had no answer for Minnesota’s…
