title: One fantasy football nugget for each NFL team
summary: It’s a new season. A clean slate. A time to wipe away all those fantasy mistakes you made a year ago… and make all new ones this year! Well, hopefully not. Fantasy football is a great way to showcase your football expertise and GM your own team, but to do that, you have to be […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 13: Jeremiyah Love #4 of the Arizona Cardinals runs against Hezekiah Masses #35 of the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter of a preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Cardinals defeated the Raiders 27-14. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s a new season. A clean slate. A time to wipe away all those fantasy mistakes you made a year ago… and make all new ones this year! Well, hopefully not. Fantasy football is a great way to showcase your football expertise and GM your own team, but to do that, you have to be equipped with the right information. That’s exactly what we have for you today, as we’ll provide one fantasy nugget for every NFL team. ARIZONA CARDINALS – Players selected third overall aren’t thrown into committee roles. Volume and dynamic ability are fantasy gold, and rookie RB Jeremiyah Love has both. ATLANTA FALCONS – Tua Tagovailoa’s short passes created the volume to help Devin Achane go from good to great. TE Kyle Pitts will be the receiving beneficiary of those dump-offs. BALTIMORE RAVENS – WR Zay Flowers quietly finished as the WR7 despite only catching five touchdown passes. There is no reason to not expect another top-10 finish. BUFFALO BILLS – Nothing is finer than being the workhorse back on a run-heavy team that scores often, and that is what RB James Cook III is. CAROLINA PANTHERS – The Panthers used a first-round draft pick on RB Jonathan Brooks. He’s finally healthy, and Carolina has a strong rushing attack. CINCINNATI BENGALS – WR Tee Higgins continues to be the best-bargain receiver who possesses both a safe floor and high upside should JaMarr Chase miss time. CLEVELAND BROWNS – Rookie TE Harold Fannin Jr. had the fifth-highest targets of his position, and there is no reason not to expect continued volume. DALLAS COWBOYS – Over the last six years, Dak Prescott has alternated between a top fantasy quarterback and an injured quarterback. Last year, he finished as QB5. Grab’em if you love him, but make sure you have a Dak-up plan. DENVER BRONCOS – WR Courtland Sutton is coming off of two-straight top-13 finishes and already has chemistry with Bo Nix. He’s the value pick while everyone else is chasing Jaylen Waddle. DETROIT LIONS – QB Jared Goff is the best-kept fantasy secret. He’s efficient, plays most of his games in a dome, has weapons galore, and a defense just bad enough to sustain scoring-friendly game scripts. He has three straight top-10 finishes. GREEN BAY PACKERS – WR Christian Watson has never finished inside the top 25 for WRs, and his target competition is Jayden Reed, Mathew Golden, and Tyler Kraft. Avoid the hype. HOUSTON TEXAS – Only three WRs have finished in the top 10 in points per game in each of the last three seasons – Puka Nacua, Amon-Ra St. Brown, and Nico Collins. INDIANAPOLIS COLTS – K Spencer Shrader is the new Brandon Aubrey. Use your last pick on him. JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS – QB Trevor Lawrence has a plethora of weapons and a great offensive coordinator. Expect another strong fantasy season from him. KANSAS CITY CHIEFS – Expectations are big for Kenneth Walker as he walks into an ideal situation, but Andy Reid spreads the ball around. Only once over the last decade (2017, Kareem Hunt) have the Chiefs had a RB finish in the top 10. LOS ANGELES CHARGERS – WR Ladd McConkey finished as WR12 his rookie year, but then what happened? Keenan Allen happened, but he’s really gone this time. Expect a return to stardom for this young Ladd. LOS ANGELES RAMS – Even with a 65/35 timeshare, Kyren Williams is a fantasy gem. He has three-straight top-10 finishes despite Blake Corum already being there to “steal” his volume. He’s the cheapest RB2 you’ll find in the draft. LAS VEGAS RAIDERS – QB Fernando Mendoza will be all the craze in Vegas at some point this year. If your roster space allows, stash this playmaking quarterback. MIAMI DOLPHINS – The Dolphins offense has been abysmal the last two seasons, and it is astounding that De’Vone Achane has finished as a top-6 RB in each of them. But he has. His volume and elusiveness won’t change. Pounce if he slides. MINNESOTA VIKINGS – Remember when Justin Jefferson was a consensus top-3 WR? Well, that time is now as long as J.J. McCarthy is not in charge of throwing him the ball. NEW ENGLAND PATRIOTS – WR A.J. Brown has never had a quarterback this good. Huge season loading… NEW ORLEANS SAINTS – There are so many good eats on Kellen Moore’s offense, but TE Juwan Johnson finished third in receiving yards for tight ends. He only had three touchdowns, but still finished in the top 10 for TEs. Had he caught three more touchdowns, he would have finished as TE3 for the year. Sleeper potential. NEW YORK GIANTS – QB Jaxson Dart has top-5 upside, but also could come with weekly high variance. If you roll the dice on him, package him with a stable QB you can find at a low cost (see Detroit Lions). NEW YORK JETS – WR Garrett Wilson is the most blah fantasy receiver out there. His upside is capped by a bad Jets offense, but his volume is continuous. The Geno upgrade should help him retain a WR2 finish. PHILADELPHIA EAGLES – Regression to the mean bodes well for RB Saquon Barkley, but wear and tear is a real thing. If you must venture down that aisle, handcuff him to Tank Bigsby, who enters RB1 territory should Barkley go down. PITTSBURGH STEELERS – QB Aaron Rodgers’ arm is spaghetti, so expect a lot of dump-off passes to running backs. This is good news for sneaky receiving RB Jaylen Warren. SEATTLE SEAHAWKS – Rookie RB Jadarian Price walks into a great opportunity after the departure of Walker and the often-injured Zach Charbonett SAN FRANCISCO 49ERS – RB Christian McCaffrey has finished as the best fantasy running back twice over the last three years. If you can stomach the risk, he delivers big rewards. TAMPA BAY BUCANNEERS – Don’t let recency bias make you sleep on RB Bucky Irving. He’s healthy now, and his volume, shiftiness, and usage as a receiver make him a valuable commodity. TENNESSEE TITANS – I love rookie first-round receivers from Ohio State, and you should too, but the WanDale Robinson fella might be one of fantasy’s best-kept secrets. He’s not a league winner, but an effective depth guy that you can snag at the end of your draft. WASHINGTON COMMANDERS – QB Jayden Daniels was a fantasy gem when he could run and he could stay healthy. Now, it feels like you can only have one or the other. Buyer beware.

title: Dallas Cowboys 2026 Opponent Preview: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
summary: The countdown to the start of the 2026 Dallas Cowboys season is in the home stretch, and we have just one NFC opponent left to preview in this ongoing series that will lead right up to that first Sunday Night Football test at the New York Giants. That team would be the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - DECEMBER 22: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers scrambles out of the pocket during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on December 22, 2024 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The countdown to the start of the 2026 Dallas Cowboys season is in the home stretch, and we have just one NFC opponent left to preview in this ongoing series that will lead right up to that first Sunday Night Football test at the New York Giants. That team would be the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who like the Cowboys were on the outside of the playoff picture looking in last season. Last season was the first time the Bucs did not make the playoffs under Todd Bowles, and the first time in five straight seasons. Continuity on offense, including Baker Mayfield, with young receivers expected to take a leap and a retooled defense will give Tampa Bay hope of reclaiming this division yet again, though it’s a division where all three other teams should and will feel confident about their own chances as well. Let’s take a closer look at what the Buccaneers have done this offseason. Buccaneers Key Free Agent Signings/Departures * SIGNED IN FREE AGENCY LB Alex Anzalone RB Kenneth Gainwell QB Jake Browning SAF Miles Killebrew G Dan Feeney (Re-signed) TE Cade Otton (Re-signed) DL A’Shawn Robinson LB Al-Quadin Muhammad * DEPARTED IN FREE AGENCY QB Teddy Bridgewater CB Jamel Dean WR Mike Evans RB Rachaad White The Buccaneers lost a future Hall of Fame wide receiver and face of the franchise player in Mike Evans this offseason when he chose the San Francisco 49ers in free agency. Evans was third on the team in targets in 2025, behind rookie Emeka Egbuka and tight end Cade Otton, who was brought back this offseason. This is an offense that will also be looking for more contributions from Jalen McMillan, Chris Godwin Jr., Tez Johnson, and a rookie “pet cat” of many draft observers, Ted Hurst. In the backfield, the team’s new complementary back to Bucky Irving is Kenneth Gainwell, coming over from the Steelers to replace Rachaad White. Gainwell and Irving both have big play potential as runners or pass catchers, and if the Bucs have a more consistent downfield pass game in 2026, watch out for what these backs can bring between the tackles to make this a more imposing offense as well. With a more balanced offensive approach and work done in the offseason to be quicker in the front seven with more pass rush juice, the Bucs will be looking for better close game outcomes to potentially take a massive leap in the win column. Alex Anzalone and A’Shawn Robinson are key additions to this front seven, along with first round pick Rueben Bain out of nearby Miami, which brings us to the rest of what the Bucs did in April’s draft. Buccaneers 2026 Draft Class Round 1, Pick 15: EDGE Rueben Bain Jr. Round 2, Pick 14 (46 Overall): LB Josiah Trotter Round 3, Pick 20 (84 Overall): WR Ted Hurst III Round 4, Pick 16 (116 Overall): CB Keionte Scott Round 5, Pick 15 (155 Overall): DT Demonte Capehart Round 5, Pick 20 (160 Overall): G Billy Schrauth Round 6, Pick 4 (185 Overall): TE Bauer Sharp The Bucs landed not one, but two Miami Hurricane defenders that were a part of a team that went to the national championship game in their home stadium, Bain and cornerback Keionte Scott. With a defensive tackle group that just added Robinson to pair with Calijah Kancey and Vita Vea, Bain is stepping into an ideal situation to win one-on-ones off the edge. How his consistent ability to do this in college would translate to the next level was hotly debated all spring, but Bain can certainly be an impact player very early on to watch as the Bucs try to get back to a higher standard on defense. Keionte Scott is a true nickel cornerback that feels like a natural fit in Bowles’ coverage scheme, while linebacker Josiah Trotter can slot in next to the freshly-signed Anzalone to develop as a rookie. The Bucs did a great job adding draft picks at positions they already have established talent and experience, giving them healthy depth and a chance to be more of a threat deeper into the season. Buccaneers 2026 Coaching Staff * New to staff this season: Offensive Coordinator Zac Robinson Passing Game Coordinator T.J. Yates Special Teams Coordinator Danny Smith Defensive Line Marcus West Quarterbacks Chandler Whitmer A concept that Cowboys fans are familiar with when it comes to the upside of hiring new defensive coordinator Christian Parker strongly applies to the Bucs coaching changes this offseason as well, and that is the added benefit of pulling a coach away from a division rival. Tampa Bay took this to an almost extreme level, nabbing offensive coordinator Zac Robinson away from the Atlanta Falcons, T.J. Yates from the Falcons, and adding QB coach Chandler Whitmer, who’s last NFL job was in 2024 – also with the Falcons. The Bucs and Falcons have played six straight one score games against one another, with the Bucs winning four of them, and these teams splitting last season. Atlanta is not expected to be very prolific on offense this season, and stealing assistants away on this side of the ball to create another situation for new Falcons HC Kevin Stefanski to navigate is well done if you’re a fan of the swashbucklers. Robinson’s best trait as an OC is his ability to scheme receivers open on the perimeter, something the Bucs need more consistency in as they evaluate this season if Mayfield will be the guy beyond 2025. Working alongside former longtime QB T.J. Yates as passing game coordinator and Whitmer as Mayfield’s latest QB coach gives the Bucs, on paper, a very strong brain trust around this offense that carries big expectations at the moment. Whitmer’s most recent stop is arguably the best résumé builder any coach coming from college to the NFL has ever had, being the QB coach and co-offensive coordinator for Fernando Mendoza and Indiana, who became the first number one overall pick out of Indiana after winning the school’s first national championship which capped an undefeated season – of course also a first for that program. NFL fans at large are familiar with the edge Mayfield plays with when feeling doubted or disrespected in any way, and although that angle comes from his own front office this time around, it very may still work to unlock the best of Baker in 2026, with coaching being a huge part of this equation too. Depending on how malleable the Bucs defense is under Bowles who will need to show adjustments as his time in the league passes the quarter century mark this season, this is a team with strong coaching continuity elsewhere and many reasons to believe in their ability to contend yet again. One of the best thing the defense appears built to do is limit big plays through the air, something they can exploit further with their own vertical pass offense, but how they match up physically against the run is a question mark. The Cowboys will take on this Bucs defense at home in primetime on a short week, immediately following a road test against the tough Houston Texans defense in week four. The last time these teams met in primetime was also in Arlington, with a 6-8 Cowboys team out of the playoff picture giving an inspired December performance in what proved to be the third to last game of the Mike McCarthy tenure. Dallas won 26-24, their last win of that season. It hardly feels like a rivalry, but all of the recent Buccaneers and Cowboys meetings have had some interesting raised stakes, and although the 2026 meeting comes early, it should feel no different on Thursday Night Football . This game is the start of a stretch for HC Brian Schottenheimer in year two where he will go up against very experienced head coaches, starting with Bowles and then Matt LaFleur in week six at the Packers, followed by Nick Sirianni at the Eagles in week seven. This comes after already playing John Harbaugh in the season opener and Dan Quinn in week…

full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - AUGUST 15: Caleb Downs #13 of the Dallas Cowboys looks on during the first quarter during the NFL preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on August 15, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the 2026 season the Dallas Cowboys largely ignored the offensive line, instead relying on names like Tyler Guyton to take a big step forward in 2026. Everything Dallas Cowboys fans need to know before the 2026 season – Staff, DMN Given how poorly last season went, there is a lot of shakeup that happened this offseason. And with the opener less than a week away, it’s probably best to catch up on all things 2026 Cowboys. Caleb Downs has a big brain. His ability to process the game allows the Cowboys to trust the rookie defensive back to play the slot, line up near the line of scrimmage or deep in the backfield. Join the conversation! Is the Cowboys Offensive Line Rebuild a Failure? – Mark Heaney, Inside The Star Dallas has done a lot of good things this offseason to add depth and rebuild critical positions. However, questions still remain along the offensive line. Starting from left to right, let’s make no mistake about it: this season is absolutely make or break for Guyton at left tackle. Dallas drafted him as a raw prospect, but that title can only last you so long. Parker’s roster building approach was two-pronged: rather than targeting the biggest names in free agency or on the trade market, he focused on adding quality starters who fit specific roles within his defensive scheme. Which is a pointless gamble if Dallas isn’t going to use the cap room to make a signficant move. Ferguson should have been playing for his future this season. The infraction occurred in the first quarter of the preseason Week 2 game against the Arizona Cardinals at the 12:07 mark. title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 7
summary: It is Day 7 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: SAN FRANCISCO, CA - JANUARY 17: Head coach Jimmy Johnson of the Dallas Cowboys celebrates after a victory over the San Francisco 49ers in the 1992 NFC Championship Game at Candlestick Park on January 17, 1993 in San Francisco, California. The Cowboys defeated the 49ers 30-20. (Photo by James Smith/Getty Images) It is Day 7 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. We’re now one week away as we reach Day 7 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, and we go to the game that changed the balance of power in the NFC and launched the Cowboys’ 1990s dynasty. Dallas went into a wet, muddy Candlestick Park against the team that had defined the previous decade and emerged with the victory, sending the Cowboys to their first Super Bowl in 15 years. Sunday, January 17, 1993 — 4:00 p.m. ET Candlestick Park, San Francisco, California Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 30, San Francisco 49ers 20 The matchup felt like a collision between generations. San Francisco, with an NFC best 14-2 record and right behind was Dallas at 13-3. Despite the 49ers’ four Super Bowl wins since the Cowboys’ last appearance, Jimmy Johnson’s young roster believed it was ready to replace them at the top of the conference. Occasional rain turned the Candlestick grass into a difficult, muddy surface, adding to the physical nature of the game. Dallas took the lead after Alan Grant fumbled a punt, which Daryl Johnston recovered at the San Francisco 22. Troy Aikman then connected with Michael Irvin to reach the one-yard line, but the 49ers managed to hold them off and force a field goal from Lin Elliott. San Francisco responded with Steve Young’s one-yard touchdown run, putting them ahead 7-3. The Cowboys regained control during the second quarter. Ricky Watters fumbled after a hit by Larry Brown, and Kevin Smith recovered for Dallas. Emmitt Smith eventually scored from four yards out to put the Cowboys ahead 10-7. However, Mike Cofer’s 28-yard field goal tied the game shortly before halftime. Elliott missed from 43 yards on the final Dallas possession, leaving the score 10-10 at the break. Dallas’s most important drive of the season came out of halftime. Aikman completed a spectacular 38-yard pass to Alvin Harper, and the Cowboys drove 78 yards before Johnston scored from three yards to make it 17-10. Cofer responded with a 42-yard field goal, cutting the Cowboys’ lead to four. The Cowboys responded with a championship-caliber performance. They controlled the football for approximately nine minutes, showcasing their dominance with a 79-yard drive. Aikman sealed the drive by finding Smith for a 16-yard touchdown, extending the Cowboys’ advantage to 24-13. The 49ers still had one major run left. Ken Norton Jr. intercepted Young and Dallas drove to the San Francisco seven, but Smith was stopped on fourth-and-one. Young then took the 49ers 93 yards, finishing the possession with a five-yard touchdown pass to Jerry Rice. With 4:22 remaining, Dallas’ lead had suddenly been reduced to 24-20 and Candlestick Park was alive again. What happened next became one of the defining plays in Cowboys history. Instead of becoming conservative, Dallas attacked on the first play after the kickoff. Aikman fired to Harper, who caught the ball over the middle and exploded downfield for a 70-yard gain to the San Francisco 10-yard line. In one play, all the momentum the 49ers had created disappeared. After three plays, Aikman found Kelvin Martin for a six-yard touchdown. However, the extra point was blocked, leaving Dallas leading 30-20 with 3:43 remaining. Around the two-minute warning, James Washington intercepted Young on San Francisco’s final serious possession, setting the stage for celebration. This game belongs this high on the countdown because it was the moment the Cowboys stopped being an exciting young contender and became the NFL’s next great team. San Francisco had been the defining franchise of the 1980s. Dallas walked into its stadium, beat it in a championship game and took control of the NFC. The Cowboys have since described the victory as the win that ignited their run as the “Team of the 90s” and the power exchange had begun. #Cowboys vs #49ers 1992 NFC Championship Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 30, San Francisco 49ers 20 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/6ENXwAN52T — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) September 6, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Aikman threw for 322 yards and two touchdowns without an interception, while Dallas went the entire game without committing a turnover. title: Why these three Cowboys players made the cut – and what to expect
summary: The preseason is over, the roster is set (for now), and the Dallas Cowboys have officially begun the next phase of their 2026 season. For some players, that meant the end of their time in Dallas. For others, it meant achieving the goal they had been working toward since training camp opened. There were plenty […]
full_text: Aug 28, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; New Orleans Saints offensive tackle Asim Richards (72) blocks Dallas Cowboys linebacker Tyrus Wheat (90) during the game between the Cowboys and the Saints at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The preseason is over, the roster is set (for now), and the Dallas Cowboys have officially begun the next phase of their 2026 season. For some players, that meant the end of their time in Dallas. For others, it meant achieving the goal they had been working toward since training camp opened. There were plenty of interesting roster decisions, but three players in particular stood out because of what they showed during training camp and preseason, and what their roster spots could mean for the Cowboys moving forward. WR Camden Brown There may not have been a bigger preseason surprise on the Cowboys roster than Camden Brown. The undrafted rookie wide receiver out of Georgia Southern entered training camp fighting for a spot in a crowded receiver room. With CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Ryan Flournoy, and Kavontae Turpin locked in, Brown was competing with a number of players for what could have been the final roster spot. Instead, Brown made the team. The 6-foot-2, 204-pound receiver showed enough throughout camp and the preseason to convince the Cowboys that his upside was worth keeping. With six receptions, 166 yards, 27.7 yards per catch and two TDs, that is production you simply can’t ignore, and now Brown finds himself on the 53-man roster. Camden Brown AGAIN! A NASTY one-handed grab for 6 DO NOT CUT pic.twitter.com/SP3iiKnAe9 — Tom Downey (@WhatGoingDowney) August 16, 2026 Now comes the hard part. Brown has gone from trying to make the team to trying to find a role on it. With the depth that Dallas has at receiver it may be difficult to do, but after seeing what he was capable of in camp and the preseason, if an opportunity arises, he can make the most of it. The easiest way to see the field for any bottom of the roster player is always through special teams. That maxim applies to all three we’ll discuss today, including Brown. WR Jonathan Mingo Mingo’s bubble roster spot was intriguing for a different reason. Unlike Brown, Mingo wasn’t an unknown coming into training camp. The Cowboys invested significant draft capital in him when he was moved from Carolina, meaning expectations have followed him throughout his young career. But his time in Dallas hasn’t exactly gone according to plan. Mingo entered this summer with something to prove, and his preseason gave the Cowboys enough reason to keep giving him opportunities. He finished the preseason with four catches for 82 yards and a touchdown. Including that 53-yard bomb in Arizona from Joe Milton. Mingo also repeatedly produced in practices at training camp. Joe Milton launches it 53 yards to Jonathan Mingo for the TD! (Via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/JW6GQRiNsK — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) August 23, 2026 The Cowboys kept Mingo on the initial 53-man roster alongside Brown, giving the former second-round pick another chance to carve out a role in an offense that already has Lamb and Pickens at the top of the depth chart. If Mingo can continue to turn the flashes we’ve seen into something Dallas can rely on, his roster spot could end up looking like one of the better decisions the Cowboys made this summer. Mingo’s NFL game experience should give him a minor role on offense, which would increase in case of any injury. Tyrus Wheat Tyrus Wheat’s spot might be the most telling roster move of the three. Wheat wasn’t competing for the same kind of spotlight as Brown or Mingo. He was competing for a place in a completely revamped Cowboys defense, where Dallas had plenty of options along the edge. And he made it. Wheat finished the preseason with eight tackles and two sacks, seven pressures and five run stops. Wheat brings versatility, experience and, most importantly, he has established himself as a core special teams contributor. . @Tyrus_Wheat18 takes down the QB 👏 📺: #NOvsDAL on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/kVTAokdKxV — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 29, 2026 The crowded edge group in Dallas means Wheat isn’t going to get a major defensive role immediately, although he’s shown when his number is called the Cowboys can count on him. Where he’ll really shine is being someone the team counts on for quality special teams play.

title: Pittsburgh perspective of new Cowboys OT Broderick Jones
summary: The Dallas Cowboys offseason has been rather quiet when it comes to contract drama and off-the-field issues. One thing that has not been quiet is the additions to the Cowboys roster. Dallas has been busy this offseason rebuilding their defense. While it started with trading for Rashaan Gary, being more active in free agency, and […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys offseason has been rather quiet when it comes to contract drama and off-the-field issues. One thing that has not been quiet is the additions to the Cowboys roster. Dallas has been busy this offseason rebuilding their defense. While it started with trading for Rashaan Gary, being more active in free agency, and using most of their draft class on defensive players, the Cowboys added very little to the offensive side of the ball. That is until they made a trade last week for Pittsburgh Steelers offensive tackle Broderick Jones. Jones, heading into his fourth year, has had a rocky start to his NFL career since being selected 14th overall in the 2023 NFL draft. But with Terence Steele having an underwhelming training camp and Drew Shelton struggling so far to start his career, the Cowboys decided on trading a third- and a sixth-round pick to the Steelers for Jones and a fourth-round pick. We can watch the tape and get an idea of why the Steelers wanted to move on from Jones, but there are signs of a player that has a future in the NFL starting at offensive tackle. I decided to talk with Steelers beat writer Nick Farabaugh to get a better understanding of what type of player the Cowboys added to their roster to compete for the starting right tackle spot. Let’s dive into our Q and A. There has been a lot of discussion around Jones health since the trade was completed. How did he look health wise in camp? Nick: Broderick Jones is back to being fully cleared to do all football activities. So, from a true health standpoint, he is fine, but the strength still needs to come back. Jones said multiple times he was 15 pounds lighter than his usual playing weight, which is around 315 pounds. That is largely due to him missing seven months of lifting while rehabbing the neck injury, so he will just need time to recuperate in that area. However, he is playing without restrictions. Jones mentioned moving around a lot as a reason for his struggles. Is there any merit to that and where do you think he’s played/fits best, left or right tackle? Nick: I do think there’s a lot of merit to that for Jones. The Steelers brought him in at left tackle and he basically played there in the entire lead-up to his rookie season before the Steelers threw him in at right tackle on limited reps in the middle of that season. As a result of that, he lapsed back into some bad habits he had at Georgia technique wise. He was thrown around from right to left tackle and back during the next few seasons, including this one, but he always looked more comfortable at left tackle. The motor movements looked more comfortable, and generally speaking, his athleticism played on both sides, but he was more in control of his pass sets on the left side. Schottenheimer spoke about the trade for Jones was about improving their depth, but more so having him compete with Terence Steele for the starting right tackle job. Do you think that’s a realistic expectation? Nick: I can’t speak to how Steele has played, but Jones struggled mightily this training camp and preseason. My initial expectation would be it is not all that realistic given the fact Jones could not beat out Dylan Cook, who has been a career-long practice squad player for the Steelers over the past few years. Cook is not that bad, but he is far more a swing-tackle level player than a starting right tackle. Jones’ struggles with his technique in the preseason make him competing for a starting spot a somewhat hard venture. Speaking of Steele, fans have always appreciated his work as a run blocker, but his pass protection as regressed significantly over the last few seasons. Should fans expect Broderick to be better in pass protection or as a run blocker? Nick: Generally speaking, Jones brings a lot of bite and aggressiveness to the run game. His aggressive streak and physicality, especially on gap runs as a puller, is one of the best parts of his game. Jones uses his athleticism well in space to tee up defenders, so he can also be a real weapon in the screen game. There is no doubt he will struggle in pass protection. Jones has too many inconsistencies with his hands and feet that show up snap-to-snap to make him a reliable pass protector where he stands now as a technician, but Cowboys fans can see Jones as a weapon in the run game, especially when he gets moving in space. What are some of Broderick’s main strengths and weaknesses? Nick: Jones developed a few bad habits he has been unable to get rid of from his time at Georgia. Most of his struggles in pass protection stem from an overreliance on his athleticism to get by, and as a result, he has some nasty habits. Jones too often ducks his head, crosses his feet, or bends at his waist in pass protection as a fallback mechanism. For him, the details in pass protection are just never consistent down-to-down. Sometimes, he reaches his set point with great footwork, but his hands get too wide and he opens his chest. At other points, the feet will be part of the problem. There is a lot of talent there, but nothing seems to click for him often enough. A few of his strengths come from his aggressive demeanor to punish the opposing edge rusher. That carries over into the run game, but he will also de-cleat jumpers and look to find work. His best trait in pass protection is identifying fronts and blitzes. Jones passes off stunts and twists with ease. The best trait in Jones’ game is his athleticism, which can sometimes allow him to get by on some reps, but it really adds to the play caller’s ability to run a diverse run scheme to his side. Jones has a good deal of strengths and tools to work with, but his game is so scattered it is hard to find a consistent player in there right now. How is Broderick in the locker room as a teammate? Nick: Jones is one of the jolliest players I’ve ever covered. It would not be a stretch to say he is the sunshine of the locker room given just how happy he is to be playing football on a day-to-day basis. He is a jokester who will love to pull pranks on guys. Either way, I can’t remember one bad word being said about Jones over his three years in Pittsburgh. He was a willing mentor and friend to any young or new players, took advice from veterans well, and added a lot of energy to some dead locker rooms over the years. Jones is a fantastic character off the field. Thanks to Nick for the information. What do you think of the trade now?

title: Best-case scenario: Examining what could take the Cowboys to the next level
summary: If you could measure the level of excitement for the upcoming Dallas Cowboys season, it would be somewhere between 1.20 and 1.22 gigawatts. For those who slept through science class, that’s over a billion watts of excitement. It feels good, and it’s not lost on us that this team is coming off of two straight […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker (left) with head coach Brian Schottenheimer at training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If you could measure the level of excitement for the upcoming Dallas Cowboys season, it would be somewhere between 1.20 and 1.22 gigawatts. For those who slept through science class, that’s over a billion watts of excitement. It feels good, and it’s not lost on us that this team is coming off of two straight losing seasons. One might think, here we go again, typical Cowboys’ optimism despite not even considering if things didn’t go as planned. Not true. We’ve considered it and shared those particular unsettling items with you yesterday . Today, we bring you happier thoughts as we talk about what could happen if the stars line up just right for our beloved Cowboys. Parker is the real deal From the moment the defense steps on the field, all eyes will be on Christian Parker’s group. Promises of a new scheme have set high expectations for this unit. Obviously, things will be better, but mediocre is not the benchmark. For the Cowboys to be true contenders, the defense must find its way into the top 10 in efficiency. That means that fancy words like “multiple,” “gap-and-a-half,” and “Star” must deliver on their promises of confusing quarterbacks and creating opportunities for defenders to affect the play. No one expects things to be magically fixed overnight, but if the defense starts out of the gate with some noticeable improvements, that’s a good sign that things are trending in the right direction. The offense is hyper-efficient Being better on defense is crucial, but let’s be real. If this team is going places, it’s going to be because of the offense. In year two of Brian Schottenheimer and Klayton Adams, the offense is poised to continue their excellence. With a physical rushing attack and the best wide receiving duo in football, the table is set for good stuff. Concerns at tackle make some wonder if the offense has limitations, but the Cowboys’ scheme has already been dealing with that, and it hasn’t held them back. For this offense, the stars will shine as Dak Prescott has never had it this good with two monster playmaking receivers at his disposal. They have an all-hands-on-deck pass-blocking group that features excellent chip blocking from players like Brevyn Spann-Ford, Hunter Luepke, and Javonte Williams, although nobody much talks about that. The Cowboys have done something crafty. They have increased their floor by having all these security measures in place to protect Prescott, while still having the firepower to be absolutely explosive. In the end, this offense is poised for big things. The GOTI stuff is silly, but if the Cowboys come out of this season with the greatest offense of 2026, it will surprise no one. They have the tools to pull it off. Difference-making new guys Never have we had an offseason where fans have praised the Cowboys’ front office so much. All the shrapnel from the Micah Parsons trade has subsided as everyone is focused on all the new cars in the driveway. There is no guarantee that these new faces will deliver good things, but there’s a fair chance some will. Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark are great players. Any notion that their better days are behind them is completely dismissed, and they should be one of the most talented defensive tackle duos in the league, and that doesn’t even take into account third-wheel Otito Ogbannia, who has done nothing but quietly impress the coaches. But the trio in the back may be equally as impressive as the trio upfront. The new safety team of Caleb Downs, Jalen Thompson, and incumbent Malik Hooker offers the defense the most dynamic safety group this team has had in decades. And it doesn’t stop there. There’s a new trio of pass rushers added to the group with Rashan Gary, Malachi Lawrence, and Von Miller added to the rotation. New acquisition linebackers Dee Winters and Jaishawn Barham join the fun, and cornerback Cobie Durant is rarely mentioned simply because there are so many other guys to talk about. The Cowboys have thrown so many darts at fixing this defense that if just half of them stick, it’s going to lead to a huge turnaround for this unit. Schotty effect The jury is still out on the second-year head coach, but if all this culture stuff turns into something, this could finally be the key factor that helps this squad get over the divisional round hump. Schottenheimer has created the perfect emotional bedrock for a deep playoff run. He brings high levels of enthusiasm with a clear message that mistakes will be corrected, one way or another. He fosters trust and chemistry, insisting on a unified, high-morale football culture. If Schottenheimer is on to something, then just maybe, all the talent the Cowboys have rustled up will finally amount to something in January. It’s what’s held this team back in the past, and if they finally have the right coaches in the right places, this could be the factor that brings the Cowboys back to their championship ways. Can you think of anything else? What is something that could happen that could help the Cowboys be contenders again?
author: Dan Rogers

title: While others play, Broncos wait
summary: Can you feel it, Broncos Country? It’s officially week 1 in the NFL! Okay, maybe it’s a little premature to get amped for Broncos football when Denver doesn’t play for another whole week, but that doesn’t make the football season any less ‘here’. This season kicks off with a Super Bowl rematch in Seattle, featuring […]
full_text: Nov 28, 2021; Denver, Colorado, USA; A general view of the Bronco on the top of Empower Field at Mile High as the sunsets in the fourth quarter between the Denver Broncos and the Los Angeles Chargers. Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-USA TODAY Sports Can you feel it, Broncos Country? It’s officially week 1 in the NFL! Okay, maybe it’s a little premature to get amped for Broncos football when Denver doesn’t play for another whole week, but that doesn’t make the football season any less ‘here’. This season kicks off with a Super Bowl rematch in Seattle, featuring the Patriots of New England and the champion Seahawks. Expect a lot of deserved seabird chest beating and exuberance in their 12th man identity, licensed from Texas A&M . On Thursday night, the NFL’s first international game takes place between the 49ers and the Rams in Australia. One wonders how our friends in the UK feel about a marquee divisional matchup being exported to Australia while Londoners are plagued for eternity with Jaguar home games. It just doesn’t seem fair. Sunday begins the bulk of the week 1 games, with 13 being played throughout the day. The first football Sunday in the 2026 season culminates in the obligatory Giants and Cowboys showdown that’s forced on innocent football fans every year, no matter how inept or awful both teams may be. It’s probably best to get this one out of the way early. Then… Finally… On Monday, a whole week from the time of this writing, the Broncos will travel to Kansas City to take on the Chiefs in a rare September tilt. Fans will finally get to see just how lethal Nix-to-Waddle connection can be this season. Questions will be answered, like how long will Sean Payton be able to keep his hands off Davis Webb’s play sheet? Will the defense absorb the loss of free agent John Franklin Myers? Will Jonathon Cooper’s offseason stupidity affect this team? Folks, you’ve waited for the 2026 season ever since a snowy white out and Jarett Stidham’s limitations surprised the Broncos in the AFC Championship game. Sure, Denver’s game is still a week away, but there is plenty of football to tide us over. Get ready Broncos Country, week 1 of the NFL season is officially here!

title: Broncos Country ready to watch Coleman, revived running game in Denver
summary: Although the top choice as the most anticipated young player to watch was not MY choice, I applaud the outcome on this week’s SBNation Reacts Poll all the same. Because who isn’t excited about a running game that could be revived by a rookie? So Jonah Coleman it is as the top choice for favorite […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - AUGUST 14: Jonah Coleman (20) of the Denver Broncos runs with the football during the Friday evening NFL preseason football game between the Atlanta Falcons and the Denver Broncos on August 14, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Although the top choice as the most anticipated young player to watch was not MY choice, I applaud the outcome on this week’s SBNation Reacts Poll all the same. Because who isn’t excited about a running game that could be revived by a rookie? So Jonah Coleman it is as the top choice for favorite young player to watch. No doubt we’ve been excited for this many seasons before. And it often depends on the scheme and how much an offensive play caller is willing to stick with the run game (ahem), but the preseason definitely brought us hope. Even Sean Payton thinks the run game is ahead of where it has been. “There’s a lot more to winning each week in regard to how we’re going to win this game and what we think we have to do to win this game. So per our run game, there’s some really good things I think that we’re doing,” Payton said earlier this week. “Then ultimately you kind of settle in on what type of run team you are relative to a zone scheme, a gap scheme and those types of things. So we certainly feel like we’re further along than we’ve been here in my three years, just with the depth in both groups.” In fact, Payton said early in camp that Coleman “did not look like a rookie.” Jonah Coleman will be a household name soon enough https://t.co/J27OkxqUYq — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 3, 2026 And hats off to Pat Bryant as well, hauling in a solid 36% of the votes. Payton has certainly been high on his progress this offseason and preseason, most recently touting the receiver’s consistency and strong hands. “Rarely does he have to leave his feet to make a clean catch. Even if you just skip to catch it, at that moment, everyone’s moving and you’re kind of frozen and rarely does he do that,” Payton noted. “So his yards-after-catch are noticeably different because his feet are on the ground as he runs through a ball. He’s smart, he’s sudden, he’s big. He’s having a heck of a camp. You guys have seen it, and it’s been consistent. He’s super intelligent. It’s really important to him, and I like his size.” My vote went to Que Robinson mostly because I’m curious how he helps fill in for an absent Jonathan Cooper. Plus, I want to see if (when) he’ll do more of this: GREAT sack by Que Robinson. He’s had a great camp pic.twitter.com/3pZO2mABdH — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 22, 2026

title: Random ESPN simulation predicts dream 2026 Detroit Lions season
summary: ESPN has a prediction system called Football Power Index, which uses a bunch of metrics and projections to simulate and predict outcomes. They use this system to create probabilities for the season, sometimes based on thousands and thousands of simulations. For example, their FPI system project the Detroit Lions to make the playoffs 71.4% of […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 14: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions celebrates a touchdown against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field on September 14, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images ESPN has a prediction system called Football Power Index , which uses a bunch of metrics and projections to simulate and predict outcomes. They use this system to create probabilities for the season, sometimes based on thousands and thousands of simulations. For example, their FPI system project the Detroit Lions to make the playoffs 71.4% of the time and produce an average of 10.5 wins this season—good for fourth-most. Every year, ESPN takes one of those thousands of simulations and zeroes in on it. How they select which of those simulations to dissect is not clear, but it’s presumed to be random. And this year’s simulation is one Detroit Lions fans would dream of. The simulation—labeled simulation No. 9,187 by author Seth Walder—not only has the Lions producing an NFL-best 13-4 record (tied with the 49ers), but it has Detroit winning the Super Bowl over the Los Angeles Chargers . Despite producing the best record, Detroit earned the NFC’s No. 2 seed, while the 49ers got the first-round bye. From there, the Lions won three straight games to get to the Super Bowl. Defeated the Packers 27-24 in the Wild Card round Defeated the Cowboys 27-20 in the Divisional round Defeated the Rams 20-17 in the NFC Championship Game Talk about an absolute dream route to the Super Bowl. First, Detroit gets to take out their biggest rival in the opening round. Then they take out a Dallas team that has been an annoying thorn in their side for decades. Then, Jared Goff gets one more slice of revenge against the franchise that jettisoned him, while Detroit also potentially ends Matthew Stafford’s career. A fun side-note from that game, Walder notes that Aidan Hutchinson wins Defensive Player of the Year over Myles Garrett. Then, in the Super Bowl, the Lions take down a Chargers team in a thriller. Here’s Walder explaining what happened in the simulation. Back and forth the game swung, with Cameron Dicker hitting a 55-yard field goal to put Los Angeles up 31-30 with 90 seconds left. But that was too much time for Goff. After a chunk passing play to Jameson Williams, the Lions found themselves in field goal range with plenty of time remaining. They handed the ball to Gibbs several times to inch closer and burn Los Angeles’ timeouts. Jake Bates connected on a 42-yard field goal as time expired to win the title. And as a sweet cherry on top, all the hype that the Chicago Bears are getting? It resulted in a 6-11 record for Ben Johnson and company. Alas, the simulation is meaningless in the grand scheme of things. But here’s hoping the reality we live in isn’t too far from from Simulation No. 9,187.

title: Discussion: What is the Detroit Lions’ ceiling for the 2026 season?
summary: “Next year is our year.” It’s become the battle cry of Detroit Lions fans annually after the previous season has come to its disappointing conclusion. There haven’t been many more recent seasons more disappointing for Lions fans than the 2025 campaign. For the prior four seasons, it had been all about growth. 2022 ended with […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 23: Head coach Dan Campbell of the Detroit Lions reacts after beating the New York Giants 34-27 in overtime at Ford Field on November 23, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images “Next year is our year.” It’s become the battle cry of Detroit Lions fans annually after the previous season has come to its disappointing conclusion. There haven’t been many more recent seasons more disappointing for Lions fans than the 2025 campaign. For the prior four seasons, it had been all about growth. 2022 ended with Detroit’s thrilling Week 18 win to kick the Packers out of the playoffs and make a statement that the Lions are coming. 2023 was the closest this team has ever come to making a Super Bowl, with an unbelievably run deep into the playoffs. In 2024, Detroit posted a franchise high in regular season wins (15), only to see it come crashing down with a second-round exit in the playoffs. After each of those seasons, it felt like it was inevitable Detroit would eventually break free of the postseason torment and finally reach the elusive Super Bowl. We said, “Next year is our year” with actual confidence, not an ironic twinge. Then 2025 happened. Detroit took their first clear step back as a franchise under coach Dan Campbell, and it certainly has some wondering if the Lions can right the ship and get back to championship contention. So today’s Question of the Day is: What is the Detroit Lions’ ceiling for the 2026 season? My answer: Well, if you believe ESPN’s prediction model and their full 2026 NFL season preview , Detroit’s ceiling for wins is a 13-4 record, and they’ve got a 71.4 percent chance of making the playoffs. So, certainly, making the playoffs should be considered the expectation, not the ceiling. But how far can this team make it? Can they really orchestrate a Super Bowl run? Does their roster compete with the consensus contenders like the Los Angeles Rams, Buffalo Bills, and Seattle Seahawks—the three teams with the best Super Bowl odds? I would contend that they do. Their offense is filled with superstardom, from Jared Goff to Jahmyr Gibbs to Amon-Ra St. Brown and Penei Sewell. And as I pointed out last week, the team’s depth on the offensive and defensive lines are deeper than they’ve been in quite some time . Sure, there are questions about how quickly the newly formed offensive line can gel together. And there is certainly warranted concern about both the starting-level talent and depth at cornerback. Every team has questions, and every roster has some talent gaps. We here in Detroit tend to obsess over those things, as they are typically the things that sink this franchise. And they could very well again this year. But at the same time, the Lions’ schedule looks easier to start the season, which should give the offensive line some grace to continue to build chemistry. And while the cornerback room certainly looks like the team’s biggest weakness, Detroit’s investment in pass rush and assignment-sound safeties could be enough to mask that weakness as much as possible. So do I think the Super Bowl is on the table for the Lions this year? Absolutely. Will it require several things to go Detroit’s way in 2026? Yes, and that is the case with every single Super Bowl winner in NFL history. So pour a little Kool-Aid in your coffee this morning. title: 2026 NFL predictions: Who will be the Detroit Lions’ Offensive MVP?
summary: It’s finally, officially Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. Our patience will finally be paid off with a full week of NFL games starting on Wednesday… then Thursday… then Sunday… then Monday. But before the games kick off, the Pride of Detroit staff will be providing their predictions for the 2026 Detroit Lions’ season […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 16: Jared Goff #16 and Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions in action against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on November 16, 2025 in Philadelphia, United States. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s finally, officially Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. Our patience will finally be paid off with a full week of NFL games starting on Wednesday… then Thursday… then Sunday… then Monday. But before the games kick off, the Pride of Detroit staff will be providing their predictions for the 2026 Detroit Lions’ season all week. And we kick things off Monday with our projections for the Lions’ Offensive MVP. You can make your predictions with the poll at the bottom of this story. Who will be the Lions’ offensive MVP in 2026? Brandon Knapp: Jahmyr Gibbs He’s arguably the top running back in the NFL, and now he is behind a reinforced offensive line with more chances to get the ball with David Montgomery gone. I think he will see an expanded role in the passing game, which pushes him toward of front of being the main weapon the Lions offense will prioritize in 2026. Anthony Balaj: Jared Goff Not because he’s the quarterback, but because he’s grown into one of the NFL’s best at his position. It’s the reliability and maturity in his play that now separates Goff from many of his peers, which will ultimately raise the floor of this young offensive line while maximizing the ceiling of the all-pro skill group. Ryan Mathews: Jameson Williams Jameson Williams will be the Lions’ offensive MVP in 2026. Most will point to Jahmyr Gibbs needing to be the MVP on this side of the ball, but if Williams is able to be the explosive threat he’s been the last two seasons on a little more volume, he’s going to be the most valuable part of the Lions’ offense. John Whiticar: Jahmyr Gibbs Sure, quarterbacks are more valuable and Jared Goff is critical to the offense’s success, but the expectations for Gibbs are sky-high. With no David Montgomery, he is now the focal point of an offense that loves to run the ball. The Lions lost a lot of games last season because their run game could not dominate early on and their passing attack was left to play catch-up. If the Lions are to be successful in 2026, they need Gibbs to be a contender for Offensive Player of the Year—and he has the talent to do so. Al Karsten: Jahmyr Gibbs Jahmyr Gibbs is primed to not only be the Detroit Lions’ offensive MVP this season, but contend for NFL Offensive Player of the Year while setting career highs in touches and total yards. Once the calendar flipped to November last season, Gibbs saw a significant dip in production outside of feasting on poor Commanders and Giants defenses. This season, however, he should benefit from both a rejuvenated offensive line and high-level play calling with the addition of Drew Petzing. That combination should put Gibbs in position to restore his consistent down-to-down production and explosiveness as he looks to return to a 50%+ success rate and 15%+ explosive play rate. With the Lions prepared to put even more on his plate in both the running and passing games, a 2,500+ total-yard, 20+ touchdown season is very much on the table. Erik Schlitt: Jahmyr Gibbs The Lions have made a major commitment to Gibbs this offseason and appear all-in on him as a key cog in this offense. With no David Montgomery to split carries with, it’s all-athlete, all the time. That’s the makings of an MVP-like season. Jeremy Reisman: Jahmyr Gibbs Outside of the quarterback, Gibbs is going to get the most touches of any Lions player—and that’s not just a function of him being the running back. He is the Lions’ offense. He’ll be their go-to guy for explosive plays. He’ll be their go-to guy in the red zone. He’ll be their early-down option to get into manageable downs and distances. And with no Isiah Pacheco early in the season, he’s likely to get an even bigger workload to start the year. Vote on your prediction for Lions’ Offensive MVP below!

title: Discussion: What are you most looking forward to seeing in Lions vs. Saints?
summary: We’re officially just a week away from the Detroit Lions’ season opener against the New Orleans Saints. Our long wait is almost over, and it will be a joy just to have the NFL back in our lives. But now that we’re within striking distance of Week 1, it’s time to actually start thinking about […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 23: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions runs in action against the New York Giants at Ford Field on November 23, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re officially just a week away from the Detroit Lions’ season opener against the New Orleans Saints. Our long wait is almost over, and it will be a joy just to have the NFL back in our lives. But now that we’re within striking distance of Week 1, it’s time to actually start thinking about the game. The Lions may be considered relatively big favorites—6.5 points according to FanDuel—but the first week of the season can be goofy. Teams tend to both be unpredictable and sloppy to kick off the season, and the Saints may not be too bad this year. It’s easy to forget that they finished the season winning four of their last five games. And we have no idea what the Lions are going to look like either? What will the reformed offensvie line look like? What will offensvie coordinator Drew Petzing have up his sleeve? Will Detroit’s front seven be as good as they looked in training camp? So today’s Question of the Day is: What are you looking forward to seeing the most in Lions vs. Saints? My answer: Well, outside of EVERYTHING, I’m excited to watch Jahmyr Gibbs. This offseason, Gibbs’ reputation seems to have launched into top-three running back conversation. What’s interesting about that rise in popularity is that it comes after a pretty mediocre season. By rushing success rate, Gibbs was just 25th out of 48 qualifying running backs. By EPA per rush, he was just 17th. But, of course, much of Gibbs’ struggles were caused by offensive line issues. Now, if you look at rushing yards over expected, Gibbs finished seventh in the NFL, per NFL Pro, and that’s what makes him extremely exciting to watch every game. Even if the Lions’ offensive line struggles out of the gate again this year, Gibbs is a danger to make a big play anyways. The offensive line could struggle to create a hole on 20 out of 21 plays. But on that one play? Gibbs could make a house call from 80 yards away. On top of that, I get the feeling we’ll finally start to see him expand his game a little as a true receiver—and more Gibbs with the ball in his hands is a good thing. title: Tucker Kraft named NFL’s #3 player on an expiring contract
summary: If you can believe it, there are already people looking toward the 2027 NFL free-agent cycle. Greg Rosenthal of NFL.com posted an article this week laying out the top 25 possible free agents for next year’s free-agent class heading into the 2026 regular season. Coming third on the list is the Green Bay Packers’ Tucker […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 02: Tucker Kraft #85 of the Green Bay Packers warms up prior to the game against the Carolina Panthers at Lambeau Field on November 02, 2025 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you can believe it, there are already people looking toward the 2027 NFL free-agent cycle. Greg Rosenthal of NFL.com posted an article this week laying out the top 25 possible free agents for next year’s free-agent class heading into the 2026 regular season. Coming third on the list is the Green Bay Packers’ Tucker Kraft. Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst has stated several times this offseason that he hopes to get Kraft, who has now returned to practice as a full participant, signed to a long-term extension before the Packers’ 2026 regular season begins. So far, though, there has been no news about a new deal for the tight end. According to Rosenthal, the only players who rank ahead of Kraft are Los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nacua and Dallas Cowboys receiver George Pickens, who was hit with the franchise tag at a $27.3 million figure in March. Here’s what Rosenthal had to say about Kraft: Both the Packers and Kraft have expressed confidence that a deal will get done soon, despite last November’s ACL tear. The 6-foot-5, 259-pounder has rare value as a complete tight end. The only other tight end on the list is Detroit Lion Sam LaPorta. It will be interesting to see which NFC North tight end ends up signing first, as whoever is second will almost certainly sign for a higher figure. They are the only two significant tight ends “due” for a new contract, following Kyle Pitts’ three-year, $54 million extension . Right now, here are the leaders at the position, in terms of average per year: George Kittle: $19.1 million per Trey McBride: $19 million per Kyle Pitts: $18 million per Isaiah Likely: $13.3 million per It seems likely that both Kraft and LaPorta will get more than Pitts, but the question is whether or not they will reset the tight end market entirely. So far, we’ve heard no details on how negotiations are going between the two parties on the Kraft deal. The Packers probably won’t be very active in free agency next year, as 2027 is when the belt will really start getting tight on the team from a cap perspective, but the top cornerbacks going into the 2027 class are the Steelers’ Joey Porter Jr., the Bengals’ DJ Turner II and the Broncos’ Riley Moss. The only running back to crack Rosenthal’s top-25 is Bengals ball-carrier Chase Brown.

title: Packers Depth Chart: We still don’t know who will start at cornerback
summary: Last week, we went through an exercise where we tried to pin down which 48 players among the Green Bay Packers’ 53-man roster would actually make the cut for being game-day actives against the Minnesota Vikings in the team’s Week 1 regular-season opener. Today, I want to focus less on the back end of the […]
full_text: Green Bay Packers Brandon Cisse (2) participates in mandatory minicamp Thursday, June 11, 2026, at the Don Hutson Center in Green Bay, Wisconsin. Dan Powers/USA TODAY NETWORK-Wisconsin | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Last week, we went through an exercise where we tried to pin down which 48 players among the Green Bay Packers’ 53-man roster would actually make the cut for being game-day actives against the Minnesota Vikings in the team’s Week 1 regular-season opener. Today, I want to focus less on the back end of the depth chart and turn our attention to the starting lineup, namely the much-talked-about outside cornerback position. Because of injuries or uncertainty, I think the biggest questions on the Packers’ depth chart right now, at least on the starting lineup, are: The offensive line (as Aaron Banks and Zach Bako-Bewele have been limited due to injury for basically all of camp) The defensive line (as we haven’t seen Javon Hargrave take a single snap in a preseason game, and don’t know how the rotation exactly works) The cornerback position (where players have been rotated in and out of the lineup) We’re going to hit on that last one today. Let’s start by talking about everyone’s favorite subject: Keisean Nixon. Keisean Nixon Much has been made about Keisean Nixon “competing” for his starting job going into the 2026 season, but it hasn’t really been rooted in reality. Yes, Nixon was rotating at the left cornerback position (the Packers play left and right corners; they don’t travel with top targets) for a very brief period of time, but it’s worth remembering the context of that short span. Nixon only really rotated significantly in practice, more than a typical entrenched starter, once Benjamin St-Juste (who is fourth in the cornerback pecking order right now) returned from an injury that led to him being sidelined during training camp. Before and after St-Juste’s “onboarding,” Nixon pretty much was a set-it-and-forget-it starter, consistently on the field at left cornerback for Green Bay’s first-team defense this summer. The headline you probably saw was about the coaching staff stating that Nixon was in a cornerback competition, backed by comments from coaches saying that every job is a competition all the time. If you didn’t catch that one, you probably saw that Nixon was frustrated that he stayed in the Week 1 preseason game for so long, as both he and rookie second-round pick Brandon Cisse were the only holdovers who also played with the second-team unit after the Packers’ first-team defense forced a three-and-out on the opening drive of the game. That, again, needs context, as Carrington Valentine, St-Juste, Kamal Hadden and Domani Jackson, all players who either made the 53-man roster or the practice squad (in Jackson’s case), were injured and unavailable to play against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Could the Packers have pulled Nixon earlier? Sure. Was Green Bay short on bodies at cornerback in that game? Absolutely. Worth mentioning: This only happened in Week 1 of the preseason, and when other cornerbacks started to get healthy, Nixon only played with the first-team defense for the remainder of the preseason. Generally, I file this under “People needed to write things in August.” You should fully expect Nixon to hold down the left cornerback position to start the 2026 regular season. The big question is what happens at right cornerback, opposite Nixon. Right cornerback What some fans might be surprised to hear is that it’s actually Cisse and Valentine battling for the right cornerback spot right now, and that we don’t have clarity on the situation- not that Nixon’s job is really up for grabs. Both Cisse and Valentine have been rotating at right cornerback throughout the summer, while St-Juste has mostly been a reserve who has split some reps with Nixon at left cornerback. Valentine and Cisse have both been injured at times during training camp, which has made the battle hard to call — one way or another. Fans were irate that Cisse was injured on a punt gunner rep in Week 2 of the preseason, but if he hasn’t outright won the job going into Week 1, I think we’ll see him a bit on special teams. Remember, the Packers have been near the bottom of the league in offensive players playing on special teams during head coach Matt LaFleur’s entire tenure in Green Bay, so a lot of the kicking game burden is placed on rotation and backup defenders. This is the punt where Brandon Cisse got hurt. He's at the top of the screen. St-Juste is the gunner at the bottom. Broncos ran a double vise pic.twitter.com/ROfkT0o8WC — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) August 23, 2026 If you want a look at Cisse’s contributions this summer, I clipped up all of the rookie’s defensive snaps this preseason, which you can find linked below. All of Brandon Cisse's pass coverage snaps through two preseason games. He's #2 always playing the (defense's) right cornerback pic.twitter.com/BGxg4qWBlN — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) August 23, 2026 Gun to my head, I’m not sure what happens at the right cornerback position against the Vikings. I could see it going to Valentine, Cisse or it being a rotation. I think all possibilities are on the table, and it’s not like the coaching staff has told us one way or another how they’re leaning opposite Nixon. — Pay attention early on to the secondary in the Vikings game this week, if the Packers’ coaches don’t outright name a starter at cornerback. We’ll know pretty early on (probably the start of the second quarter) if there’s a rotation going on, or if someone has been anointed as a true full-time starter at right cornerback.

title: Packers Preview: Get ready for Edgerrin Cooper playing on the edge
summary: One of the biggest changes you’re going to notice about new defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon’s scheme is his Penny package, which is essentially a 3-4 defense on the line of scrimmage with one true off-ball linebacker, split safeties and another deeper safety in the middle of the field. Green Bay Packers fans are familiar with […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Edgerrin Cooper #56 of the Green Bay Packers warms up before the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the biggest changes you’re going to notice about new defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon’s scheme is his Penny package, which is essentially a 3-4 defense on the line of scrimmage with one true off-ball linebacker, split safeties and another deeper safety in the middle of the field. Green Bay Packers fans are familiar with the 3-4 base defense, which was run by Dom Capers, Mike Pettine and Joe Barry in the past, along with the typical 4-2-4 Nickel defense that is played for the majority of snaps league-wide. This Penny wrinkle, though, is a little different than what you’re used to seeing from most NFL teams. That’s why we wrote about what it means for the secondary in an article two weeks ago . Today, though, I want to focus on the line of scrimmage, particularly with how Gannon is deploying “off-ball” linebacker Edgerrin Cooper. Edgerrin Cooper’s role in Penny Generally, when 3-4 defenses play Penny, they take their Will linebacker off the field to add a slot defender. The Packers, as a baseline, don’t play a slot defender, but a third safety. The other change-up Green Bay has is that they aren’t taking their Will linebacker (Cooper) off the field, at least with the first-team defense. Because Cooper is one of the team’s better defenders, Gannon has actually played Cooper on the edge, displacing the edge defender opposite Lukas Van Ness (generally Barryn Sorrell) this preseason. So instead of taking off the Will to add a slot defender, the Packers’ first-team defense has taken off an edge defender to play a third safety and then slid Cooper to an on-the-ball position. I keep reiterating that this is only true of the first-team defense, because with the second- and third-team units, Green Bay has played true edge rushers in Cooper’s role and actually has taken the Will off the field. This seems to be a game plan that the team has to keep one of its best players on the field, while also still keeping three defensive tackles jammed up on the line of scrimmage to stop the run. Penny with Edgerrin Cooper on the edge pic.twitter.com/U4rL2um5Mj — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) September 6, 2026 As you can see in the clip above, Cooper has been playing on the edge to the opposing offense’s passing strength (the side with the most receivers). Van Ness has been playing opposite the passing strength. Same 3 penny look but the the slot is split from the formation. Cooper detaches from the edge. Very college football pic.twitter.com/UjYsLJplUL — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) August 8, 2026 So far, we haven’t seen a clip of Cooper actually rushing the passer from this look, as on passing plays only three defensive tackles and Van Ness have been sent at the quarterback, but that will probably change once the regular season begins. As a reminder, teams play Penny to prevent shot plays down the field (with the three safeties) and to stop the run (with the five line of scrimmage players) when teams are playing three-receiver sets, as opposed to stopping the short passing game or middle-of-the-field passing concepts. Very first game last year, Packers end up with Preston Smith lined up against the opponent's #1 WR in the slot. Ok, clearly have to work on some kind of call within the structure of the defense to get out of that. You have all season AND the offseason. I just can't. pic.twitter.com/A6kKqLtiKO — Aaron Nagler (@AaronNagler) October 10, 2023 Having Cooper as the designated “dropper” out of an odd front look should help protect the Packers from one of the hiccups that they ran into when they’ve run a 3-4 defense in the past, which was that teams would simply spread them out and get Preston Smith into the slot. At a minimum, Cooper should be able to help out in coverage a bit more than Smith, but the big question is whether or not Cooper will be able to set an edge against NFL tight ends and offensive tackles in the run game. So far, we’ve only seen him play that look against the run just once. The other question with the Penny package, overall, is whether Van Ness and three defensive tackles have enough juice in the pass-rushing department to actually generate pressure on opposing quarterbacks. The Micah Parsons question We’ve seen Van Ness kick inside in some looks under Gannon, but they’ve all been in the team’s Nickel sets, not their 3-4 defense or in Penny. One question I have down the line is what this Penny formation ends up looking like when Micah Parsons returns to the lineup, whenever he gets off the PUP list. Does Van Ness just go to the bench, and the team keeps Cooper on the field? Does Cooper go to the bench, and the team keeps Van Ness on the field? Do all three stay on the field, with Cooper and Parsons on the edge and Van Ness kicked inside in place of a defensive tackle? It’s hard to make heads or tails of the situation right now, since Parsons wasn’t a factor in the Packers’ preseason, but I can say as a fact that Van Ness never kicked inside the offensive tackle this summer outside of Nickel personnel looks — which don’t include either the 3-4 defense or the Penny defense. — Keep an eye out for the Packers’ Penny look throughout the regular season. You’re almost certainly going to get this look against the Minnesota Vikings in the regular-season opener. Green Bay ran it enough, be it on Family Night or in the preseason (with multiple units), that I’d be shocked if it’s a tool they don’t use regularly. Whenever Parsons does come back, though, it will evolve in some way. What it will evolve into is sort of an open question right now.
