title: Groupthink: Texans 2026 Season Outlook
summary: Ladies and gentlemen, you’ve arrived at Week One of the NFL Season. Soak it up, the wait is over. The Texans have Greater Expectations than Pip. Three straight AFC Divisional Round finishes has set the benchmark for this franchise. Fans and pundits expect the team to make a run, but another tough schedule and a […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - AUGUST 20: Quarterback C.J. Stroud #7 of the Houston Texans leads his team onto the field ahead of the NFL preseason game between the Houston Texans and the Las Vegas Raiders on August 20, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Ladies and gentlemen, you’ve arrived at Week One of the NFL Season. Soak it up, the wait is over. The Texans have Greater Expectations than Pip. Three straight AFC Divisional Round finishes has set the benchmark for this franchise. Fans and pundits expect the team to make a run, but another tough schedule and a questionable offensive line will set the terms for this team. With the season right around the corner, I checked in with the Battle Red Blog crew to gauge their hopes, expectations, and reality checks for the 2026 season. What is your outlook for the 2026 season? What record do you think the Texans will have, and if they make the playoffs how far will they go? VBallRetired: I will go 11-6 and AFC South champions. I see them losing in the divisional round again. The team will look very similar to last season with great defense and spotty offense. We will be a better running team but the passing game takes a step back without Higgins. That glass ceiling just can’t quite be broken this year. Mike Bullock: I’ll echo the 11-6, but I think this year H-Town gets another AFC Championship appearance only to lose in some gut wrenching, “this is why we can’t have nice things” sort of way. Lights-out defense, improved offense, but a few “tragic” ball bounces sets another team up to get destroyed by the LA Rams in the Super Bowl. Then the “waiting for next season since 2002” kicks back in. L4Blitzer : I’ll go with the ol’ standby of 10-7 with a +3/-2 on the record. Houston plays a difficult schedule (7th toughest) and they hopes that the offense can actually be better vs last year. If they can improve the offense and can avoid any major defensive injuries, they have a better chance to get that coveted 2 or 1 seed. However, if the offensive line can’t gel and/or Stroud is more broken from last January than we thought, then a losing record could be in play. Playoffs are likely but I won’t put them higher than the divisional round until I actually see them do it. Patrick H.: I’m gonna be optimistic and say they go 12-5, get the first round bye and get to the conference championship game. Beyond that I don’t know that I feel confident saying I like our chances against the field. So much of this hinges on four things. A) The bad/inexperienced playcalling at offensive coordinator has been resolved (only time will tell). B) The offensive line has been sufficiently addressed by the talent and depth on the roster. (11 offensive linemen made up of high draft picks, free agents, and trades on the opening roster). C) The offensive line lives up to the expectations of being at least average (a significant improvement over the last several years). D) The struggles C.J. Stroud previously experienced were caused by the problems mentioned in A, B, and C and have all been resolved. E) A crap ton of good injury luck. If all of these hold true, nothing stops this team. Kenneth L.: To quote Mike’s Why this is Houston’s Year post, Nick Caserio and Demeco Ryans have “assembled arguably the best team the Texans have ever had” in three years. Top to bottom, the Texans have the weapons, defense, and top-end talent to secure a Super Bowl. Going all the way takes more than talent. There’s health, luck, a couple good calls, and continuous roster management needed. My big prediction is that by Week 7, if the Texans are 6-1 or 5-2, the will trade their first round pick for an offensive lineman. A top-end guard on a failing team could be the difference maker for this Texans team. The weakness, it doesn’t take nine years of writing for this site to tell you that the offensive line is confounding. Neither Braden Smith (IR) or Wyatt Teller will start on this re-made (x4 seasons in a row) offensive line. There’s concern over LT Aireontae Ersery’s development and regression by Ed Ingram. I think Houston will go 12-5. Losses to Buffalo, Dallas, Jacksonville, Baltimore, and Philadelphia. These are teams that can score at will, because otherwise this defense will SWARM. I’m hoping this defense is must-watch TV for fans. I the playoffs, Houston will be without a doubt the team no one wants to face regardless of their rank. Unfortunately, I do predict another divisional round exit. Whether it’s to the emerging teams such as New England or Denver, or the stalwarts Buffalo, Kansas City, or Baltimore, someone will have our number.

title: Monday Musings: Will Chiefs’ offense or defense rank higher in 2026?
summary: With a week to go until the Kansas City Chiefs kick off the 2026 regular season against the Denver Broncos on “Monday Night Football,” it’s time to think about the year as a whole and how it could play out. I joined Jay Binkley of 96.5 The Fan for a Chiefs discussion on the Kansas […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy of the Kansas City Chiefs watches during pregame warm-ups prior to the preseason game against the Los Angeles Rams at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images With a week to go until the Kansas City Chiefs kick off the 2026 regular season against the Denver Broncos on “Monday Night Football,” it’s time to think about the year as a whole and how it could play out. I joined Jay Binkley of 96.5 The Fan for a Chiefs discussion on the Kansas City airwaves on Monday morning and enjoyed thinking through the last question Jay asked: By the end of the season, which unit will be better? Offense or Defense? It’s a tough question. Last season, the Chiefs’ defense finished sixth in points allowed and 10th in total yards allowed; the offense finished 21st and 20th in the same categories, respectively. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo’s unit has outranked the offense in both for three consecutive seasons. In 2022, the last season before offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy initially left the staff, the offense ranked first in points and yards while the defense ranked 16th and 11th. That was the last time the Chiefs’ offense clearly drove the team’s success. Still, I see the Chiefs’ defense outranking the offense this season. The rookies will come on as the season progresses under Spags, especially pass rusher R Mason Thomas and cornerback Mansoor Delane, and could be a top-10 or top-8 unit by season’s end. The offense may not be putting up the gaudy statistics that quarterback Patrick Mahomes has before, but a strong run game should give the offense a higher floor than the last few seasons.

title: Another game-by-game prediction for the Chiefs’ 2026 season
summary: The NFL regular season is back! After months of waiting, football returns to our televisions Wednesday evening. Before the games kick off, I wanted to predict the record and what level of team we have in the Kansas City Chiefs this season. We’re following the optimistic perspective from Rocky Magana’s 12-5 prediction last week. Let’s […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 28: Head coach Andy Reid of the Kansas City Chiefs watches second quarter game action during an NFL preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks at Arrowhead Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL regular season is back! After months of waiting, football returns to our televisions Wednesday evening. Before the games kick off, I wanted to predict the record and what level of team we have in the Kansas City Chiefs this season. We’re following the optimistic perspective from Rocky Magana’s 12-5 prediction last week . Let’s get started with Week 1 against the Denver Broncos . Week 1: vs. Broncos I’m starting the season with a loss. I don’t love the Chiefs-Broncos matchup. The Broncos have a secondary that can blanket Kansas City’s pass catchers, and one of the most ferocious pass rushes in the NFL. On top of this, left tackle Josh Simmons might not play. Without Simmons, I don’t think the Chiefs will be able to pass protect long enough for receivers to get open. I expect the defense to keep the score close, but don’t trust the offense. Verdict: Loss Week 2: vs. Indianapolis Colts The good news for the Chiefs is if Simmons misses some time, the next three opponents don’t have fierce pass rushes. The Chiefs offense should look much better in this game. The Colts offense isn’t as strong this year without Michael Pittman and Braden Smith. With Daniel Jones off an injury as well, the Chiefs bounce back. Verdict: Win Week 3: at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins are going to be one of the worst teams in the NFL. This should be an easy win for the Chiefs. Verdict: Win Week 4: at Las Vegas Raiders Maxx Crosby could give us some problems, but it appears Kirk Cousins will be starting for the Raiders in this game. I expect the Chiefs pass rush to dominate against a shaky offensive line and an old, immobile quarterback. We go into the bye 3-1. Verdict: Win Week 5: Bye Week 3-1 Record! Week 6: vs. Los Angeles Chargers At this point, the hope is Simmons will be back. I expect the Chiefs to split their series with the Chargers this year. I think the Chargers will start the season stronger as they have a new offensive scheme with Mike McDaniel that won’t have much tape on them yet. I do think they will slow down as time goes on, but this is still early enough in the season for them to give us problems. Verdict: Loss Week 7: at Seattle Seahawks The Chiefs defense will keep this game close, but I don’t trust our offense against Mike McDonald. Seattle is best at defending the middle of the field and limiting the open windows the Chiefs want to attack. They will make the Chiefs throw outside the numbers against our receivers, and I don’t trust the Chiefs to hit enough throws to move the ball. This is a tough matchup for this roster. Verdict: Loss Week 8: at Broncos As I mentioned, I just think Denver is a bad matchup for us. For two years, the Broncos secondary has smothered the Chiefs. Even with Simmons back, their pass rush and blitzing can still get home. The Broncos offense should be better with Jaylen Waddle at wide receiver. The Chiefs need to make upgrades to their roster to match up with Denver better. Verdict: Loss Week 9: vs New York Jets The previous three games are a brutal way to come out of the bye, but fortunately, the next three should be wins. The Jets are also one of the worst teams in the NFL, and I expect the Chiefs to play desperate in this spot. I would predict a Chiefs blowout in this game. Verdict: Win Week 10: at Atlanta Falcons I expect the Chiefs to keep that positive momentum into Atlanta. The Falcons quarterback situation is pretty dire, and their pass rush is one of the worst in the NFL. These games should give the Chiefs a chance to catch an offensive rhythm. Verdict: Win Week 11: vs. Arizona Cardinals The Cardinals’ skill-position talent is exciting, and they have a young defense. Of these three easier games, I think this one will be the most competitive. But the Chiefs still have much more talent than the Cardinals. The Chiefs’ defense chokes out whoever plays quarterback for the Cardinals in this game. Verdict: Win Week 12: at Buffalo Bill s After three easier games, the schedule gets tough again with Buffalo on a short week. Joe Brady is a different coach, but the Bills have consistently beaten the Chiefs in the regular season. I expect the Chiefs’ defense to play well this year, but I think the Bills run the ball well in this game, and I think the Chiefs lose a close game late. Verdict: Loss Week 13: at Los Angeles Rams The Rams have one of the most loaded rosters in recent NFL years. They have a chance to have top-3 units on both sides of the ball. I could see the Chiefs keeping it close with their game plan, but the Rams’ defense, with Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald, closes it out. Verdict: Loss Week 14: vs. Cincinnati Bengals After two tough losses, I think the Chiefs bounce back in a shootout in Cincinnati. The Chiefs’ run game takes off here for the rest of the year. The Bengals also score points, but Kansas City’s young defenders make big plays late to close out the win. Verdict: Win Week 15: vs. New England Patriots This was a tough one for me to pick, but I ended up having this as a loss. The Patriots secondary is very good in man coverage and could stifle our passing game. Drake Maye is really good and can make aggressive throws to beat our defense. This is a close game that goes down to the wire that New England pulls out. Verdict: Loss Week 16: vs. San Francisco 49ers San Francisco has so many injured players already, and they’re an old team. I don’t expect them to play well this late into the season. The Chiefs roll in this game. Verdict: Win Week 17: at Chargers By this point, I expect the Chargers to show more cracks, and the Chiefs will be peaking. The Chiefs go into Los Angeles and win by double digits as they dominate the Chargers’ shaky interior offensive line and run the ball well. Verdict: Win Week 18: vs. Raiders Rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza will probably be playing by then, but with the Chiefs at 10-7 and likely needing this win for their playoff hopes, they come out focused and end the game early. Verdict: Win Bottom Line Overall, I had the Chiefs at 10-7. The light early schedule besides Denver should give them a chance to start 3-1. Their stretch after the bye week and after Arizona is brutal, but Kansas City does have lighter stretches as well. By December, I expect them to be playing their best football as the run game develops and the defense improves over time. Teams that can play man coverage well will be a tough matchup for us, which caps the Chiefs’ record for me, but I think they’ll be in the mix to make the playoffs.

Players with less than four accrued seasons who are cut while injured revert to a team’s IR if unclaimed on waivers. title: The Rams can help close Kyle Shanahan’s window
summary: Sean McVay and Kyle Shanahan were hired as head coaches in the same year for the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers, respectively. McVay boasts a Super Bowl win while Shanahan has finished on the cusp twice. Shanahan is not running out of time with the 49ers. He’d be one of the most sought […]
full_text: San Francisco 49ers' head coach Kyle Shanahan speaks to the media at AAMI Park in Melbourne on September 7, 2026. (Photo by Martin KEEP / AFP via Getty Images) / -- IMAGE RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE - STRICTLY NO COMMERCIAL USE -- | AFP via Getty Images Sean McVay and Kyle Shanahan were hired as head coaches in the same year for the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers, respectively. McVay boasts a Super Bowl win while Shanahan has finished on the cusp twice. Shanahan is not running out of time with the 49ers. He’d be one of the most sought after candidates on the open market if he separated from the team. However, the sand is dwindling for this version of the 49ers. Thursday night’s game between these two teams is not a must-win for either NFC West foe. Shanahan must win over the next four months or his window in San Francisco could be shut so tight it may not be worth trying to re-open. The 49ers’ offense is Shanahan’s hallmark. Year 10 brings a quarterback that is still young surrounded by a lot of pieces that no longer are. Trent Williams is soon to be 38—around the same age as Matthew Stafford at a much more physically demanding position. Kyle Juszczyk is 35. Mike Evans is 33. George Kittle is 32 and is coming off another serious injury. Christian McCaffrey is 30 but is much older in running back years. Ricky Pearsall has been swallowed whole by the injury bug. The problem isn’t so much that the 49ers are old—that isn’t necessarily true. They are simply old in all the wrong places. San Francisco has tried to turnover its defense and raise the next generation of stars. It simply hasn’t worked. I wrote last season that the 49ers’ draft class was off to a poor start to their careers . That is still true after the calendar has turned. Mykel Williams will start the season on the PUP list and miss at least the first four games. There is talk about San Francisco’s best rookie piece from a year ago, Alfred Collins, no longer being a scheme fit for Raheem Morris’ defense. Brock Purdy helped a roster littered with talent reach new heights. He brought more to the table than Jimmy Garoppolo ever did. But now that the 49ers are paying Purdy top dollar, can he elevate a middling roster to competitive in the same way he made a great roster even more formidable? Purdy may never be a superstar quarterback. We know a sizeable portion of his production should be credited to Shanahan. There are serious questions about the signal caller’s game. Can he find a deep ball and reduce turnovers under pressure? The state of the 49ers feels very fragile. Shanahan has years left on his contract and teams would probably trade at least a first round pick in order to bring him on board. But his runway in San Francisco seems to be coming to an end, barring a surprise turnaround. If the Rams take care of business on Thursday night, they can keep Shanahan and the 49ers on their downward trajectory.

title: Shanahan throws shade at Rams: NFL ‘let them off the hook’
summary: Kyle Shanahan believes that the Los Angeles Rams are so pressed about playing the 49ers at SoFi Stadium that they convinced the NFL to move the game to Australia this season, and San Francisco’s coach said on Sunday that it still won’t matter. In a press conference just days ahead of their Week 1 matchup, […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 22: Sean McVay, head coach of the Los Angeles Rams, embraces Kyle Shanahan, head coach of the San Francisco 49ers, after a game at SoFi Stadium on September 22, 2024 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Kevork Djansezian/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kyle Shanahan believes that the Los Angeles Rams are so pressed about playing the 49ers at SoFi Stadium that they convinced the NFL to move the game to Australia this season, and San Francisco’s coach said on Sunday that it still won’t matter. In a press conference just days ahead of their Week 1 matchup, Shanahan said that the league “let the Rams off the hook” by moving a Niners “home game” (aka at SoFi Stadium) to Melbourne, but that “it won’t be much different here”. Shanahan expects the same pro-49ers crowd to be present at the Melbourne Cricket Grounds this Thursday. Shanahan said he was initially disappointed that NFL "let the Rams off the hook" by taking away a 49ers' "home game" at SoFi Stadium. But after being in Melbourne for a few days, Shanahan feels "it won't be much different here" — he expects 49ers' fan dominance in MCG — David Lombardi (@LombardiHimself) September 7, 2026 The 49ers have had an undeniable presence at SoFi Stadium, but Shanahan isn’t being shy about his belief that the Rams have pushed the NFL to move the game as to avoid the story this year. ProFootballTalk’s Mike Florio has described Shanahan’s attitude about the game this season as “salty” regarding the trip to Australia: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan has been salty about the Rams’ desire to export a home game to Australia, in order to avoid yet another San Francisco-fan takeover of SoFi Stadium. Now that Shanahan and the 49ers have hunkered down in Melbourne, Shanahan feels differently. Shanahan currently believes “it won’t be much different” in Austrialia — and he expects the so-called Faithful to take over the 100,000-seat Melbourne Cricket Ground on Thursday night. But if the Rams gave up their supposed home-field advantage against the 49ers in order to avoid the embarrassment of having red far outnumber blue in the L.A. venue, it apparently won’t be much different for the NFL’s first-ever game in Australia. The Rams have lost six of their last seven regular season home games against the 49ers, but did win a playoff game at SoFi Stadium in 2022.

title: Week 1 is an important test for Rams CB Jaylen Watson
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have historically been OK with a lack of size at the cornerback position. Their last few draft picks—although rare—have demonstrated this from Cobie Durant and Derion Kendrick to the likes of Tre Tomlinson. But the Rams did something very out of character this offseason: they made a major free agent signing […]
full_text: Woodland Hills, - June 08:Rams Jaylen Watson (35) at Rams practice on Monday, June 8, 2026. (Photo by David Crane/MediaNews Group/Los Angeles Daily News via Getty Images) g | MediaNews Group via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams have historically been OK with a lack of size at the cornerback position. Their last few draft picks—although rare—have demonstrated this from Cobie Durant and Derion Kendrick to the likes of Tre Tomlinson. But the Rams did something very out of character this offseason: they made a major free agent signing and brought in a player with real size attributes. Jaylen Watson is listed at 6-2 and 197 lbs. The addition of Watson got lost in the shuffle during the aftermath of LA’s trade for higher profile corner Trent McDuffie, his Kansas City teammate. McDuffie also fits the Rams’ preference or accommodation of smaller defenders, although he has a strong lower half and is a willing tackler out of the slot. However, in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers, Watson may be the more important contributor out of the two. The San Francisco 49ers’ biggest offseason addition was receiver Mike Evans. It wouldn’t be wise for the Rams to ask McDuffie to cover one of the most physical receivers in the NFL—this is a job for Watson. The 49ers are hoping that Evans can deliver a similar impact to Davante Adams’ contributions in his first season in Los Angeles. The veteran caught 60 passes for 789 yards and 14 touchdowns in 14 games. San Francisco isn’t betting on Evans accumulating 1,000 yards. They are looking for the same type of red zone production that helped LA boast the highest scoring offense in 2025. There is just one man that stands between Evans and that goal in Week 1. Expect to see Watson on Evans early and often—and the corner must primarily win his opportunities in the short areas of the field. The good news for Watson is that Evans may not be 100% healthy to start the season. He missed nearly all training camp and preseason practices and just recently started ramping up. Evans is probable to play, although it could be realistic to expect a limited workload. You can almost guarantee that, if on a snap count, San Francisco will ensure he’s on the field in the red zone. Jaylen Watson versus Mike Evans is one of the most important matchups as the Rams and 49ers clash in Melbourne, Australia in a NFC West season opener.

title: Matthew Stafford has been fantastic in international games
summary: When the Los Angeles Rams take the field in Melbourne this week against the San Francisco 49ers, it will feel somewhat like home for quarterback Matthew Stafford, even though they’ll be playing several thousand miles from L.A. Stafford has played in a pair of international games during his long career, and both times he’s put […]
full_text: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 19: Matthew Stafford of Los Angeles Rams (#9) and Jarquez Hunter of Los Angeles Rams (#27) celebrate after the NFL 2025 game between Los Angeles Rams and Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium on October 19, 2025 in London, England. (Photo by Dan Istitene/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the Los Angeles Rams take the field in Melbourne this week against the San Francisco 49ers, it will feel somewhat like home for quarterback Matthew Stafford, even though they’ll be playing several thousand miles from L.A. Stafford has played in a pair of international games during his long career, and both times he’s put up performances to remember. Last year, Stafford led the way in a dominant 35-7 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars in the Jags’ second home, London. It was bizarre game for the Rams, box score-wise, considering they only tallied 271 yards but scored five touchdowns. All five of those touchdowns, in fact, came from the right arm of the NFL’s Most Valuable Player. While only averaging 5.5 yards per attempt and racking up 182 total passing yards, Stafford hit Davante Adams for three scores, plus one apiece for Terrance Ferguson and Konata Mumpfield. One of the most impressive parts of the win and Stafford’s effort in particular is the fact the Rams didn’t have first-team All-Pro wide receiver Puka Nacua available in the game. Without him, Stafford completed passes to 10 different receivers and Los Angeles cruised to a victory last October. Matthew Stafford faced a season-high 55.9% blitz rate against the Jaguars and threw all five of his touchdowns against the blitz. Stafford tied Patrick Mahomes and Baker Mayfield for the most TD passes against the blitz in any game since 2016. #LARvsJAX | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/kkDwSMpf5B — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) October 19, 2025 You have to go over a decade back in time to get to Stafford’s other international appearance, a legendary comeback for the Detroit Lions over the Atlanta Falcons. Two full seasons before the notorious collapse in the history of football, the Falcons led the Lions 21-0 at the half in London. Atlanta wouldn’t score again, however, while Stafford engineered one of his NFL-high five fourth-quarter comebacks that season. Along with three field goals from Matt Prater, including the game winner as time expired, Stafford connected with Golden Tate in the third quarter and Theo Riddick in the fourth for touchdowns as part of the comeback effort. That was one of Stafford’s best seasons in Detroit, earning a Pro Bowl nod while leading the Lions to the postseason, a rarity at the time for that franchise. That game, in particular, was one of the biggest moments of that campaign. Ideally, this would be a harbinger of things to come for the Rams this week, but considering past events don’t dictate future outcomes (and neither of those games was completely on the opposite side of the world), this is probably little more than a pair of fun anecdotes. But, if it helps you get some trash talk off this week, then it was all worth it.

title: A positive historical trend for Aaron Donald
summary: One of the biggest questions around the NFL pertaining to Aaron Donald’s return to the Los Angeles Rams is about whether or not he can still be the same Aaron Donald he was during his original run, when he was the best defensive player in football. It’s still entirely possible that he’s a massively impactful […]
full_text: One of the biggest questions around the NFL pertaining to Aaron Donald’s return to the Los Angeles Rams is about whether or not he can still be the same Aaron Donald he was during his original run, when he was the best defensive player in football. It’s still entirely possible that he’s a massively impactful piece for the Rams’ defense, but at the same time the odds are slim he’s as good as he was then. Again, he was previously the best defensive player in football and has since spent two years away from the game. But there is one thing that’s certainly working in his favor: the position he plays. This isn’t a hard-and-fast rule by any means, but generally speaking interior defensive linemen, especially ones that already play at a high level, often age more gracefully than other players and positions. I have no idea how close to 100% prime Aaron Donald the 2026 version of Aaron Donald will be; I'm just excited we get to find out. But here's one thing I would say…Donald is already one of the freakiest humans to ever play the game, it feels like a total waste of time trying… — Sam Monson (@SamMonsonNFL) August 30, 2026 In 2025, there were just two interior defensive lineman 35 years old or older who played an NFL game. That’s relevant, of course, because that’s how old Donald is now. One was 36-year-old Cameron Heyward, one of the best defensive tackles of his era, who started all 17 games for the Pittsburgh Steelers and earned his second second-team All-Pro honor , and sixth All-Pro nod overall. Then there’s John Jenkins, who’s never been a star but has been as steady as they come at the position. With the Baltimore Ravens last season, Jenkins started 14 games and played in all 17, forced a pair of fumbles and tallied a 64.7 PFF grade, which was 45th among 134 qualified interior defensive linemen. No, that’s not a perfect metric, but you get the gist. Go back a season prior, to 2024. Heyward was a first-team All-Pro at 35 years old, Jenkins (also then 35) posted the second-best Approximate Value (a metric from Pro-Football-Reference) of his career, and Linval Joseph had a fine if not unspectacular year in Dallas. Pro-Football-Reference also lists Calais Campbell as a nose tackle in 2024, and if you want a shining example of a lineman who is just as effective as they continue to age, that’s your guy. This is just a small sample of examples overall. You can dig back through recent NFL history and find plenty of guys who fit this bill. Damon “Snacks” Harrison was a sought-after piece up front for years as he continued to age. In 2018, Buffalo Bills legend Kyle Williams was a Pro Bowler at 35 years old. The Carolina Panthers got a year’s worth of quality snaps from 35-year-old Hollis Thomas in 2009. The reason this feels relevant is that we’re not just cherry picking one successful guy out of 20 options for all these years. There aren’t many who last to that age, but the ones who do aren’t just serviceable, they’re legitimate needle movers. That includes Aaron Donald, who is still TBD on playing. https://t.co/2iaYovqPhr — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 4, 2026 That brings us back to Donald. Clearly, there’s some positive history on his side here in the sense that older defensive linemen still make a positive impact, historically speaking. There’s also the fact that, to paraphrase Scott Steiner, he’s a genetic freak and he’s not normal. No disrespect to even a future Hall of Famer like Heyward, but Donald is on the short list of the greatest players to ever suit up. He may not be at the peak of his powers when he takes the field, whether that’s in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia or later on. But there are still plenty of good reasons to believe Aaron Donald is going to be a game wrecker in his return to the field.

title: Raiders News: Former Raider Richie Incognito is excited about the new OL coach
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are looking to improve at the offensive line position. It was abysmal last season, and the hope is that the new coaching staff can maximize the group’s talent. Offensive line coach Rick Dennsion is already making an imprint. During preseason, the execution was precise and looked completely different than it did […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 10: Owner and managing general partner Mark Davis of the Las Vegas Raiders talks to Richie Incognito #64 before a game against the Chicago Bears at Allegiant Stadium on October 10, 2021 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are looking to improve at the offensive line position. It was abysmal last season, and the hope is that the new coaching staff can maximize the group’s talent. Offensive line coach Rick Dennsion is already making an imprint. During preseason, the execution was precise and looked completely different than it did the year before. Cousins was under pressure one snap, and Mike Washington Jr. averaged 7.3 yards per carry. It caught the eye of former Raider Richie Incognito. Incognito was with the Raiders in 2019 before injuries ended his career. During an interview with Raider Nation Radio, he gave his thoughts on Dennsion and the new outlook for the line. “These guys work hard and their frustration last year was they are putting in all this time, they’re not getting the results on the field, but they really felt like they weren’t getting coached up in the meeting rooms, so there was a lot of frustration.” “I think that frustration is completely gone with a guy like Rick Dennison. He is highly detailed. He’s all about fundamentals. He’s going to get these guys all on the same page and you could see it in the preseason. You could see the double teams happening, the bodies hitting the floor. The backs hitting the holes, so it’s an exciting time.” Hopefully all of this hits the field next Sunday against the Miami Dolphins. It will be the first test for the new offensive line to make its mark on the season. title: Revisiting the Raiders’ return game with the 53-man roster settled
summary: Now that the dust from the 53-man roster shuffle is settled and the Las Vegas Raiders preparing for their Week 1 season and home-opener, it’s ample time to revisit the team’s long-dormant return game. With the Silver & Black knee-deep in training camp and preparing for a trio of preseason clashes, I dove into the […]
full_text: May 20, 2026; Henderson, NV, USA; Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Tre Tucker (1) practices during organized team activities at Intermountain Health Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Candice Ward-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Now that the dust from the 53-man roster shuffle is settled and the Las Vegas Raiders preparing for their Week 1 season and home-opener, it’s ample time to revisit the team’s long-dormant return game. With the Silver & Black knee-deep in training camp and preparing for a trio of preseason clashes, I dove into the Raiders’ kickoff and punt return units as special teams boss Joe DeCamillis navigated through the 90-man roster to identify talent to man the two specialized roles. Midway through August, wide receivers Tre Tucker and rookie Malik Benson were getting looks for the respective gigs , in practices. But when it came to the preseason clashes, the reps were dominated by late free-agent addition Deven Thompkins. The 26-year-old wide receiver was a July 27 add — alongside Patrick Johnson — and the diminutive (5-foot-8 and 155-pound) but speedy (4.35-second 40-yard dash time at Utah State’s Pro Day) wideout fielded seven kickoffs for 198 total return yards (28.3 yards per return average) with a long of 33 yards. He also returned four punts for 25 yards (6.3 yards per return average) with a long of 12 yards. When cutdown day arrived on Sunday, Aug. 30, however, Thompkins was waived before being signed to the practice squad the following day. While there’s a distinct possibility Thompkins is a call-up from the taxi squad during the regular season, his roster availability creates redundancy which is a good thing over the course of the 17-game regular season that can be grueling. That said, let’s take a look at the Raiders on the 53-man roster who not only have experience as NFL return men, but are likely to be the choice for DeCamillis as Las Vegas embarks on the initial season under rookie head coach Klint Kubiak. From yesterday at #Raiders camp…AJ Cole with the booming punt, Deven Thompkins with the return. pic.twitter.com/UWKedlb5bB — Paul Gutierrez (@PaulHGutierrez) August 5, 2026 The Incumbents As the Raiders embarked on preseason contests, they were mandated by the NFL to produce depth charts. While there were some spots already set in stone — such as elite punter AJ Cole III being the starting punter (especially without anyone competing with him) — the starting kick and punt returner was Tucker. Running back Dylan Laube was listed as the second-team kick return man while rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy was second-team punt returner. We’ll focus on the veterans Tucker and Laube for this portion, though. Let’s start with the wide receiver. I’ve written about this before, but I’ll reiterate: During his collegiate career at Cincinnati, Tucker was a prolific Bearcats’ kickoff return man amassing 67 total returns for 1,670 yards and two touchdowns; season high in 2021 with 22 returns for 557 yards and a score. Because of that production and usage, it was a logical assumption when the Raiders made the wideout their third-round pick (100th overall) in the 2023 NFL Draft, Tucker would get his fair share of opportunities to do that job in Las Vegas. No dice. In his three seasons in the league, Tucker’s career count reads: One kick return for 23 yards, and that lone statistical mark is from last season. This is largely due to the Silver & Black’s wide receiver room dwindling in name talent since Tucker was drafted meaning he was often precluded from special teams play because of his importance to the offense (Tucker’s total snap counts read: 2,260 on offense to just 104 on special teams in his initial three seasons in the NFL). Las Vegas wide receiver group is still questionable at best, so despite being listed as the top return man in preseason, Week 1 and beyond most likely will have another Raider manning the duties. This brings us to Laube, a reserve running back taken in the sixth round of the 2024 draft (208th overall) that’s been cutting his teeth on special teams his first two season in the league (318 special teams snaps to just 29 offensive snaps). The 26-year-old tailback paced the Raiders with 33 kick returns for 855 yards (25.9 yards per return average) with a long of 38. #Raiders RB Dylan Laube back at it after making the 53 🏴‍☠️ Special teams impact helped lock in his roster spot: 🏈 Led team in kickoff & punt return yards this preseason 🏈 Posted a team-high 3 special teams tackles 🏈 Versatility too valuable to leave off the roster Now… pic.twitter.com/tUQlsV6Z5B — Taylor Rocha (@TaylorRochaTV) August 28, 2025 The Noobs That term above isn’t just for players new to the NFL, but also to the Silver & Black. Dareke Young, who reunites with Kubiak after the wide receiver/special teamer spent his four seasons with the Seattle Seahawks, made the most of his limited opportunities as a kick return man in the Pacific Northwest with 10 returns for 322 yards (32.2 yards per return average) with a long of 60 yards. While he’s been an adept gunner on coverage units, standing 6-foot-2 and 224 pounds, he’s a blend of physicality and speed that can provide more of an imposing presence as a return man. Let’s get back to Benson. A rookie riser for much of the offseason, the 6-foot-1 and 195-pound sixth-round pick (195th overall) from the most recent draft brings much-needed electricity and explosiveness — on both offense and special teams. The 23-year-old wideout did well with his opportunities as Oregon’s punt returner last season with nine returns for 161 yards and a score — an 85-yarder against USC. McCoy, on the other hand, was getting reps as a punt returner in training camp and did field six of them at Tennessee in 2024 for 59 yards (9.8 yards per return average). The fourth-round selection (101st overall) in the 2026 draft is still getting back to health and confidence he showcased before a knee injury sidelined him for the 2025 season. Thompkins isn’t the only practice squad member who has experience as a return man. Running backs Dare Ogunbowale and undrafted rookie Roman Hemby have fielded kickoffs. The veteran Ogunbowale has 22 kick returns for 424 yards under his belt, but the 32-year-old hasn’t returned a kick since the 2024 season (one for 12 yards). Hemby, on the other hand, had nine returns for 203 yards at Indiana in 2025 and in preseason action, the 24-year-old returned four kickoffs for 105 yards. Horizon The assumption here is Tucker’s role on offense means shielding him from potential bit hits and injury as a return man. Which facilitates to Laube and/or Benson getting primary looks. McCoy will likely figure in as a punt returner but ensuring the promising prospect remains healthy for a defense looking to establish an identity under defensive coordinator Rob Leonard can put him in a similar category to Tucker on offense. But don’t be surprised to see Thompkins yo-yoing from practice squad to active roster as the season progresses.

title: Raiders News: Amy Trask thinks the Raiders made the right call on Mendoza
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders decided to roll with Kirk Cousins as the starting quarterback to start the season. It wasn’t a surprise to much of the Raiders fan base with Fernando Mendoza expected to sit and learn behind the veteran. The expectation had already been set. Former Raiders executive Amy Trask agrees with the decision. […]
full_text: Amy Trask at Sportico Invest Los Angeles held at 1 Hotel West Hollywood on May 8, 2024 in Los Angeles, Calfornia. (Photo by Jesse Grant/Sportico via Getty Images) | Sportico via Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders decided to roll with Kirk Cousins as the starting quarterback to start the season. It wasn’t a surprise to much of the Raiders fan base with Fernando Mendoza expected to sit and learn behind the veteran. The expectation had already been set. Former Raiders executive Amy Trask agrees with the decision. During a segment on CBS Sports Network, she gave her thoughts on the Raiders quarterback situation. “You drafted him with the No. 1 pick, presumably because you believe him to be your quarterback of the future. So you need to balance short-term with long-term. And my understanding is that Klint Kubiak is putting an emphasis on long-term planning, long-term success. And I think that speaks highly of Klint.” The Raiders are in rebuild mode, and the team is looking to be a contender in the next few seasons. That’s why it is important to make sure Mendoza is ready to play so his confidence isnt shaken up early. Mendoza does have the personality to handle it, but there is no need to rush right now. title: Hitman or Hype? Harrison Smith’s Return Highlights Vikings Roster Overhaul
summary: Harrison Smith is BACK for Year 15, the Vikings roster churned 24 hours after setting the 53, and Aaron Jones vs. Jordan Mason remains unsettled — here’s everything you missed on Two Old Bloggers. The Minnesota Vikings barely let the ink dry on their initial 53-man roster before tearing it apart. Within 24 hours, they […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - DECEMBER 14: Harrison Smith #22 of the Minnesota Vikings looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on December 14, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Harrison Smith is BACK for Year 15 , the Vikings roster churned 24 hours after setting the 53, and Aaron Jones vs. Jordan Mason remains unsettled — here’s everything you missed on Two Old Bloggers . The Minnesota Vikings barely let the ink dry on their initial 53-man roster before tearing it apart. Within 24 hours, they added offensive linemen Trevor Keegan and Nick Samac, cut Max Brosmer and Dillon Bell (re-signing both to the practice squad), and then delivered the biggest surprise of the weekend: Harrison “Hitman” Smith returning on a one-year deal worth $12.25 million, escalating to $16.25 million with playoff incentives. As Darren Campbell put it: “Bringing back Harrison Smith bolsters that depth.” With Jamal Adams lost for the year, Theo Jackson battling a leg injury, and both Jakobe and Jacob Thomas nicked up, the safety room was paper-thin. Smith, now 37, remains the NFL’s active interceptions leader and is the only player in the secondary besides Josh Metellus who can audible out of coverages late in the play clock. The Vikings also signed 35-year-old edge rusher Kyle Van Noy to the practice squad — a move both hosts endorsed but questioned in its timing. “They got to add a veteran with some track record,” Darren argued, noting that Jadeveon Clowney, Von Miller, and other targets had already signed elsewhere while Minnesota waited. On the running back battle, the unofficial depth chart lists Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason as co-starters, but Darren made the case that Jones will open as 1A: “The receiving abilities and pass blocking — those are two things that Aaron Jones really has Kevin O’Connell and Wes Phillips’ trust.” Mason out-rushed Jones by 210 yards last season but caught just 14 passes. The show also covered J.J. McCarthy’s uncertain future — “his story isn’t written yet,” per Nolan Teasley — the new GM’s refreshingly blunt press conference style, and ESPN’s Top 100 snubbing Andrew Van Ginkel and Brian O’Neill. “If Brian O’Neill was on the Dallas Cowboys, he’d be All-Pro every year,” Darren quipped. Key Points: Harrison Smith returns on a 1-year, $12.25M deal (up to $16.25M with playoffs); Mike Garafolo confirmed he’s playing Week 1 Vikings added OL Trevor Keegan and Nick Samac off waivers; Max Brosmer and Dillon Bell cleared and re-signed to the practice squad Kyle Van Noy signed to the practice squad for edge depth; Flores familiarity a plus, but 2025 PFF grades (63.0 overall, 51.8 pass rush) raise concerns Aaron Jones likely opens as RB1A over Jordan Mason due to superior pass catching and pass blocking; new wide-zone blocking scheme under Keith Carter and Frank Smith J.J. McCarthy could be QB3; his future depends on his development, Kyler Murray’s performance, and trade interest New GM Nolan Teasley is direct and concise — a sharp contrast to Kwesi Adofo-Mensah’s word salad ESPN Top 100 included only Justin Jefferson (10th); Andrew Van Ginkel and Brian O’Neill both snubbed Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: Football is back, and the Vikings face the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium to open the season. Two Old Bloggers moves to Saturdays starting next week — so if you want deep-dive Vikings analysis with the numbers, the visuals, and the passion, make sure you’re subscribed. Fan With Us! We have your Minnesota Vikings talk amongst the Two Old Bloggers , Darren @KickassblogVike and Dave @Luft_Krigare . Join the conversation! Fan with us at Vikings 1st & SKOL @Vikings1stSKOL and the at the @BleavNetwork . Question for you: If you were Kevin O’Connell, would you start Aaron Jones or Jordan Mason against the Packers — and how would you split the snaps?

title: 2026 NFL Week 1: Green Bay Packers at Minnesota Vikings
summary: Ladies and gentlemen, we have officially made it to the start of the 2026 NFL season, and it’s going to get off to quite a start for our Minnesota Vikings as they play host to their biggest rivals. The Vikings will welcome the Green Bay Packers to U.S. Bank Stadium to kick off the regular […]
full_text: Ladies and gentlemen, we have officially made it to the start of the 2026 NFL season, and it’s going to get off to quite a start for our Minnesota Vikings as they play host to their biggest rivals. The Vikings will welcome the Green Bay Packers to U.S. Bank Stadium to kick off the regular season, and it will be featured across the country on CBS in the late window on Sunday afternoon. These two teams split their series last season. The Packers thumped the Vikings in Week 12 at Lambeau Field by a score of 23-6 as Micah Parsons single-handedly shredded the Minnesota offensive line, while the Vikings won the regular season finale at U.S. Bank Stadium, 16-3, as the Packers rested a bunch of their players as they had nothing to play for going into the postseason. Green Bay will come into this one without a couple of pretty significant pieces. Parsons, who tore an ACL late last season, is on the Physically Unable to Perform List for the Packers and will miss at least the first four games of this season, while running back Josh Jacobs is on the Commissioner’s Exempt List, fallout from a domestic violence incident from this offseason. The Vikings, once again, have another new face at quarterback to start the season, as Kyler Murray will take over as the starter for Kevin O’Connell’s team. He played just one drive in the preseason, but has apparently gotten very solid reviews in practice this offseason. We’ll see how well that transfers over to the field when things get real. The Vikings’ defense, which finished last season on a serious roll, will look to bring that momentum into this season. If the offense can back them up at a higher level than they did last season, this could be a big year in Minnesota. Kickoff for this one is scheduled for 3:25 PM Central time, with coverage being provided by CBS, which is WCCO-4 in the Twin Cities area. We will have all of our stories for this week’s game in this stream for you to access all in one place, so keep it right here for all of the latest news on this week’s contest. title: Vikings 2026 Season Forecast
summary: It’s time for my annual Vikings season forecast. And like my forecasts for the rest of the NFC North teams, I will be looking at roster/coaching changes this offseason, injuries and luck factors from last season, and the change in strength of schedule from last season to this season to guide my forecast. One thing […]
full_text: It’s time for my annual Vikings season forecast. And like my forecasts for the rest of the NFC North teams, I will be looking at roster/coaching changes this offseason, injuries and luck factors from last season, and the change in strength of schedule from last season to this season to guide my forecast. One thing you never find attached to any pundit’s predictions is their track record, except this one. Predicting outcomes of football games and seasons is far from an exact science, but there are some key factors that can and do impact a team’s season, some of which are not immediately obvious. Nevertheless, there are so many interrelated variables involved that perfection is impossible. My own track record is far from perfect, but since I started using my current formula I’ve at least been closer than the over/under total two of the last three seasons- 2023 being way off due to Kirk Cousins going down mid-season. In any case, this will be my tenth prediction over the past eleven seasons, having abandoned any prediction in 2016 after Teddy Bridgewater went down just prior to the start of the season. Here are the results: 2015 : Prediction: 10-6. Actual: 11-5. Preseason over/under: 7.5 2016 : No prediction after Bridgewater went down. Acutal: 8-8. Preseason over/under: 9.5 (pre-Bridgewater injury). 2017 : Prediction: 12-4. Actual: 13-3. Preseason over/under: 8.5 2018 : Prediction: 13-3. Actual: 8-7-1. Preseason over/under: 10 2019 : Prediction: 11-5. Actual: 10-6. Preseason over/under: 9. 2020 : Prediction: 11-5. Actual: 7-9. Preseason over/under: 8.5 (March) 2021 : Prediction: 13-4. Actual: 8-9. Preseason over/under: 9. 2022 : Prediction: 12-5. Actual: 13-4. Preseason over/under: 9.5. 2023 : Prediction: 11-6. Actual: 7-10. Preseason over/under: 8.5. 2024 : Prediction: 10-7. Actual: 14-3. Preseason over/under: 6.5. 2025 : Prediction: 11-6. Actual: 9-8. Preseason over/under: 9. The most difficult aspect of predicting the Vikings season record the past few years has been the lack of continuity at the quarterback position. In 2023, Kirk Cousins went down mid-season, leading to a trio of backups – one of which wasn’t on the roster at the beginning of the season- trying to manage the rest of the way. 2024 saw the reclamation of Sam Darnold, who I was optimistic about compared to most but not optimistic enough as it turned out. And last year I was too optimistic about J.J. McCarthy’s ability to have a Sam Darnold-like season, based on a piece I did in April 2025 that compiled the average stats of first-round quarterbacks landing in ‘good’ situations in their first full season as a starter. Of the 27 quarterbacks I measured in that piece, only Mark Sanchez had a slightly worse season than McCarthy did last year in terms of passer rating and ANY/A and it’s fair to say that Sanchez did not have the offensive weapons that McCarthy had (he did have the top defense). Given McCarthy’s relative performance compared to his backups last season, it didn’t really matter that he missed seven games and departed a couple others early due to injury. Minnesota Vikings Last Season and Offseason Changes The Vikings finished 9-8, including 4-2 in the division last season which resulted in a third-place finish. They managed to win nine games despite the second-worst quarterbacking in the league (above only the Browns) and the most giveaways in the league (30), based on a roughly top five defense and only two missed field goals all season. At one point the Vikings were 4-8 but took advantage of a soft remaining schedule to win their last five games. They have continuity this season in coaching with Kevin O’Connell, Wes Phillips, Matt Daniels, and Brian Flores all returning as head coach and coordinators. Brian Flores was extended and is now believed to be the highest paid coordinator in league history. It is noteworthy that the Vikings added Frank Smith as assistant head coach who is the de facto run game coordinator. In terms of baseline scheme, the Vikings will remain primarily an outside zone running team, but Frank Smith, who served as offensive coordinator under Mike McDaniel in Miami the past few years, along with Keith Carter as offensive line coach, will bring some innovation and greater attention to detail that the Vikings’ run game has been missing. The Vikings didn’t show much of their new run game in the preseason, but there has been a lot of buzz about it in training camp. We’ll see if it was warranted. Kyler Murray The big offseason addition was quarterback Kyler Murray, who the Vikings are hoping will raise their quarterback play from the bottom of the league to at least league average, if not higher. Unlike Sam Darnold, the Vikings previous quarterback reclamation project, Murray comes to the Vikings with roughly league average, rather than considerably worse, performance metrics. Both Murray and Darnold had mediocre teams around them in their pre-Vikings careers as starters. It’s worth noting that Murray has been an above league-average quarterback over his pro career with the Cardinals, which if he was able to maintain that this season would be a major improvement over the Vikings’ 2025 quarterback performance. Murray’s QBR rankings ( an adjusted EPA-based metric ) each season since being drafted #1 overall in 2019: 2019: 14th (57.7) 2020: 14th (61.9) 2021: 7th (63.2) 2022: 18th (53.6) 2023: 22nd (48.0) 2024: 9th (63.4) 2025: 23rd (47.2) (over 5 games) By contrast, the Vikings QBR last season- weighted average of McCarthy (35.6), Wentz (43.3), and Brosmer (14.3)- was 35.4. The way QBR is formulated, a league-average quarterback is meant to have a 50 QBR. This metric also represents the percentage chance the quarterback’s team would be expected to win, all other factors being equal, given the quarterback’s performance. Over Murray’s career, he has a season average QBR of 58.0. By contrast, Sam Darnold’s season average QBR prior to joining the Vikings was 42.9. Darnold had a 57.3 QBR in his season with the Vikings. Outside of Murray’s ACL injury shortened years of 2022-2023- also years the Cardinals defense ranked 31st in points allowed- and last season when he only played in five games (and had a 29th ranked defense), Murray has been an above average starting quarterback in QBR ranking and cracked the top ten in the two most recent seasons. And he did so in two significantly different schemes. When Murray has had an above average defense in points allowed (15th in 2024, 11th in 2021, 12th in 2020) his QBR has been in the low 60s. That’s not an unreasonable baseline expectation this season, given the team around him and Murray’s QBR history. Offensively, outside of quarterback, the Vikings replaced WR3 Jalen Nailor with Jauan Jennings, who isn’t the athletic downfield threat Nailor was but may fit better with the Vikings scheme this year as a big, tough, contested catch, move-the-chains type receiver who can also block. Blake Brandel, who started 7 games last year at center, and took snaps there in a few others, takes over as the starter this season from the retired Ryan Kelly. The Vikings also replaced the retired C.J. Ham with Max Bredeson at fullback. They also added Demond Claiborne as RB3. Overall these are minor roster changes compared to last year’s roster. Defensively, the Vikings traded edge rusher Jonathan Greenard to the Eagles, promoting Dallas Turner to the starting job and recently acquired Kyle Van Noy to provide experienced and capable depth. The Vikings also moved on from Javon Hargrave and Jonathan Allen at defensive tackle, promoting Levi Drake-Rodriquez and Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins while drafting Caleb Banks in the first round and Domonique Orange in the third round. Elijah Williams will also rotate at defensive tackle this season and looked good in preseason and joint practices. The Vikings also drafted linebacker Jake Golday in the second round. In the defensive secondary, the Vikings will likely have the same starting lineup with the return…

title: SB Nation Reacts Results: Vikings Fans Fairly Satisfied With Offseason Overall
summary: Just seven days from now, the 2026 NFL season will officially begin for our Minnesota Vikings, as they will host the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium. That means the offseason is officially over, and we asked you as part of our SB Nation Reacts survey for this week exactly what you thought about […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: A Minnesota Vikings fans cheers during an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images Just seven days from now, the 2026 NFL season will officially begin for our Minnesota Vikings, as they will host the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium. That means the offseason is officially over, and we asked you as part of our SB Nation Reacts survey for this week exactly what you thought about it. We have those results, and for the most part it appears that folks were relatively happy with how things went. Of those who took the time to respond to our survey, 45% gave the offseason a “B” grade, which is pretty good. Combine that with the 7% that graded it as an “A,” and over half of our respondents think that the purple had a better-than-average offseason overall. Another 34% thought that the moves the team made merited a “C” grade, which is an average mark. So, the overwhelming majority of you seem to think that the offseason in Minnesota wasn’t anything approaching a disaster or anything like that. Still, a few of the people who responded were more on the “gloom and doom” end of the spectrum. There were 11% of the people who responded to the poll that gave the Vikings a “D” for their offseason moves, while the remaining 3% went as negative as possible and slapped a big ol’ “F” on what the Vikings have done since the 2025 season came to an end. That seems a little harsh, but everyone is free to have their own perspective on things. Frankly, I think a “B” is just about right. I think the Vikings addressed a lot of the things they needed to address. Hopefully the quarterback issue is solved, and if it is this team has a lot of potential to do some damage in 2026. The defense should continue to be a menace as long as there aren’t too many injuries. Will it be enough to make a run in what should still be the most competitive division in the NFL? We’ll have to see. As always, we’d like to thank everyone who took the time to participate in this week’s survey. Be sure to keep your eyes open for the next one! title: Patriots preparing to go soundless in Seattle to start the new season
summary: Seattle’s Lumen Field is one of the loudest stadiums in pro football already, but the 12s might take it up a notch come Wednesday night. Not only will their team open the 2026 NFL season at home, it also will unveil its Super Bowl banner earned in February. That banner, of course, was earned at […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - DECEMBER 28: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots under center during the game against the New York Jets on December 28, 2025 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Seattle’s Lumen Field is one of the loudest stadiums in pro football already, but the 12s might take it up a notch come Wednesday night. Not only will their team open the 2026 NFL season at home, it also will unveil its Super Bowl banner earned in February. That banner, of course, was earned at the detriment of the New England Patriots. And those very same Patriots will have a front-row seat to the Seahawks’ celebration, which also means they get an opportunity to play spoilers. In order to do so, however, overcoming a tough environment will be crucial. And in order to do so and get a more satisfying result especially on the offensive side of the ball, New England will be relying on a silent snap count extensively. For Drake Maye and company, one of the secrets to success is being soundless in Seattle. “There’s advantages and disadvantages to working in the silent, and I think it’s mostly just us repping it,” said Maye. “Coach [Mike] Vrabel and the offensive staff do a great job of preparing us, and I think we got a lot of work at it, and those guys got a good grip on it. So, we got to stay out of penalties, avoid penalties and keep the positive plays going, and I think when we are ahead of the chains, we tend to do better for ourselves.” “I just think it’s the communication and getting guys on the same page,” said Maye’s position coach, Patriots QB coach Ashton Grant. “A lot of what we do is verbal communicating, so when you go into a loud environment where you can’t use your voices, I think just trying to get everyone on the same page when we’re trying to snap the ball and what other communication we’re trying to get done, I think it becomes important.” Now in his third year, Maye is no stranger to using a silent count in a game. The same is true for the experienced offensive line and skill group surrounding him. And yet, at first glance there appears to be an element of uncertainty. With verbal communication not an option, the operation suddenly relies on every player being on the same page timing-wise. As offensive line coach Doug Marrone explained, however, the core elements at play still remain the same. It’s all about focus and responsibility, as would be the case using a normal pre-snap cadence. “I’ve always tried to train myself when I was a player to just be like, ‘Okay, here’s my job. Here’s my responsibility. Okay, here we go. The number one thing I have to do right now is just focus on this on this snap count,’” Marrone explained. “And it doesn’t change really. This is where people may really understand: it’s the same way when we’re doing it with the cadence. It’s that same type of focus that you need. … “For me as a player when I did it, it was a matter of just managing that you know, ‘Here it comes.’ It’s different in college because the best player you played in college, you’re playing every week, and it’s at every position. So, you’re kind of just making sure, like, ‘Look, I’m not going to try to cheat this thing. I’m not going to get it. We’re going to get off at the same time and we’re going to be okay.’” At the end of the day, much of the responsibility for the timing being correct falls on the quarterback and center. In New England’s case, that means relying on a new pairing: while Maye is still calling the shots from the QB position, Jared Wilson is now handling the snaps in place of veteran Garrett Bradbury. While Wednesday’s game will be Wilson’s first as the Patriots’ starting center, offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels is not worried about the offensive operation not being on point. “The quarterback and the center, if they’re not on the same page, [the rest of the offense] doesn’t really matter,” McDaniels said. “So, whatever we talk about with Drake, you kind of also are talking about Jared. They distribute a lot of information to their teammates and they do a really good job of it.”

title: Patriots vs. Seahawks preview for NFL Week 1
summary: The New England Patriots’ 2025 season as a whole was a success, but it ultimately ended in a disappointing loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the Super Bowl. Seven months removed from its 29-13 defeat, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel will get another crack at the newly-crowned world champions: it’s Patriots at Seahawks […]
full_text: SAN JOSE, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 04: A Seattle Seahawks helmet is seen during a practice ahead of Super Bowl LX at San Jose State University on February 04, 2026 in San Jose, California. (Photo by Eakin Howard/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots’ 2025 season as a whole was a success, but it ultimately ended in a disappointing loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the Super Bowl. Seven months removed from its 29-13 defeat, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel will get another crack at the newly-crowned world champions: it’s Patriots at Seahawks to kick off the NFL’s 2026 season. The two teams will face off at Seattle’s Lumen Field on Wednesday night, a highly-anticipated rematch that will feature a new-look Patriots team going up against a steady Seahawks squad that saw only marginal changes during the offseason. The question is whether or not New England managed to close what was a 16-point gap on Super Bowl Sunday. We will find out on Wednesday. For now, let’s get to know the Seahawks in our first opponent preview of the season. Seahawks key stats The Seahawks were the best team in the NFL last season, and their stats reflected this. And given that the personnel turnover has been minimal — more on it in a second — it would not be a surprise to see them post similar numbers in 2026 as well. Given that those numbers are the only serious statistical information we have about the team, if we disregard its 0-2-1 preseason slate, let’s take a look at them. Record: 14-3 (1st NFC West/1st NFC) Scoring differential: +191 (1st) Turnover differential: -3 (t-19th) Offense: 28.4 points/game (3rd), 351.4 yards/game (8th), 28 giveaways (31st), 0.036 EPA/play (14th), 0.137 EPA/dropback (8th), -0.076 EPA/run (22nd) Defense: 17.2 points/game (1st), 285.9 yards/game (6th), 25 takeaways (6th), -0.113 EPA/play (1st), -0.065 EPA/dropback (5th), -0.206 EPA/run (1st) Even though it was ranked only 14th in the NFL in expected points added and turned the ball over more than every team but one during the 2025 regular season, the Seahawks offense was quite successful as a whole. That was particularly true in the passing game, where the team finished second in net yards per attempt (7.6) — a ranking mirrored by the defense (5.1). The points and yards per game rankings were impressive as well, but do not quite hold up when looked at on a drive-by-drive basis: Seattle was ranked 11th in both categories on a per-series average. Defensively, there was no such drop-off between the raw data and the efficiency metrics. Seattle finished the regular season first in points allowed per game (17.2) and first in points allowed per drive (1.48), sixth in yards per game (285.9) and fourth in yards per drive (25.8), and top-10 in virtually all major categories including scoring percentage (28.7%; 2nd) and turnover rate (12.8%; 6th). The run defense was particularly stout, but teams did not have any easier of a time moving the ball through the air. Long story short, this was as complete a defense as any in the NFL — and the Patriots found this out first-hand in the Super Bowl. Seahawks 2025 season In this section, we typically look back at the games already played this season. With this being opening week, however, there are no such points of reference. Instead, let’s recap Seattle’s championship campaign from a year ago. Week 1: 17-13 loss vs. San Francisco 49ers (0-1) Week 2: 31-17 win at Pittsburgh Steelers (1-1) Week 3: 44-13 win vs. New Orleans Saints (2-1) Week 4: 23-20 win at Arizona Cardinals (3-1) Week 5: 38-35 loss vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-2) Week 6: 20-12 win at Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) Week 7: 27-19 win vs. Houston Texans (5-2) Week 8: Bye Week 9: 38-14 win at Washington Commanders (6-2) Week 10: 44-22 win vs. Arizona Cardinals (7-2) Week 11: 21-19 loss at Los Angeles Rams (7-3) Week 12: 30-24 win at Tennessee Titans (8-3) Week 13: 26-0 win vs. Minnesota Vikings (9-3) Week 14: 37-9 win at Atlanta Falcons (10-3) Week 15: 18-16 win vs. Indianapolis Colts (11-3) Week 16: 38-37 (OT) win vs. Los Angeles Rams (12-3) Week 17: 27-10 win vs. Carolina Panthers (13-3) Week 18: 13-3 win at San Francisco 49ers (14-3) Wild card round: Bye Divisional round: 41-6 win vs. San Francisco 49ers NFC Championship Game: 31-27 win vs. Los Angeles Rams Super Bowl: 29-13 win vs. New England Patriots All things considered, the Seahawks were deserving world champions last season. They were arguably the strongest team already in the regular season, posting a league-best scoring differential of +191, before going on a dominant postseason run. Barner* (88), Eric Saubert (81), Elijah Arroyo (18), Nick Kallerup (89) Offensive tackle (3): Charles Cross* (67 | LT), Abraham Lucas* (72 | RT), Josh Jones (74) Interior offensive line (6): Grey Zabel* (76 | LG), Jalen Sundell* (61 | C), Anthony Bradford* (75 | RG), Olusegun Oluwatimi (55), Beau Stephens (70), Christian Haynes (64), Bryce Cabeldue (77) Interior defensive line (6): Leonard Williams* (99), Byron Murphy II* (91), Jarran Reed (90), Brandon Pili (95), Mike Morris (94), Rylie Mills (98) Defensive edge (5): DeMarcus Lawrence* (0), Uchenna Nwosu* (7), Derrick Hall (58), Dante. Fowler Jr. (56), Connor O’Toole (57) Linebacker (5): Ernest Jones IV* (13), Drake Thomas* (42), Tyrice Knight (48), Patrick O’Connell (52), Chazz Surratt (44) Cornerback (4): Devon Witherspoon* (21), Josh Jobe* (29), Nehemiah Pritchett (28), Julian Neal (1) Safety (4): Nick Emmanwori* (3), Julian Love* (20), Ty Okada* (39), Avery Smith (27) Specialists (3): Jason Myers (5 | K), Michael Dickson (4 | P/H), Chris Stoll (41 | LS) Long gone are the days when Sam Darnold was the latest in a long list of quarterbacks failing to live up to the expectation of being a highly-drafted quarterback with the New York Jets. The journey to Seattle was not an easy one to travel for the third overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft, but he made it count and is coming off the best season of his career: Darnold was the motor powering one of the league’s top offenses in 2025, and there is no reason to believe in a serious drop-off even under a new offensive coordinator. Of course, it helps when you have one of the best wide receiver trios in football to throw to. The first player to mention is, of course, JSN. The reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year, Jaxon Smith-Njigba finished the 2025 regular season with 119 catches for a league-leading 1,793 yards and 10 touchdowns. Darnold’s go-to guy and big-play threat all rolled into one, he added 17 passes for 199 yards and a pair of scores in the playoffs. In 20 total games last season, the first-team All-Pro cracked 100 receiving yards 10 times. One prominent departure from last year, meanwhile, is running back Kenneth Walker. The MVP of Super Bowl LX signed with the Chiefs this offseason, and was replaced by Jadarian Price in the first round of the draft. Price will be running behind a high-quality offensive line that retained all five starters this offseason. On the other side of the ball, the Seahawks are featuring one of the most disruptive defensive lines in football. Led by a starting quartet of edge rushers DeMarcus Lawrence and Uchenna Nwosu as well as interior linemen Leonard Williams and Byron Murphy, blocking Seattle’s front line again projects to be a handful for opposing offenses. The Patriots, of course, were unable to limit the group’s impact in the Super Bowl. The hope is that some reshuffling as well as some natural growth from youngsters Will Campbell and Jared Wilson will make for a more competitive battle this time…

title: Examining the roster ties between Patriots, Seahawks ahead of Week 1
summary: Familiarity from February remains heading into the first game of September. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, four players in the fold for the 2026 season opener have been both New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks during their NFL journeys. Here’s a glance through those connections ahead of Wednesday’s 8:20 p.m. ET […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Dre'Mont Jones #5 of the New England Patriots reacts against the Philadelphia Eagles during an NFL preseason football game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Familiarity from February remains heading into the first game of September. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, four players in the fold for the 2026 season opener have been both New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks during their NFL journeys. Here’s a glance through those connections ahead of Wednesday’s 8:20 p.m. ET Super Bowl LX rematch at Lumen Field. SEATTLE Eric Saubert, tight end — Saubert has been a member of 11 organizations since becoming Drake University’s first NFL draft choice in 34 years. The No. 174 overall selection in the 2017 class spent his initial campaigns with the Atlanta Falcons before being acquired at Gillette Stadium in exchange for a conditional pick back in 2019. The stint started and finished that August at the league’s 53-man roster deadline. But the 32-year-old blocking tight end has found a home with the Super Bowl LX champions on the heels of myriad transactions. Saubert signed a one-year deal with Seattle in 2025 and had earned a one-year extension after activated from injured reserve last December. A veteran of 112 games in the regular season, including 24 starts, he has caught 51 passes for 420 yards and three touchdowns. An additional two starts came during the Seahawks’ latest playoff run. NEW ENGLAND Ben Brown, guard — The Patriots released Brown as the NFL deadline dust settled last week. The vested veteran, who signed a contract extension in December, quickly returned to the 53-man roster after the procedural move. Brown’s NFL career got underway as an undrafted free agent with the Cincinnati Bengals in 2022. A torn biceps in his preseason debut resulted in him spending all of his rookie season on injured reserve. Waived the following August, the Ole Miss product signed to the Seattle practice squad. From there, Brown was promoted to the active roster that September, waived and re-signed to the practice squad that October, then let go that November. Stints with the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders followed before he was signed off the latter’s practice squad and started at center in Foxborough the same week in the fall off 2024. The 28-year-old interior lineman has gone on to appear in 27 games for New England, starting 14 between center and guard while totaling 998 snaps on offense and 124 snaps on special teams. Greg Van Roten, guard — A veteran of 144 NFL games toured Foxborough in August. And as injuries mounted along the offensive line in the preseason, that visit that gave way to a contract. The 36-year-old Van Roten had been unsigned since opening of the new league year. He now resides on the reigning AFC champions’ 53-man roster. Standing 105 starts into his run, the 2012 undrafted free agent out of Penn has also been a member of the Green Bay Packers, Jacksonville Jaguars, New York Jets and Buffalo Bills. And in 2014, Van Roten spent six months in Seattle before being released at the 53-man roster deadline and moving into the CFL ranks with the Toronto Argonauts. Between guard and center, the veteran has amassed 105 starts and finished past two campaigns having logged 100 percent of the offensive snaps. Dre’Mont Jones, outside linebacker — The Patriots reached a three-year deal with Jones as the official start of NFL free agency loomed in March. The 29-year-old edge rusher and convert from defensive tackle checks in as a veteran of 108 games and 69 starts. Entering the league out of Ohio State in the third round of the 2019 draft at No. 71 overall, Jones has since racked up 253 tackles, 37.5 sacks, three forced fumbles, three fumble recoveries and one interception. He spent 2025 between the Tennessee Titans and Baltimore Ravens by way of trade. Prior to then, Jones saw action in every game across a pair of campaigns with Seattle before being released entering the final leg of a three-year contract. His Seahawks stay featured 23 starts, 8.5 sacks as well as a safety.
