title: Josh McDaniels owns Super Bowl struggles ahead of Seahawks rematch
summary: New England Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels isn’t running from what went wrong last February, when the Seattle Seahawks dominated his offense in Super Bowl LX. “I didn’t do a good enough job. Point it at me. They ‘out-everythinged’ us in the game,” McDaniels said on Sunday. “We have a lot of things we’ve learned. […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 08: Josh McDaniels of the New England Patriots runs on the field prior to Super Bowl LX against the Seattle Seahawks at Levi's Stadium on February 08, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images New England Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels isn’t running from what went wrong last February, when the Seattle Seahawks dominated his offense in Super Bowl LX. “I didn’t do a good enough job. Point it at me. They ‘out-everythinged’ us in the game,” McDaniels said on Sunday. “We have a lot of things we’ve learned. But I think this will be a different game, I think it will be a new game. It’s a new year. We have some different players. They have a few guys that are new. We’ll see how different it is. They certainly found some opportunities last year, and hopefully we’ve done a good job trying to limit those Wednesday night.” After being one of the best offenses in football during the regular season, the Patriots’ unit struggled down the stretch against some of the league’s best defenses. That ended with a 29-13 loss in the Super Bowl to the Seahawks, when Drake Maye was sacked six times. New England’s offense was gashed by Seattle’s pressure packages while rookies Will Campbell and Jared Wilson struggled on the left side of the offensive line. Ahead of the rematch to open the 2026 NFL season, McDaniels is excited to see the growth from Campbell, Wilson — who is back at his natural center position — and the rest of his second-year players. Campbell, specifically, struggled in the Super Bowl while playing through a sprained right MCL. Now healthy, McDaniels has enjoyed the approach from his starting left tackle to start the year. “He’s had a really good mindset all year. Locked in,” McDaniels said of Campbell. “He had a good spring, good [training] camp — trying to work on the things he knows at his position are important and critical to his improvement.” New England’s new-look offensive line, which also features free agent addition Alijah Vera-Tucker, will be tested again Wednesday night. The Seahawks front returns the majority of its unit, while McDaniels noted the challenges that head coach Mike Macdonald’s defensive scheme presents. Still, the Patriots offensive coordinator feels confident in their offensive game plan and said the players have a good week of preparation. He also has quarterback Drake Maye in a better spot after spending their second full offseason together. “Drake just knows a lot more than he did last year in general at this time. And he’s learned a lot of valuable lessons I think over time,” McDaniels said. “He’s also had a great mindset and approach this spring and summer about the things that he can do better and he’s worked really hard. Nobody’s worked harder. “I know he’s eager to get out there and actually play a game and see how far we’ve come.”

title: Patriots kicker returning to football roots with jersey number change
summary: Worn by leading wide receiver Stefon Diggs, the No. 8. jersey was a big part of the New England Patriots’ 2025 campaign. With less than a week before the 2026 season opener, however, it remained vacant. For Andy Borregales, that was all the opportunity he needed. The second-year kicker, who had started his NFL career […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 02: Stefon Diggs #8 of the New England Patriots and Andy Borregales #36 of the New England Patriots warm up against the Atlanta Falcons before the game at Gillette Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images Worn by leading wide receiver Stefon Diggs, the No. 8. jersey was a big part of the New England Patriots’ 2025 campaign. With less than a week before the 2026 season opener, however, it remained vacant. For Andy Borregales, that was all the opportunity he needed. The second-year kicker, who had started his NFL career wearing No. 36, recently adopted the number in what is a return to his personal football roots. “It was the first number I ever wore when I started playing football at five years old,” Borregales told reporters in the Patriots locker room on Sunday. “I kind of waited until the end; if anyone was going to get it, go get it. I saw that it was still available, so I was like, ‘I might as well just try to get it,’ and here we are.” Borregales recalled wearing the No. 8 jersey all the way up until middle school. When his older brother José left for high school, however, he decided to pick up his old No. 30 jersey. From that point on, he found himself kicking in the 30s rather than the single digits. That remained the case throughout his stint at the University of Miami, where he again followed in his brother’s footsteps, and into the NFL. Wearing No. 36, Borregales made 31 of 38 field goal tries as well as 60 of 62 extra points as a sixth-round rookie. Like his predecessor in the No. 8, he therefore had an active hand in the Patriots’ fortunes last season. But unlike Stefon Diggs, Borregales is still around: whereas the veteran wideout was cut in March and has since joined the Washington Commanders, the 23-year-old place kicker is locked into his position on New England’s current roster trying to be a worthy wearer of his new digit. “I had a great relationship with him,” Borregales said of Diggs. “I hope he’s doing good in Washington, and I do believe he’s going to be doing good. He was a great guy. He was a good locker room guy.” Borregales is entering his second season in Foxborough off a generally solid summer, albeit one that saw him miss three kicks in the preseason opener against the Colts. He was perfect in the two exhibition games since, but that single performance nonetheless raised questions about his readiness. For his coordinator, Jeremy Springer, there is nothing to be concerned about. “Oh, he’s ready to go. I don’t have any doubts in Andy not being ready to go,” Springer said. “He’s a very mature athlete as a kicker and he prepares that way. He never gets too high or too low. I’ve seen that a million times here, whether it’s a good game, bad game, good practice, bad practice, he learns from it, he studies it and he comes back better the next day.” Borregales will be asked to do so again this season. The only difference is that it will be in a new number that very much is an old one for him.

title: Sunday Patriots Notes: Tough love shaped A.J. Brown’s leadership
summary: Almost seven full months removed from the Super Bowl, the New England Patriots are finally preparing for a meaningful game again. On Wednesday night, they will participate in the 2026 regular season opener against the very same Seattle Seahawks who beat for the Vince Lombardi Trophy in January. Naturally, all of our attention this coming […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: A.J. Brown #1 of the New England Patriots looks on after the preseason game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images Almost seven full months removed from the Super Bowl, the New England Patriots are finally preparing for a meaningful game again. On Wednesday night, they will participate in the 2026 regular season opener against the very same Seattle Seahawks who beat for the Vince Lombardi Trophy in January. Naturally, all of our attention this coming week will be on that game. For now, however, let’s clean out our notebook from the week that was. Welcome to the final offseason addition of our Sunday Patriots Notes . Tough love shaped A.J. Brown’s leadership Even though he is not among the six players voted captains for 2026, wide receiver A.J. Brown nonetheless will hold a leadership role within the team this season. He is, after all, among the Patriots’ most experienced players and somebody who has had a long relationship with head coach Mike Vrabel. That relationship has helped shape Brown’s leadership style and maturation process since he entered the league as a second-round draft pick in 2019. “Early on, he was just so tough on me, and I didn’t really understand it as a young player,” said Brown about the mentoring he received from Vrabel while both were with the Tennessee Titans. “Now, I know the expectation that I have for myself and the expectation that he has for me. It comes from a good place.” Having been on the receiving end of Vrabel’s tough love to start his NFL career, Brown knows what to expect. He consequently uses his own experience to help his younger teammates in New England. One of those is outside linebacker Gabe Jacas. “Vrabes was on him really tough,” said Brown. “I’ll be sitting in my chair laughing just to see that process, witness it all over again. I went and had a couple words with Gabe to keep him locked in. I hope that my words help.” Brown’s leadership did not develop overnight but rather bit by bit over his first seven years as a pro. Vrabel was part of three of those before the wideout was shipped from Tennessee to Philadelphia in a 2022 draft-day trade. But while the two men kept in contact even while apart, it took their reunion earlier this offseason for Vrabel to get another up-close look at Brown’s development as not just a football player but off the field as well. What he saw left him impressed. “The maturity has been probably what I have appreciated seeing on a daily basis,” he said. “We had A.J. as a young player, continued that relationship personally, and I could sense that he was growing and making strides in that regard. But having him here, seeing him each and every day, the way that he communicates and where he’s at in the training room, just seeing his daily routine and the way that he talks to the young receivers or the way that he communicates with Todd [Downing], Josh [McDaniels] or the quarterback, I would say that that’s probably a little different than the day-to-day person I saw as a young player.” For Brown himself, it’s all part of the job — one that will look different in 2026, after his trade from the Eagles to the team he has been rooting for since his childhood. “I’m super excited,” he said on Saturday. “I literally looked at the sign today, saying, ‘I’m a Patriot.’ I’m still in awe. I’m grateful. I’m excited.” Captains not the only team leaders While Brown was not voted a captain by his peers, six of his teammates were: quarterback Drake Maye, tight end Hunter Henry, offensive tackle Morgan Moses, linebacker Robert Spillane, cornerback Marcus Jones and safety Kevin Byard. They will lead the team, but as Mike Vrabel explained, are not the only ones with leadership responsibilities. “Those guys have, since I have been here, the five that were here last year were great leaders, very consistent players, very consistent demeanor in their preparation and the type of teammates that they were,” said Vrabel. “We added Kevin this year, so I am always appreciative of those guys that lead. We will have a leadership group as well that will assist them, and again, we will meet. But, it is not like we have to have a standard meeting for them to approach me and talk about something.” Meanwhile, elsewhere in the league, two ex-Patriots were voted captains with their respective teams. Long snapper Joe Cardona is a captain with the Rams, while kicker Nick Folk is one with the Falcons. The expectation is that offensive linemen Joe Thuney and Ted Karras will also receive the honor with the Bears and Bengals, respectively. Patriots need to put their money where their mouth is Without direct inside knowledge, it is hard to assign blame between the Patriots and Christian Gonzalez’s camp for the stalled contract extension negotiations. However, based on what has been reported so far, it seems as if the pact’s structure is an issue that has not yet been resolved. Rumor has it that the team’s publicly-stated desire to make Gonzalez the highest-paid cornerback in football is not just lip service, but that they are less enthusiastic about the guarantees. For a team has twice stated its intentions publicly from the highest ranks — through owner Robert Kraft and de facto general manager Eliot Wolf — that is a disappointing approach. Sure, there is a fiscal element to it the organization needs to consider, but overall the reporting so far has made it sound like the Patriots are doing half-measures rather than committing full-on to a player who has a strong case as the best on the roster. If true, this sends a concerning message to Gonzalez and possibly even the next big name to enter the negotiating table, quarterback Drake Maye. In order not to cause any further issues, the Patriots need to put their money where their mouth is and compensate their home-grown blue-chip cornerback according to his value: at the top of his position in more ways than total value. How the Patriots use their money Gonzalez’s contract extension, if it happens, will change the Patriots’ contractual outlook for the future and possibly the 2026 season as well. If so, the following outlook — courtesy by NFL analyst Sebastian Carl using numbers from Over the Cap — might be changing. For now, however, here is how the Patriots use their money heading into this year’s regular season: One change compared to the last two years is the Patriots having a contract qualify for the “elite” category, defined as a one of the top 32 cap hits in the NFL. The honor belongs to defensive tackle Milton Williams, whose $28.5 million cap figure ranks 23rd in the league this season. The joys of the practice squad While most of the attention during and after cutdown weekend was reserved for the men on the 53-man roster, they are not the only ones happy with the eventual outcome of training camp. For others, including undrafted rookie wide receiver Cameron Dorner, even making the practice squad is a win. “I can’t stop smiling,” Dorner said this week. “I’m happy to be here. It was one of the best moments of my life, all the hard work that I put in. I can’t complain. All the coaches here have been super great to me, pushing me to be the best player I can, also be a better man off the field. It was a it was a pretty cool moment for me.” Flanked by sophomores The Patriots moved some pieces around on the left side of the offensive line, inserting veteran free agency signing Alijah Vera-Tucker at left guard. title: Saints enter 2026 NFL season with second-easiest strength of schedule
summary: The New Orleans Saints are set to enter the 2026 NFL season with one of the easiest schedules. Saints’ opponents for 2026 had a win percentage of .434 in 2025, just .005 better than the Cleveland Browns’ opponents, who had a win percentage of .429. New Orleans finished last in the NFC South in 2025 […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - DECEMBER 28: Head Coach Kellen Moore congratulates Tyler Shough #6 of the New Orleans Saints on the sidelines after a touchdown during a game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Nashville, Tennessee. The Saints defeated the Titans 34-26. (Photo by Wesley Hitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints are set to enter the 2026 NFL season with one of the easiest schedules. Saints’ opponents for 2026 had a win percentage of .434 in 2025, just .005 better than the Cleveland Browns’ opponents, who had a win percentage of .429. Each team's strength of schedule this season 📊 pic.twitter.com/4ozyTPKI8N — NFL (@NFL) September 6, 2026 New Orleans finished last in the NFC South in 2025 with a 6-11 record. With their division placement, the Saints are awarded a 4th-place schedule, matching them up with other 4th-place finishers. The Saints will face the Arizona Cardinals, Las Vegas Raiders, New York Giants, and their Week 1 opponent, the Detroit Lions, thanks to finishing last in the division. Also factoring into their weak strength of schedule is the lack of power in the NFC South. Each of the Saints’ division rivals finished 8-9 in 2025. While the black and gold finished last in 2025, there are expectations that they will place better in 2026 with an improved roster and questions among their rivals. Outside the Carolina Panthers, who finished first in 2025, the entire NFC South has a strength-of-schedule rating under .500. Despite this, Carolina is the favorite to win the division in 2026. The Atlanta Falcons are expected to take a step back, and there are plenty of questions surrounding the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. While New Orleans has the quote-unquote easiest schedule in the NFC South, their schedule isn’t as easy as it seems. The Lions are a better team than they finished last season, and they’ll follow that tough Week 1 matchup with a tough road trip to the Baltimore Ravens. While an easier strength of schedule should result in more wins for the Saints in 2026, it’s still the NFL. Any team can win on any given Sunday, and that’s true for New Orleans, who are projected to enter as underdogs for a majority of their matchups for the upcoming season. The plan should be simple. Go in every week and give it your all, no matter the opponent.

summary: This Sunday, the New Orleans Saints will open the 2026 NFL regular season on the road against the Detroit Lions. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images This Sunday, the New Orleans Saints will open the 2026 NFL regular season on the road against the Detroit Lions. The player to watch finished his rookie season on fire and is looking to carry that momentum into his first season as the clear cut starter: QB Tyler Shough . Shough gave Saints fans every reason to believe they may have found their long-term answer at quarterback. Now, he has to carry that confidence into his second season and avoid the infamous sophomore slump. This Sunday in Detroit, the biggest thing to watch will be how comfortable Shough looks running the offense with a full offseason under his belt. Considering what we’ve seen from Shough this offseason, whether it be his work ethic or him consistently building chemistry with his teammates, New Orleans should expect him to play with more confidence and take advantage of opportunities when they present themselves. A strong performance against the Lions would give Shough and the Saints something to build on immediately. More importantly, it could reinforce the belief that the production he showed toward the end of last season wasn’t a fluke. Shough doesn’t need to be perfect. He needs to look like a guy who is comfortable running the offense while trusting his supporting cast. A guy that has a better understanding of the intricacies of the NFL. If he can start the season playing with the same confidence he showed down the stretch of his rookie year, the Saints could have something special brewing. For Shough, Week 1 isn’t just the beginning of another season. It’s the first chance to show that last year’s momentum was only the beginning.

That follows on the heels of the news that backup quarterback Jameis Winston has also signed an extension that will keep him with the team through the […]
full_text: Jon Runyan Jr. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants have reached a two-year, $22 million contract extension with starting left guard Jon Runyan Jr. , according a report from ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter . That follows on the heels of the news that backup quarterback Jameis Winston has also signed an extension that will keep him with the team through the 2028 season. Runyan’s extension reportedly includes $21.5 million guaranteed, and is a higher average annual value than the three-year, $30 million contract Runyan signed with the Giants in 2024. Runyan receiving an extension like this could be considered a shocking development. The 29-year-old entered the spring in the final year of his contract. Many figured this would be his final season with the Giants, and that he would face a challenge for his starting left guard job. Instead, Runyan took almost every snap in the spring and summer as the first-team left guard. Daniel Faalele, thought to be a Runyan challenger after four years playing for John Harbaugh with the Baltimore Ravens, was traded to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Josh Ezeudu was also traded. Evan Neal was cut. Runyan has a connection to the Harbaugh family. He played four seasons at Michigan for Jim Harbaugh, John’s brother. The Giants now have every starting offensive lineman except center John Michael Schmitz signed beyond this season. They also have two young backup offensive linemen they like in Marcus Mbow and J.C. Davis.

title: NY Giants aim for good start after John Harbaugh’s rigorous summer
summary: The New York Giants’ season-opening game against the Dallas Cowboys next Sunday night might not be a “must-win” game for the Giants. It sure would, though, be a significant one. The Giants have begun seasons 0-2 or worse in 10 of the last 13 years. It seems appropriate that the Giants will begin the John […]
full_text: John Harbaugh | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants’ season-opening game against the Dallas Cowboys next Sunday night might not be a “must-win” game for the Giants. It sure would, though, be a significant one. The Giants have begun seasons 0-2 or worse in 10 of the last 13 years. Season starts since 2013 Tom Coughlin 2013 — 0-6 (7-9 finish) 2014 — 0-2 (6-10 finish) 2015 — 0-2 (6-10 finish) Ben McAdoo 2016 — 2-0 (that extended to 10-4, then an 11-5 finish and a playoff berth) 2017 — 0-5 | 1-8 (3-13 finish | McAdoo, GM Jerry Reese fired with four games remaining and the Giants 2-10) Pat Shurmur 2018 — 1-7 (5-11 finish) 2019 — 0-2 | 2-11 (4-12 finish) Joe Judge 2020 — 0-5 | 1-7 (6-10 finish) 2021 — 1-5 (4-13 finish) Brian Daboll 2022 — 6-1 (9-7-1 finish … wild-card round victory over Minnesota Vikings) 2023 — 1-5 (6-11 finish) 2024 — 1-3 | 2-13 (3-14 finish) 2025 — 0-3 | Daboll fired at 2-8 (4-13 finish) It seems appropriate that the Giants will begin the John Harbaugh era in a nationally-televised game against the Cowboys. The Giants and Cowboys have played seven times in season-opening games since 2012. The Giants are 1-6 in those games, with their only victory coming in 2016. The memory of the 40-0 whitewashing by Dallas in 2023, the last time the teams met in a season-opener, is still fresh for Giants fans. The Giants hired Harbaugh, with 15 winning seasons, 12 playoff appearances, and a Super Bowl title in 18 years with the Baltimore Ravens, in an effort to get an organization that has lost its way since the 2011 Super Bowl victory, back on track. One of the things Harbaugh has to fix is the Giants’ history of burying themselves by the middle of October. Sometimes, by the end of September. The Ravens started the 2025 season 1-5, so Harbaugh is not immune to poor starts. Still, his track record is the antithesis of how the Giants have started seasons. Harbaugh’s Ravens went 12-6 in 18 season-opening games. In home openers under Harbaugh, the Ravens were 15-3. Part of that early-season success has to be that Harbaugh pushes players harder in the spring and summer than most current coaches. Harbaugh uses padded practices as much as the Collective Bargaining Agreement will allow, and generally keeps players on the field as long as the rules say he can. Even jog-throughs in West Virginia lasted 2½ hours. Harbaugh’s methods don’t need validation. His resume speaks for itself. The Giants, though, are long overdue for a change in their fortunes. Veteran cornerback Greg Newsome, who competed against Harbaugh’s team while with the Cleveland Browns, said the coach runs “tough, gritty” practices. “We’re going to work, and I like that,” Newsome said during training camp. “There’s no off days for us in terms of not competing. He’s going to make sure we compete.” Veteran defensive tackle D.J. Reader also lauded Harbaugh’s focus on getting the most out of each day during training camp. “You’ve got to callous the body,” Reader said. “The thing that’s important in football is callousing the body to be ready to take on those blows throughout the season, because you’re going to get chinks in your armor, and if you didn’t build your armor up enough to be able to withstand those hits, those dents, those little scratches you’ll take in your armor, then shame on you. “I think it’s important to be able to callous the body. Do it with intent. Be smart about it, but you have to callous the body to go out there and play this game. You’re not just going to roll out there, roll out of bed, and be able to go out there on Sundays and get it done.” Several times in recent years the Giants have employed the “go easy in the summer, then roll out of bed in Week 1 and go play” approach. The results have been mostly ugly. If things don’t go well at the beginning of this season, they certainly will not have that as an excuse. Tight end Isaiah Likely spent four years in Baltimore before following Harbaugh to New York. “That first two weeks we had in Greenbrier, out of 11 days, 10 practices, I feel like that’s normal to me. Like, I’m just – if I wake up, I’m putting on cleats. That’s just the mantra I have,” Likely said. “So, hearing how Giants training camp was in the past, that was kind of mind-boggling to me, but I feel like the guys embraced it. We had a good time in Greenbrier, and then when we got here, I feel like now everybody’s on the same mantra as, if we’re in the building, it’s all ball.” The Giants are 2.5-point underdogs against the Cowboys, per FanDuel Sportsbook . It is, of course, a Sunday night game. It is at home. It is Harbaugh’s first game. It is a division game, in a division where the Giants have been the poor, down-trodden step-child for a long while now. It is the first chance for the Giants to show the NFL that they are not the same old Giants. Oh, and in Week 2 the Giants have to travel across the country to face the Los Angeles Rams. The team that is favored to win the 2027 Super Bowl. The team some are already saying has a legitimate chance to go 17-0 this season. The team with Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald, Matthew Stafford, and a host of other star players. So, yeah, winning against the Cowboys on opening night takes on added importance. If the Giants are going to avoid what has become their annual 0-2 start, they would seem to have a better chance to do that in Week 1 than Week 2. Brandon Lee Gowton of the newly-relaunched NFC East Mixtape podcast and Bleeding Green Nation recognized the importance of the beginning of the season for the Giants when he said this: “It’s super-important for the Giants to get off to a great start this season … If you beat the Cowboys, which they have struggled to do so often now, especially in games that truly mattered, that would truly set the tone tone that you bring in John Harbaugh, this is a new era. We have Jaxson Dart here. “I think the Giants really need to win that first game, or at least split with the Rams in that Week 2 game, because once you do that the schedule opens up a bit and I think they can rattle off some wins to build some momentum.” ‘Mixtape’ co-host RJ Ochoa of Blogging the Boys obviously doesn’t want to see a Week 1 Giants’ victory. He also, though, acknowledged, what avoiding an 0-2 start could do for the retooled Giants. “A win against either one of these two teams, both games of which are on prime time, would establish a different feel, would establish a different level of belief.” A new era begins for the Giants next Sunday. Can they start it in a new way?

title: Ex-New York Jets Progress Report: Part II (Defense)
summary: With rosters set, it’s a good time to keep track of where any former Jets have ended up and what their role will be in 2026. We will cover this over three parts. Today is part two, where we will cover defensive players, and then we will deal with special teamers next week. As ever, […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 23: Quinnen Williams #92 of the Dallas Cowboys runs out of the tunnel prior to an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images With rosters set, it’s a good time to keep track of where any former Jets have ended up and what their role will be in 2026. We will cover this over three parts. Today is part two, where we will cover defensive players, and then we will deal with special teamers next week. As ever, this list is intended to be exhaustive, but if we missed anyone, let us know in the comments. Commanders: Washington will be retaining linebacker Frankie Luvu and defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw – two of their four highest paid defensive players – on the roster as expected. They also added defensive tackle Byron Cowart and are retaining him on the practice squad. Cowboys: Defensive tackle Quinnen Williams will be one of the leaders in Dallas’ defense this season, and he’ll do so with a new three-year big money extension under his belt. Eagles: Defensive back Michael Carter II made the Eagles’ roster after taking a paycut to remain with the team. Another ex-Jets defensive back, Jaylen Mahoney, was not retained. Giants: The Giants’ defense is quite ex-Jet heavy as safety Jason Pinnock , linebacker Zaire Barnes , defensive lineman Shelby Harris and defensive back Elijah Campbell all made New York’s final roster. Of the four, Harris should have the biggest role because he’s currently listed as as a starter. Two more defensive linemen – Leki Fotu and Ben Barten – were cut, although Barten was added back to the practice squad. Defensive backs Korie Black and Jarrick Bernard-Converse ended up on injured reserve. Packers: The Packers had three ex-Jet defensive backs in camp – Trey Dean, Jaylin Simpson and Shemar Bartholomew – but none of the three were retained. Vikings: Linebacker Blake Cashman will be starting again for the Vikings, but Jamal Adams won’t be joining him after suffering a season-ending injury in preseason. Bears: The Bears haven’t had any ex-Jets on their defense this offseason. Lions: The Lions secondary will feature cornerback DJ Reed and safety Chuck Clark this season. Clark could have a key role early in the season – when one of their opponents is the Jets – due to injuries. Defensive lineman Jay Tufele and cornerback Bump Cooper also spent time with the Lions but weren’t retained. Bucs: The Bucs are another team who have had no ex-Jets on their defense. Saints: Defensive tackle Nathan Shepherd returns for the Saints, where he has been listed as a starter. Panthers: Claud Cherelus returns for Carolina at linebacker, but he will be coming off the bench for the third year in a row. Falcons: Atlanta had claimed safety Keidron Smith when the Jets released him but he failed to make their roster or practice squad. Rams: The Rams were another team without any ex-Jets on their defense. Seahawks: Defensive tackle Leonard Williams was also a recipient of a lucrative three-year extension during the offseason and he’ll anchor the Seahawks’ defense once again following last year’s Super Bowl win. Linebacker Chazz Surratt also made the roster but Ja’Markis Weston was not retained. Cardinals: Defensive back Isaiah Oliver failed to lock down a roster spot in Arizona and he wasn’t signed to their practice squad. 49ers: Safety Ashtyn Davis is on the 49ers roster, albeit after initially being cut and then brought back the next day. Cornerback Brandon Codrington was also added to the practice squad. Bills: The Bills opted not to retain linebacker Jimmy Ciarlo. Defensive tackle Phidarian Mathis is still with the organization though, albeit that he is suspended for the first three games. Dolphins: Although neither was on their team during preseason, Miami added defensive lineman Mazi Smith and defensive back Jaylin Simpson to their practice squad. Someone who was in action for them in preseason, and reportedly played well, was defensive tackle Fatorma Mulbah, but Miami did not retain him. Patriots: Defensive tackle Leonard Taylor III made the Patriots’ final roster and will be in a backup role in 2026. Bengals: Defensive back Ja’Sir Taylor was with the Bengals in camp but he is now on injured reserve. Browns: Former Jets linebacker Quincy Williams will start for the Browns in 2026. Interestingly, their unofficial depth chart lists Williams as the starting Mike linebacker in a 4-3 system, which would represent a change of role for him, if accurate. Carson Schwesinger will wear the headset in any case. Ravens: Baltimore hasn’t had any ex-Jets on their defense this offseason. Steelers: Defensive back Brandin Echols should provide the Steelers with good depth in the secondary again, but linebacker Jamin Davis wasn’t retained. Texans: Defensive tackle Sheldon Rankins returned to the Texans and has won a starting role again. Houston also retained ex-Jets cornerback Bryce Hall on their practice squad, and also signed defensive tackle Junior Tafuna to their practice squad after the Jets opted not to retain him. Codrington was also with the team before ending up with the 49ers. Colts: Cornerback Sauce Gardner and defensive lineman Micheal Clemons will be on the Colts’ roster this year, albeit with Clemons coming off the bench. Another defensive lineman, Derrick Nnadi, was not retained. Titans: The Titans had six ex-Jets on their defensive line and four made the final roster: Jermaine Johnson , John Franklin-Myers , Jacob Martin and Solomon Thomas . Jalyn Holmes and Khalen Saunders didn’t make it but Holmes ended up on the practice squad. Safety Tony Adams was the other ex-Jet to make the team but he’ll be coming off the bench. Bartholomew was also signed to the practice squad after not being retained by the Packers. Cornerback Mario Goodrich wasn’t retained and linebacker Milo Eifler ended up on injured reserve. Jaguars: Defensive back Corey Ballentine was released and not signed to the practice squad, while linebacker Jared Bartlett ended up on injured reserve. Broncos: The Broncos went through the entire offseason without having any ex-Jets on their defense. Chargers: The Chargers retained linebacker Del’Shawn Phillips , and he’ll be a backup and special teamer with them. Raiders: The Raiders made a late move for defensive lineman Folorunso Fatukasi and he is on their roster to start the season. Chiefs: Finally, the Chiefs cut safety Tanner McCalister but then re-signed him to their practice squad.

title: The Eagles will need a receiver to step up in 2026
summary: No team is perfect. Even the Super Bowl contenders have some flaws. For the Eagles, there are perhaps a few more flaws on this year’s roster than we’re used to seeing from this group, although they still should be considered contenders to win their third straight division title and represent the NFC in the Super […]
full_text: No team is perfect. Even the Super Bowl contenders have some flaws. For the Eagles, there are perhaps a few more flaws on this year’s roster than we’re used to seeing from this group, although they still should be considered contenders to win their third straight division title and represent the NFC in the Super Bowl once again. While the defense appears to be pretty set, questions remain about the offense, especially among the guys catching the ball. The Eagles entered the off-season knowing they would eventually trade A.J. Brown and without much in the pantry at tight end. Dallas Goedert is back as the starter at that position, and DeVonta Smith’s promotion to WR1 should provide a decently-high floor at both of those spots. I also expect the offensive line to perform at a higher level this year, and for the duo of Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby to allow the offense to be one of the best rushing units in the league. But I’m worried about the receivers. First, I love DeVonta Smith. He can do it all. He’s a burner who can make every contested catch there is, despite his slim frame. It’s incredible he’s been able to stay as healthy as he has during his Eagles career. I’ve always believed he could do more than was asked of him in previous seasons, and the hope is the Sean Mannion offense will present more easy buttons for him and Jalen Hurts to take advantage of. I hope he can replicate Brown’s numbers, but I don’t believe it’s automatically going to happen. Even if Smith is everything they hope he will be, there is still a lot of uncertainty concerning the rest of the pass catchers. There’s really no way you can feel confident in any of them at the start of the season. It’s clear the Eagles went into the off-season planning on first round draft pick Makai Lemon to play a major role and even, perhaps, be their starting outside receiver opposite Smith. But his summer-long battle with his hamstring delayed his participation in training camp. He was not impressive in the third preseason game and it’s hard to see him making a significant impact in his first year. Frankly, there are some Jalen Reagor vibes right now. Dontayvion Wicks’ summer was encouraging, but he was brought on board to be the team’s slot receiver, the spot that he played in Green Bay under Mannion. It’s good that he has experience in Mannion’s offense and that familiarity will help. But he’s also a player who compiled just 332 yards in 14 games a season ago, and his season high yardage total is 581, in his 2023 rookie season. He averaged just 23.7 yards per game last year. Training camp superstar Darius Cooper is an interesting player and, who knows, maybe he’ll emerge as a surprise contributor in 2026. But most cap superstars fizzle once the real games begin. Then there are the wily veterans, Elijah Moore and Hollywood Brown, both of whom made the 53-man roster in the hopes one of them can find the fountain of youth. Moore combined to haul n 9 passes for 112 yards with the Bills and Broncos a year ago. He’s still just 26, so maybe there’s more there. Brown is 29 and put up 587 yards on 49 catches a season ago. That’s 255 more than Wicks, by the way. And as The Philly Voice’s Jimmy Kempski noted a couple weeks ago, this is not an imposing physical group of wideouts. Heights/weights of the seven Eagles WRs who have at least a reasonable chance of appearing in regular season games this season: pic.twitter.com/ITcK6dUlDv — Jimmy Kempski (@JimmyKempski) August 22, 2026 The drop-off in receivers would be a bit less worrisome if the tight end situation was better. But after Goedert, who is now 31, there is absolutely nothing. Like Lemon, second round pick Eli Stowers was expected to come in and serve as a secondary pass catcher to Goedert. But Stowers’ summer has been brutal, appearing totally overmatched at this level. It is entirely possible he won’t even be activated on game days this year. That leaves the Eagles with run-blocking specialist Johnny Mundt and frequent practice squad player E.J. Jenkins as the back-ups. If Goedert goes down with an injury, something that happens almost every year, the tight end position will be totally and utterly useless in the passing game. The bottom line: someone outside of DeVonta Smith needs to step up this season. The Eagles need a receiver to emerge from this muddled pack to be Hurts’ reliable No. 2. They need a chain-mover, someone to pile up 700-800 yards this year and give opposing defenses someone else to think about other than Smith. Without it, I don’t see how this offense can function. I’m expecting Mannion’s scheme to struggle at the start of the season. Howie Roseman clearly felt he addressed the Brown departure with quantity over quality. Given their cap situation, it’s understandable. Less understandable is their inability to secure another competent tight end. The best case scenario is the Eagles relying on a dominant running game, with a passing offense based off of that, freeing up players in space and utilizing running backs out of the backfield a bit more, too. And one hopes another tight end ( Zach Ertz? ) will be added to the roster, too. I think the Eagles will be good this year, but it might be in spite of a receiving corps filled with question marks.

title: Eagles News: Philadelphia’s X factors for the 2026 season
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! It’s easier to buy a bounce back season from Cam Jurgens (although back injuries are never comforting) than it is from Landon Dickerson. Jurgens looks healthy and sounds excited for the new season. Dickerson reportedly gave consideration to retirement after 2025 […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - DECEMBER 15: Cam Jurgens #51 and Landon Dickerson #69 of the Philadelphia Eagles in action against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Lincoln Financial Field on December 15, 2024 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! It’s easier to buy a bounce back season from Cam Jurgens (although back injuries are never comforting) than it is from Landon Dickerson. Jurgens looks healthy and sounds excited for the new season. Dickerson reportedly gave consideration to retirement after 2025 (although he denied as much) and he looked physically diminished at times during camp. That being said, we did see positive signs from the running game in training camp. We’ll see if it carries over to game action. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … 2026 NFL season X factors: Key players for all 32 teams – ESPN LG Landon Dickerson and C Cam Jurgens. There are many directions to go with the Eagles. Dontayvion Wicks is the clear WR2 after never really cracking WR4 with the Packers. Can he be a consistent veteran presence in A.J. Brown’s absence? Edge Jonathan Greenard is stepping in for Jaelan Phillips, who was a huge force multiplier for the defense last season. A pec injury forced Greenard to sit out all of training camp, which begs the question: Is he ready to go in the new system? But I’m circling the duo of Dickerson and Jurgens here. The Eagles’ left guard and center — both in the top five highest-paid players at their respective positions — were shells of themselves last season because of lingering injuries. Jurgens had back issues so intense that he had to go to Colombia for stem-cell treatment. Dickerson had a right meniscus tear, a back injury and multiple ankle injuries. He, too, joined Jurgens in Colombia for stem-cell therapy. The Eagles’ running game suffered dramatically as Philadelphia’s two core interior players labored with nagging injuries. On running back carries (i.e., not tush pushes and other QB runs), the Eagles averaged only 1.2 yards before contact per carry after producing 2.0 the season previous — almost half as good of a run-blocking unit as it had been. No matter the new schemes and clever tricks of offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, the Eagles’ offense was Super Bowl-caliber only when the running game was shredding behind an elite offensive line. Dickerson and Jurgens must truly be healthy if we’re to see that version of the Eagles again, and that makes them Philly’s biggest X factor of all. The Eagles’ trendsetting roster – BGN There are over 500 players on practice squads and over 600 players who were in a camp that are currently free agents (or on LSU’s roster). If you need another backup running back, slot receiver, slot corner, off ball LB, there’s plenty lying around. The Eagles problem isn’t that they have 4 QBs. Their problem is that one who is second on the depth chart is a washed up Andy Dalton. Roob’s Observations: How good can Saquon be at an age when most RBs are fading? – NBCSP WHAT TO EXPECT FROM SAQUON: Saquon Barkley had a terrific training camp and it sure looks like he’s primed for a big bounce-back year in Sean Mannion’s offense after an up-and-down 2025 in a miserable offense behind a banged-up offensive line. But he’s also 29, and that’s an age where running backs historically are going downhill. In the last 20 years, only four running backs have rushed for 1,300 yards after turning 29 – Thomas Jones twice with the Jets, Michael Turner with the Falcons, Adrian Peterson once and Derrick Henry twice. Now, Barkley takes such good care of himself and looked so locked in during camp and seems like such a natural fit in this scheme, I don’t see any reason he can’t rush for 1,500 yards if he plays all 17 games. Only nine backs have ever rushed for 1,500 yards after turning 29, only Henry in the last 20 years. But I don’t care what the history is or what the numbers say. I’ll be surprised if Saquon isn’t in that ballpark by the time we get to January. He’s still that good. Eagles mailbag: What backup could end up starting by season’s end? – PhillyVoice I think that there’s an argument that Trotter is a better player, right now, because he has had more time in the scheme, he understands where he needs to be, he can anticipate where the ball is going, and he has Vic Fangio’s trust. However, if he is better, it’s marginal at best. Jihaad Campbell is a far more gifted player in terms of size and athleticism and the only way he is going to get better is if he plays. Their respective ceilings aren’t close. Campbell has All-Pro potential. Trotter does not. So Campbell (rightfully) is going to play. If Campbell is just bad for some reason and he is making losing plays, could they make a switch? Sure, but I think they’ll be patient there, and in my opinion Campbell played well enough as a rookie that there’s little reason to anticipate that he’ll falter. The spot that I would look at is LG. If Landon Dickerson gets banged up again like he did in 2025 and his body simply won’t cooperate, I do think it’s possible that a fresh Drew Kendall could fill in and be a better player. But also, if any of the three starting interior linemen go down, Kendall will be the first guy off the bench. He’s easily the top backup candidate to start games this season. Super Bowl LXI predictions: Los Angeles Rams lead seven NFL favorites to hoist Lombardi Trophy – NFL.com Ben McWilliams: Eagles over Bills. Joe Brady helps Josh Allen get over the hump, but the Bills fall short in the Super Bowl to an Eagles team led by an elite defense. Once a wish kid herself, this Eagles Cheerleader now makes wishes come true – PhiladelphiaEagles.com The Eagles and Make-A-Wish thought they were hosting five wish kids to play mini-golf with Jalen Hurts last week. As it turns out, there were actually six wish kids at the event. Three Eagles Cheerleaders went to spend time with the wish kids and their families. Among them was Jordyn, a rookie cheerleader who had just made her debut to fans at Public Practice. Once a wish kid herself, Jordyn found herself on the other side of the Make-A-Wish experience, making sure the kids’ and families’ day was special. “It was honestly a really surreal experience,” Jordyn said. “I really felt like I was living two lives in that moment. It was truly an honor to be there with those kids and be there for them that day.” “It really was one of the best days of my life.” A native of Richboro, Pennsylvania, Jordyn was diagnosed with kidney cancer at only 3 years old. When she became part of the Make-A-Wish family, the cheerleader-to-be asked to go to Disney World. Raiders’ Patrick Johnson a feel-good story, but veteran earned his spot – Silver And Black Pride Johnson, who entered the league and spent the majority of is NFL career with the Philadelphia Eagles as a seventh-round pick (234th overall) in the 2021 NFL Draft, tops Slone in experience and and gameday production this preseason. And has the mentality required for NFL longshots as he was a July 27 signing by the Raiders — Slone in comparison was inked as an UDFA back on April 30. Rams Cut DB Zech McPhearson From Injured Reserve – NFL Trade Rumors The Los Angeles Rams officially released DB Zech McPhearson from injured reserve with an injury settlement on Saturday. McPhearson, 28, is a former fourth-round pick of the Eagles back in 2021. He signed a four-year rookie contract with Philadelphia following the draft. How the Cowboys season could go wrong – Blogging The Boys The unsettling Prescott pattern. If the Cowboys lose their franchise quarterback for an extended amount of time, that’s bad news, and we’re all well aware of that. That means every year we hold our breath that Dak Prescott doesn’t get hurt. At 33 years old, he’s no longer a spring chicken, meaning his body doesn’t respond the same way, and certain ailments can…

title: Falcons finally name starting QB for Week 1 vs. Steelers
summary: The Atlanta Falcons will turn to veteran quarterback Tua Tagovailoa to open the 2026 regular season against the Pittsburgh Steelers, according to ESPN insider Adam Schefter. Tagovailoa is expected to make the start in Week 1 at Pittsburgh with second-year quarterback Michael Penix Jr. continuing to work his way back from knee surgery. Penix’s recovery […]
full_text: The Atlanta Falcons will turn to veteran quarterback Tua Tagovailoa to open the 2026 regular season against the Pittsburgh Steelers, according to ESPN insider Adam Schefter . Tagovailoa is expected to make the start in Week 1 at Pittsburgh with second-year quarterback Michael Penix Jr. continuing to work his way back from knee surgery. Penix’s recovery has kept him from taking the majority of the first-team repetitions during the offseason and preseason, allowing Tagovailoa to establish himself as the Falcons’ primary option under center heading into the regular season. Now, Tagovailoa will get the opportunity to lead Atlanta into one of the more challenging road environments in the NFL when the Falcons travel to Acrisure Stadium to face the Steelers. The matchup also provides an intriguing early test for Pittsburgh’s revamped defense due to the Falcons offensive weapons. Running back Bijan Robinson and wide receiver Drake London are two of the better skill players in the league. Pittsburgh will look to apply pressure to Tua and force him to make difficult decisions against a defense expected to be aggressive under new DC Patrick Graham. With Penix still working toward a full return, Tagovailoa will have the first opportunity to establish himself as Atlanta’s quarterback. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers will face depleted Falcons pass rush Week 1
summary: In the 2025 NFL Draft, the Atlanta Falcons went all-in on improving their edge rusher room, spending two first-round draft picks on the position in Georgia’s Jalon Walker (No. 15 overall) and Tennessee’s James Pearce Jr. (No. 26 overall). However, the Falcons will be without the contributions of both players for most of the 2026 […]
full_text: Jul 30, 2026; Atlanta, Falcons, USA; Atlanta Falcons defensive end Samson Ebukam (52) warms up on the field during training camp at IBM Performance Field. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In the 2025 NFL Draft, the Atlanta Falcons went all-in on improving their edge rusher room, spending two first-round draft picks on the position in Georgia’s Jalon Walker (No. 15 overall) and Tennessee’s James Pearce Jr. (No. 26 overall). However, the Falcons will be without the contributions of both players for most of the 2026 season, starting with Sept. 13’s opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Walker, who finished 2025 with 5.5 sacks, was placed on season-ending injured reserve in early August after tearing his ACL in camp. And Pearce, who recorded 10.5 sacks in 2025, will miss the first eight games of 2026 with a suspension after domestic violence-related charges in February . The Falcons signed veteran pass rusher Za’Darius Smith out of retirement in mid-August to bolster their depth chart at the position. Smith will be 34 when the season begins. He recorded 1.5 sacks in two starts with the Eagles last year, but recorded nine sacks in 2024. Smith is currently listed as a backup on the Falcons’ current depth chart , although ESPN projects him as a starter in 2026. Currently, the Falcons’ listed starters at defensive end are Cameron Thomas (2.5 sacks last year) and Brandon Dorlus (8.5 sacks last year). Dorlus is more of an interior rusher, but is expected to get more playing time at defensive end this season due to the Falcons’ need at the position. Other names who could be prominent members of the rotation include veteran Samson Ebukam (two sacks last year) and potential practice squad elevations Zach Harrison (4.5 sacks last year) and Bralen Trice. While the Falcons aren’t completely devoid of talent on the edges, Week 1 should be a more favorable matchup than previously expected for the Steelers’ offensive tackles, who have their own question marks entering 2026. Troy Fautanu will be making his first NFL regular season start since switching to left tackle, while Dylan Cook or the rookie Max Iheanachor is expected to start on the right side. The Falcons’ interior defensive line, however, is expected to be a tougher assignment, with the aforementioned Dorlus and proven starters such as D’Shawn Hand and the recently-acquired Gervon Dexter Sr., who recorded six sacks from the interior for the Chicago Bears in 2025. Stay tuned to BTSC for more Steelers vs. Falcons game preview information ahead of Week 1.

full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - AUGUST 14: Jack Strand #18 of the Atlanta Falcons drops back to pass during the fourth quarter against the Denver Broncos in an NFL preseason game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers open their season in t-minus one week against the Atlanta Falcons. It’s not controversial at all to say the Steelers are the more talented team, but they may have an even bigger advantage when the ball is kicked off next Sunday. There is a real possibility that the Steelers will face Atlanta’s fourth-string quarterback, as John Fricke of 92.9 The Game in Atlanta points out. “One week out [and the] Falcons have not yet named a starter,“ Fricke posted on X . ”Tua did not win the job. He was a D-II All-American in 2025. He finished his collegiate career with an astounding 13,161 yards and 126 touchdowns. While he was an undrafted rookie, the Falcons may feel more comfortable with Strand after seeing what Tua Tagovailoa showed them in preseason play – a stretch of play that reportedly made him “impossible” to start in the eyes of the Falcons, via Ian Rapoport . title: Steelers offensive line named one of the ‘best bargains’ in NFL
summary: Much like most Steelers fans, NFL offensive line expert Brandon Thorn is cautiously optimistic about Pittsburgh’s starting five entering the upcoming season. In his “2026 OL Almanac” published Aug. 28 on his Trench Warfare Substack, Thorn ranked the Steelers’ starters as the 18th-most talented offensive line in the league, while also noting they are the […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Zach Frazier #54 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on during the game against the Green Bay Packers at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Much like most Steelers fans, NFL offensive line expert Brandon Thorn is cautiously optimistic about Pittsburgh’s starting five entering the upcoming season. In his “2026 OL Almanac” published Aug. 28 on his Trench Warfare Substack, Thorn ranked the Steelers’ starters as the 18th-most talented offensive line in the league, while also noting they are the cheapest. In a section of the almanac listing some trends that stood out to him, Thorn wrote that the Bengals offensive line (ranked 14th in talent) and the Steelers “are the top two value units” in the NFL, praising how each “are built around a homegrown core with continuity” and affordable contracts. In Pittsburgh’s case, every starter minus right tackle Dylan Cook (who is still only costing the team $1.075 million this year), is still on their rookie contract, while projected future starters Max Iheanachor and Gennings Dunker are also on rookie deals. Expecting Iheanachor to start at some point in 2026, Thorn has the Steelers ranked as the league’s least-experienced starting line in terms of collective starts (also the third youngest), but also the fourth-most athletic when it comes to Relative Athletic Score. Thorn wrote that Pittsburgh’s apparent offensive line bargain comes with an asterisk given the group’s unproven right side of Spencer Anderson and Iheanachor, and two of its best players, Troy Fautanu and Mason McCormick, switching sides this year to the left. However, he noted that the Fautanu and McCormick’s previous college experience on the left side — and Zach Frazier being “a top-two center in the NFL” — should alleviate some of the concerns. “Pittsburgh is playing a lottery ticket on the right side while banking on having a strong trio from left tackle to center,” Thorn concluded in his Steelers blurb. “If Iheanachor hits, this talent rank will clear 18th by season’s end.” Currently, Thorn has the Steelers as the second-best offensive line in the AFC North, just behind the Bengals (14) but ahead of the Ravens (21) and Browns (31). After a largely disappointing preseason and chatter about how the group could struggle to gel in a new offense , the Steelers’ line will have the opportunity to gain some positive momentum in the upcoming season opener against the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13.

Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox has predicted that the Detroit Lions could acquire Porter in exchange for a 2027 first-round pick, a move that would give Pittsburgh another premium asset […]
full_text: The Pittsburgh Steelers could face a difficult decision regarding Joey Porter Jr. as contract negotiations continue to stall, and one NFL analyst has proposed a blockbuster solution. Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox has predicted that the Detroit Lions could acquire Porter in exchange for a 2027 first-round pick, a move that would give Pittsburgh another premium asset while potentially resolving the uncertainty surrounding the young cornerback’s future. The prediction comes as Porter enters the final year of his rookie contract without a long-term extension. The situation has become increasingly complicated in recent weeks, with reports indicating that the two sides remain at an impasse. Porter has also reportedly considered requesting a trade or sitting out games if an agreement cannot be reached. Knox believes Pittsburgh could ultimately view a trade as a legitimate option if the organization determines that keeping Porter long term is unlikely. “If things get to a point where the Steelers don’t believe they can keep Porter, flipping them for a high 2027 pick will become an option for them.” The potential return would be significant. Rather than allowing Porter to play out the final season of his rookie contract and potentially depart in free agency, Pittsburgh would acquire another first-round selection to add to its draft capital. Knox also connected the hypothetical trade to the Steelers’ long-term quarterback situation. “Aaron Rodgers isn’t the future at quarterback, and while Pittsburgh may hope that either Will Howard or Drew Allar can be, it wouldn’t hurt to have a pair of first round picks in what is expected to be a QB-heavy draft,” Knox writes. That could make a 2027 first-round pick particularly valuable for Pittsburgh. Rodgers is entering the season as the Steelers’ veteran option at quarterback, while Howard and Allar represent potential succession plans. If neither young quarterback establishes himself as the long-term answer, an additional first-round selection could give general manager Omar Khan more flexibility to move up the board for a quarterback. For Detroit, meanwhile, Porter would represent an aggressive addition to a secondary on a team with Super Bowl aspirations. A talented, physical corner entering his prime would give the Lions another proven defensive playmaker and potentially strengthen one of the most important positions on the roster. Porter has established himself as a significant piece of Pittsburgh’s defense since being selected No. 32 overall in the 2023 NFL Draft. He has started all 41 games he has played and recorded 165 tackles, 31 passes defended and three interceptions over his first three seasons. The timing, however, is critical. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy has acknowledged an “impasse” in the negotiations, while Porter recently returned to practice after missing time with a back injury. A trade involving Porter would still represent a major departure for Pittsburgh. The Steelers have little incentive to move a 26-year-old starting cornerback entering his prime, particularly with the team attempting to contend in 2026. But if the contract stalemate becomes irreparable, a first-round pick could change the equation. For now, the Lions acquiring Porter remains only a bold prediction—not a reported trade negotiation. But with Pittsburgh’s quarterback future still uncertain and Porter’s contract situation unresolved, Knox’s proposal gives the Steelers an intriguing alternative if the two sides cannot find common ground. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images As if the Seattle Seahawks’ safety room wasn’t injured enough, there could be a problem for another one of their starters. Following Sunday’s practice, the Seahawks released their first injury report of the 2026 season, and while the main focus is rightfully on Nick Emmanwori given his ankle surgery recovery, there’s some concern regarding the availability of Ty Okada, who did not practice due to a hamstring issue. Okada is replacing Coby Bryant as the other starting deep safety alongside Julian Love, and with Bud Clark out for the year there’s literally no other healthy depth on the active roster. The Seahawks do have Rodney Thomas II, Maxen Hook, D’Anthony Bell, and A.J. Finley all available on the practice squad. Emmanwori, meanwhile, was limited in practice but it seems like he is very much touch-and-go as far as Week 1 readiness. We also finally have confirmation that wide receiver Tory Horton has been dealing with his own hamstring injury, and he was similarly limited in Sunday’s practice. Horton did not play in preseason and missed several practices during that span. For some good news in the Seahawks secondary, rookie corner Julian Neal was a full participant after hurting his quad during training camp. The third-round pick missed all of preseason with that injury, further complicating matters in Seattle’s reshaped cornerback depth chart. On New England’s side, starting defensive tackle Christian Barmore and running back TreVeyon Henderson were both DNPs due to their respective injuries. Henderson is not expected to play on Wednesday after tweaking his ankle two weeks ago. Barmore is a name worth monitoring as one of the forces on New England’s interior defensive line. title: Seahawks-Patriots preview: How different are the Patriots since the Super Bowl?
summary: The Seattle Seahawks’ 2026 regular season begins with a familiar opponent, but I don’t think Seattle can approach Wednesday night as if it is simply picking up where Super Bowl 60 ended. For the first regular-season edition of “Eye on the Prey” as part of The Hawks Eye podcast, I was joined by Taylor Kyles […]
full_text: Jul 28, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots safety Kevin Byard III (31) does a drill with wide receiver Romeo Doubs (87) during training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Seattle Seahawks’ 2026 regular season begins with a familiar opponent, but I don’t think Seattle can approach Wednesday night as if it is simply picking up where Super Bowl 60 ended. For the first regular-season edition of “Eye on the Prey” as part of The Hawks Eye podcast , I was joined by Taylor Kyles of Patriots Daily to take a deeper look at what has changed in New England and what Seattle should expect when the Patriots arrive at Lumen Field for Week 1. Roster changes, plus another year for Drake Maye The biggest difference is the amount of talent New England has added around Drake Maye. The Patriots made an aggressive move for A.J. Brown, added Romeo Doubs from the Green Bay Packers to the receiving corps and strengthened the offensive line with former New York Jets guard Alijah Vera-Tucker, allowing the Patriots to move Jared Wilson from left guard to center. Defensively, veterans such as safety Kevin Byard and former Seahawks pass rusher Dre’Mont Jones give Mike Vrabel additional flexibility. This was already a 14-win team last season, so the offseason was less about rebuilding and more about addressing the areas that kept New England from finishing the job against Seattle in February. “I think one of the biggest things was the offensive line,” Kyles said. “And look, that wasn’t a secret going in. Will Campbell had a sprained MCL and was playing next to Jared Wilson, so you had two rookies on one side of the line of scrimmage. Garrett Bradbury had been pretty solid for what the expectations were, but you kind of knew that he wasn’t exactly a strength for that unit. He was really just kind of holding the spot for a season. Morgan Moses, I mean, the guy’s 36 years old. As you can imagine, I think when you look back at the tape, honestly, looking back recently, it really stood out. It was like, Morgan’s a good player, but for a guy that age, all those games it really did add up. And I think it kind of showed in his plays. So, the offensive line clearly needed reinforcements. It needed its younger players to take a step forward.” Taylor and I spent a good portion of the conversation discussing how those additions could change the chess match between Maye and Mike Macdonald. Seattle’s defense created problems last season through disguise, simulated pressure and post-snap rotation. A.J. Brown now gives Maye a receiver who can win even when the coverage is technically sound, which could force Seattle to make some difficult decisions about how aggressively it wants to pressure while also protecting against explosive plays. “[The red zone offense] looks like it’s going to be more potent. And obviously that starts with AJ Brown because all you need is the twofer in the red zone. If you’re a threat on a slant and you’re a threat on a fade, very hard to defend that. But you’ve also seen Romeo Doubs have a lot of success in the red zone, which isn’t a surprise. He’s been kind of a red zone merchant his entire career.” Another year in Josh McDaniel’s offense could also provide valuable experience for the MVP runner-up. “A major emphasis for the Patriots offense this offseason is incorporating tempo, having Drake get to the line of scrimmage and different types of tempo. It’s not always ‘let’s go as fast as we can and just call a play.‘ Sometimes it’s ‘let’s get to the line of scrimmage, dummy call, see what they’re in, and then try to get ourselves in good position.‘ So, the biggest things for me really and obviously like receiver, we can kind of hit on that, but really it was the trenches and it was Drake Maye between the ears, just a lack of experience that really got exposed as he got into the game and you felt like, all right, they’re not running the ball. Everyone knows what’s going on. Is Drake going to take what they give him? Is he gonna kind of panic a little bit? And you saw the inexperience.” A cornerback matchup the Seahawks could exploit On the other side, this will be our first opportunity to see Brian Fleury’s offense in a meaningful regular-season game. New England still has plenty of high-end defensive talent, particularly in the secondary with Christian Gonzalez, and its interior defensive front has the ability to disrupt an offense without requiring constant pressure packages. How Fleury uses motion, play-action and formations to create favorable matchups will be one of the most fascinating parts of Week 1. Taylor did note one possible wide receiver vs. cornerback matchup that would worry him from a Patriots perspective. “I didn’t like Rashid Shaheed versus Carlton Davis before the Super Bowl,” Kyles said. “I was pretty clear about that. I did not think that was a good matchup for the Patriots. Maybe it didn’t manifest that way, but like you mentioned, he’s even better, and Carlton Davis missed most of training camp. In some of the joint practices, quite frankly, he was getting kind of cooked off the line in a way that slightly concerned me. Mow Marcus Jones, if they match up, I like it. I think if Rashid Shaheed’s going to go up and make an impressive catch, awesome. But I think Marcus would be on his hip. He’s one of the most explosive players at that position. If Marcus Jones were three inches taller, he’d be a Pro Bowler. Like, he’s a phenomenal player. It’s just he’s small and there’s only so much you can do at that size, and even then he still makes plays. “I don’t like it because unless Carlton Davis gets his hands on Rashid Shaheed, he just can’t run with him. That’s the reality. He’s an older corner. Again, he’s a pro and I think technically there’s a lot of things he can do to kind of even that matchup a little bit. But if Sam Darnold decides that he wants to really test that matchup, I have a hard time thinking that he’s not going to get some results he likes.” We also went through New England’s offseason, training camp and preseason, the Patriots’ remaining roster questions, the matchups that could ultimately decide the game, and our keys to victory. This may be a Super Bowl rematch, but both teams have evolved since February. That is what makes Wednesday night so interesting! Watch the full conversation with Taylor Kyles below as we break down Seahawks vs. Patriots from every angle. full_text: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seahawks fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys. After marauding through their schedule, the 2025 Seattle Seahawks beat the divisional rival San Francisco 49ers (handily) and the divisional rival Los Angeles Rams to earn a spot in the Super Bowl this past February. Once there, the Hawks put on a show, shutting down and shutting out the New England Patriots until into the 4th quarter of a 29-13 beatdown. That recent performance, along with the fact that Seattle retained a staggering 20 of 22 starters from last year’s campaign, perhaps color the fan poll results for the Seahawks’ first game on Wednesday, September 9th. Of Seahawks fans polled, 94% think that Seattle will win by some amount. The prediction that got the highest percentage of votes (48%) was the Hawks winning by 9+ points to kick off the NFL season. Following closely behind, the scenario involving the Seahawks overcoming the Pats by a more competitive range of 1-8 points came in at 46% of fan vote. The 6% of voters who think the Patriots will win by a margin of 1-8 points might be keeping in mind that New England did make an effort to get tougher in the offseason. The team had a very public pursuit of A.J. Brown at wide receiver and signed Alijah Vera-Tucker to shore up an offensive line that was manhandled by the “Dark Side” defensive line. Interesting, as Seattle opened Super Bowl LX as -4.5-point favorites. As of today, FanDuel Sportsbook lists Seattle as being favored in the Week 1 Wednesday rematch, but this time by only -3.5. Are the Seattle Seahawks still not getting their just dues? They set a franchise record, earning a +191 scoring differential in 2025, and look to be building something for the long term. Each season starts the team-building process anew. The Seahawks do have a unique situation; in immediately squaring off against an opponent they demoralized on the biggest stage. And they’ll raise a banner over their heads before the game is even played. Looking forward to seeing if the Seattle Seahawks can continue to demand respect.
