title: Seahawks contract breakdown: The details of the Leonard Williams extension
summary: Just days remain until the Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots in the first meaningful NFL football game since the Seattle Seahawks walloped the New England Patriots 29-13 in Super Bowl 60 to bring home the second Lombardi Trophy in franchise history. But, last year is last year, and 2026 is a new season. […]
full_text: Nov 2, 2025; Landover, Maryland, USA; Seattle Seahawks defensive end Leonard Williams (99) reacts to the win against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Just days remain until the Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots in the first meaningful NFL football game since the Seattle Seahawks walloped the New England Patriots 29-13 in Super Bowl 60 to bring home the second Lombardi Trophy in franchise history. But, last year is last year, and 2026 is a new season. That, of course, means it’s time for the Seahawks to defend their Super Bowl title, and when they take on the Patriots Wednesday in the season opening game it will mark the first time defensive lineman Leonard Williams takes to the field since signing a three-year, $90 million contract extension with Seattle in late August . Leonard Williams contract extension details For those fans who have been curious about the details of Williams’ new contract extension, here is how it lays out: Signing bonus : $22M 2026 : Base salary: 3.8M (fully guaranteed), per game roster bonuses: $850k 2027 : Option bonus: $10M (vesting guarantee), base salary: $10.73M (vesting guarantee), per game roster bonus: $1.02M, workout bonus: $250k 2028 : Option bonus: $10M ($5.35M vesting guarantee), base salary: $12.73M, per game roster bonus: $1.02M, workout bonus: $250k 2029 : Base salary: $32.73M, per game roster bonus: $1.02M, workout bonus: $250k 2030 & 2031 : void years for cap management purposes That’s a lot of numbers, and most fans want them distilled down to cap hits, so here are the cap hits over the life of the contract: 2026 : $22.036M (base salary $3.8M, signing bonus proration from 2024 free agent contract $8.3M, signing bonus proration from 2026 extension $4.4M, proration of 2025 base salary to signing bonus conversion $4.686M, per game roster bonuses $850k) 2027 : $23.086M (base salary: $10.73M, signing bonus proration from 2026 extension $4.4M, proration of 2025 base salary to signing bonus conversion $4.686M, proration of 2027 option bonus $2M, per game roster bonuses $1.02M, workout bonus $250k) 2028 : $27.586M (base salary: $12.73M, signing bonus proration from 2026 extension $4.4M, proration of 2025 base salary to signing bonus conversion $4.686M, proration of 2027 option bonus $2M, proration of 2028 option bonus $2.5M, per game roster bonuses $1.02M, workout bonus $250k) 2029 : $42.9M (base salary $32.73M, signing bonus proration from 2026 extension $4.4M, proration of 2027 option bonus $2.5M, proration of 2028 option bonus $2M, per game roster bonuses $1.02M, workout bonus $250k) 2030 (void year, not on roster) : $13.4M (signing bonus from 2026 extension $4.4M, proration of 2027 option bonus $2M, proration of 2028 option bonus $2.5M, 2031 proration of 2027 option bonus accelerated into 2030 due to voiding, $2M, 2031 proration of 2028 option bonus accelerated into 2030 due to voiding $2.5M) In addition, according to Pro Football Talk , the contract includes an escalator for 2028 if Williams is a first- or second-team All-Pro in 2027, along with an incentive for the same in 2028. That, of course, raises the question why the Seahawks would use an escalator in one season and an incentive in the next. The answer to that question likely rests in the cap situation the front office anticipates for 2027. Specifically, as of right now with just 40 players under contract for the 2027 season the Seahawks are looking at roughly $30M of cap space, which means once they sign their draft picks, build out the practice squad and set aside money for injury replacements during the season, they aren’t exactly looking at being flush with cap space. However, for 2028 they are currently looking at having north of $100M of available cap, and that is the clue as to why the All-Pro incentives are structured the way they are. To get directly to the point, if Williams is selected as an All-Pro during the 2026 season, then an incentive for All-Pro for 2027 would be considered likely to be earned and would count the full $2M against the cap for the duration of the season . The Seahawks would only get that cap space back after the season when the league does the end of year incentive netting, meaning that if Williams is an All-Pro in 2026 it would tie up $2M of valuable 2027 cap space regardless of how well he plays. In contrast, by making the $2M for 2027 an escalator instead of an incentive, Williams still gets the exact same $2M if he is an All-Pro that year, but it puts the cap hit for that $2M in the 2028 league year instead of 2027. Then, in 2028 when the cap situation should not be nearly as tight, the team can much more easily handle a $2M likely to be earned incentive, so for 2028 the $2M is in the form of an incentive. The next piece worth noting is that many fans will certainly look at the cap numbers of the contract and point out that there is no way the team will keep Williams around at age 35 in 2029 on a $42.9M cap hit. That is entirely possible, but it is worth noting that should Seattle move on from Williams after the 2028 season, the team would recognize $22.3M of dead money in the form of: $8.8M unamortized signing bonus from 2026 extension $6M unamortized from 2027 option bonus $7.5M unamortized from 2028 option bonus Not predicting anything one way or another at this point, simply pointing out what could be. Lastly, one other item of note which will bear watching over the coming seasons is the vesting guarantees of the contract. As has been noted time and again here at Field Gulls, under John Schneider the Seahawks do not put fully guaranteed money past the first year of a contract, and that is the same in this contract. All the guarantees in this extension in 2027 or later are in the traditional structure used by the team where they are guaranteed for injury at signing, and vest into full guarantees the Friday after the Super Bowl in the year of the guarantee. For 2027 those guarantees are in the form of Williams’ $10.73M base salary and the $10M option bonus. More interesting, though, is 2028 when $5.35M of the $10M option bonus is guaranteed for injury at signing, and will vest into a full guarantee the Friday after the Super Bowl. What makes that so interesting is that once they look at an online salary cap page, many fans may be quick to point out that the Seahawks could save nearly $10M of 2028 cap space by moving on from a 34-year old Williams, but that’s not accurate. First it’s not accurate because as of publication today the dead money numbers listed on those salary cap pages do not currently include any of the 2027 option bonus money. In addition, because of the vesting guarantee for $5.35M of the 2028 option bonus, if Seattle were to move on from Williams once that guarantee has vested, the dead money the team would recognize would be: $31.236M (2025 base salary to signing bonus proration $4.686M, 2026 signing bonus proration $13.2M, 2027 option bonus proration $8M, 2028 option bonus portion that is effectively fully guaranteed $5.35M) Given that Williams is set to carry a $27.586M cap hit for 2028, moving on after the guarantee vests would result in a net loss of cap space, while even moving on before the guarantee vests – assuming he finishes the season healthy and would even be able to – would free up only $1.7M of 2028 cap space. Boiling it all down, based on the contract structure there is every reason to believe Williams will be wreaking havoc on opposing offenses for the next three seasons, which should be quite enjoyable for everyone except opposing offenses.

title: Why Seahawks national ‘disrespect’ is really about not believing in Sam Darnold
summary: We’re less than a week away from the start of the 2026 NFL season, and despite what the likes of Ephraim Salaam might believe, the Seattle Seahawks—not the Los Angeles Rams—are indeed the reigning Super Bowl champions. The Rams are Super Bowl favorites this year for perfectly understandable reasons. A team that narrowly missed out […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - AUGUST 28: Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks throws a pass before an NFL preseason game between the Seattle Seahawks and Kansas City Chiefs on Aug 28, 2026 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We’re less than a week away from the start of the 2026 NFL season, and despite what the likes of Ephraim Salaam might believe, the Seattle Seahawks—not the Los Angeles Rams— are indeed the reigning Super Bowl champions . "They're gonna steamroll everybody. I put my money on the Rams. I'll take the Rams over the field. They have everything they need to to repeat." @EphraimSalaam sees the Los Angeles Rams as a scary factor in the NFC | @WillardAndDibs pic.twitter.com/nszExB5eiX — 95.7 The Game (@957thegame) September 2, 2026 The Rams are Super Bowl favorites this year for perfectly understandable reasons. A team that narrowly missed out on the Super Bowl with an MVP quarterback just added the literal Defensive Player of the Year, a very good cornerback, and lost no one of real consequence in free agency. Jared Verse was their biggest loss and they replaced him with, to repeat, the literal Defensive Player of the Year. Oh yeah, and Aaron Donald is back. But the Seahawks, despite being among the betting favorites to win it all this year, have been treated as somewhat of an afterthought even outside of the Rams’ typically splashy offseason. Have a look at the Super Bowl 61 predictions on NFL.com and the Seahawks are nowhere to be found. I imagine when more predictions roll out, the Seahawks will not be in the mix for selection despite having among the best odds to at least make it back. Maybe it’s because the Seahawks came out of nowhere last year when preseason expectations were, at best, a playoff berth. Or maybe it’s because betting on a repeat has largely proven to be a poor gamble. While I believe some of the perceived slights are overblown and that there are still a few public faces who are supportive of the Seahawks, like FS1’s Danny Parkins and NFL Network’s Kyle Brandt… It’s seems all offseason the media has been so eager to rip the crown off the Seahawks before it even finishes sinking into place on top of Seattle’s head and put it on the Rams’ brow. Finally @KyleBrandt with some straight up BALL KNOWLEDGE on how “Biblically dominant” the… pic.twitter.com/sNnLDDmSh9 — Nick Lee (@NickLee51) June 9, 2026 “Coming in at #2, everybody’s super team, the Rams… I have the Seahawks being the forgotten champions and running it back.” @DannyParkins shares his NFC West predictions: pic.twitter.com/Ar9mBKi1GA — First Things First (@FTFonFS1) September 2, 2026 …There is no getting around the why Seattle is not considered a prime pick to pull off a repeat. It’s Sam Darnold. This is a quarterback-driven league and quarterbacks drive more obnoxious discourse than any other position in North American sports. Sam Darnold spent a good chunk of his career being a punchline for his ill-fated stint with the New York Jets. His career revival with the Minnesota Vikings was an amazing story until he crashed without a parachute in his final two games. When the Seahawks signed Darnold in free agency , that moved the national needle not a jot. Was it fair to be skeptical that Darnold was a one-year wonder under a highly respected offensive mind in Kevin O’Connell? Absolutely. We’ve seen one-off great quarterback seasons and then nothing else of consequence afterward. But Darnold didn’t prove to be a one-year wonder. He might not have put up the gaudy stats like he did in Minnesota, but he played like an above-average quarterback who didn’t drag a talented roster down and at times (like the NFC Championship) elevated his game when the team needed him most. Two very good seasons with two different organizations is enough for any sensible person to think that this version of Darnold is sustainable and not a fluke. And yet, the “yeah, buts” remain. “Yeah, but Darnold still led the league in turnovers.” (While having a high passing efficiency) “Yeah, but Darnold had an elite defense.” (So did C.J. Stroud, but he actively threw away a playoff game in a half) “Yeah, but Darnold doesn’t have his Super Bowl MVP running back anymore.” (Many of his best games were with an ineffective run game) “Yeah, but Darnold lost his offensive coordinator.” (We’re TBD on Brian Fleury, but I don’t think he’ll collapse without Klint Kubiak) Darnold’s struggles early in his career may be behind him, but the perception may be unshakeable unless he transforms into an MVP caliber quarterback, which I’m not sure he’ll attain (at least not in a low-volume passing offense). Even if the best is yet to come for Sam, I don’t really care if he never becomes MVP great, especially after we obsessed way too much about it in the last couple of good Russell Wilson seasons. If someone on a rookie contract had Darnold’s productivity and wins over the past two seasons, they’d be projected as a future superstar. But it’s Sam Darnold, so there’s almost an expectation that he’s going to be seeing ghosts again. I’d argue that if you hypothetically swapped out Darnold for a widely considered superior quarterback (e.g. Josh Allen, Joe Burrow, Patrick Mahomes, Lamar Jackson, Jordan Love) then the Seahawks would probably remain favorites or at least be level with the Rams. We’ve sort of been here before when the Seahawks were last champions. The Legion of Boom and Marshawn Lynch took the plaudits, while Russell Wilson was somewhat patronizingly referred to as a “game manager.” Don’t believe me? Have a sampling of these headlines from either side of Super Bowl 48… Russ might have had his own disrespect at the time when he was compared to Andrew Luck, Colin Kaepernick, and Cam Newton and looked upon as good, but not as good as any of them. But even the biggest Wilson skeptics acknowledged he was a dynamic play-maker who kept turnovers to a minimum and made clutch plays when he needed to. The underlying point, however, is that Wilson was getting compared to QBs who were considered to among the best, and it also did not stop national media from picking the Seahawks to at least get to Super Bowl 49 . The framing of Darnold is generally that of a two-hit wonder who might still not even be a good quarterback , almost as if to suggest he played almost no meaningful role in consecutive 14-win seasons and a Super Bowl win. I loath to include his hot takes in this piece, but this doozy from Jason McIntyre just last week is one to behold. "We're a little irrationally high on Sam Darnold. I think the best comparison for him is Trent Dilfer." @jasonrmcintyre argues Darnold's success is all thanks to the Seahawks' elite defense & special teams units pic.twitter.com/GBBv8gcwLY — Herd w/Colin Cowherd (@TheHerd) August 27, 2026 Trent Dilfer averaged under 10 passes completed per game during the Baltimore Ravens’ four playoff games. He famously won a game in which the Ravens had six total first downs and he went 5/16 for 117 yards . When he was with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, he once lost a home game by committing four turnovers despite the Buccaneers defense holding the New York Giants to no offensive touchdowns and FOUR first downs. McIntyre spews out molten lava takes for fun on Fox Sports on a weekly basis, but the concept of Darnold even being talked about this way after the past two seasons is ignorance, stupidity, and the unwillingness to evolve original opinions. I was very much on the wagon of making fun of Darnold, even through some of his bad moments in Minnesota, but the Vikings stint at least upgraded my opinion of Sam to lukewarm. Between his attitude, his tangible on-field improvements, and winning a Super Bowl, I’ve flipped my opinion on Sam for the better. It is okay if your initial or longstanding opinion on a player changes in the face of new information, as opposed to being stubborn about your priors. Of course, it…

title: Two more Seahawks documentaries that will bring 12’s joy before the 2026 season
summary: The offseason hype has been all about the Los Angeles Rams. Understandable (if unforgivable) — since they took some aggressive swings in a year in which L.A. is hosting the Super Bowl. They are also not stationed in the upper left outpost of the Pacific Northwest. Luckily, HBO’s refreshing “Hard Knocks” series took a unique […]
full_text: The offseason hype has been all about the Los Angeles Rams. Understandable (if unforgivable) — since they took some aggressive swings in a year in which L.A. is hosting the Super Bowl. They are also not stationed in the upper left outpost of the Pacific Northwest. Luckily, HBO’s refreshing “ Hard Knocks ” series took a unique peek into how an elite-tier franchise is run. That same outpost of non-east coast-bias is one that was framed in full majesty, complete with shimmering water, careening bald eagles and a city abuzz with positive vibes. Volume 🆙 Episode 3 of Hard Knocks: Training Camp with the Seahawks out now on @hbomax pic.twitter.com/tfldVYfBcj — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) August 19, 2026 Hard Knocks aside, if you want to revisit the glory of last year’s title run one more time before the title defense starts on 9/9, then there are two documentaries worth your time. America’s Game: The 2025 Seattle Seahawks Mike Macdonald used to download and memorize all the "America's Game" documentaries and listen to them on his iPod Nano. Tremendous. Which sports film / doc / DVD/ VHS tape do you watch so much that the VHS stopped working ? From this week's "The Schrager Hour" @OmahaProd pic.twitter.com/t12V5E1rMX — Peter Schrager (@PSchrags) September 2, 2026 NFL Films created a moving tribute to last year’s Super Bowl-winning Seahawks’ championship season. America’s Game on the 2025 Seattle Seahawks is currently airing on YouTube TV. The same America’s Game that Seahawks head coach, Mike Macdonald (born in Boston) confessed to watching in high school when the New England Patriots were authoring a dynasty. America’s Game brought to life player and coach perspectives on the way to the title. Ernest Jones IV says of Sam Darnold and his redemptive journey at quarterback in Seattle: “I think he just models what everybody on that team’s been through. We’ve all been rejected, we’ve all… not been respected.” Darnold addressed Jones IV’s expletive-laden defense of him after a 4-INT performance against the Rams: “He had my back. It’s what I’ve kinda been talking about with this whole team: everyone had each other’s backs throughout the season. You come back into the locker room, and you just felt that brotherhood; we had a brotherhood, we had that love. And I felt that when E.J. said those things.” Darnold continued: “I don’t think it was a coincidence that we didn’t lose a game the rest of the year.” It was also amazing to hear that the “Dark Side” defense “actually ran out of blitzes in the 2nd quarter” of the big game. Super Bowl Champions: The 2025 Seattle Seahawks The Roku documentary, “Super Bowl Champions: The 2025 Seattle Seahawks” has been out since March, but it is an alternate view. It was more of a game-to-game summarizing of the journey. In the NFC Championship game, Rams head coach Sean McVay called the play when DeMarcus Lawrence dropped to the flats with Kyren Williams (to form bracket coverage of a hot route) a “fortuitous bust,” saying, “They kinda lucked into having two guys peel on Kyren right there I know that can’t be part of their design.” Even Seahawks coach, Mike Macdonald admitted that they “we actually didn’t even execute that play well on the fourth down.” For his part, D-Law laughed at the term, “fortuitous bust,” saying: “I’ll take it. I’ll take it all day.” Lawrence would go on to explain that “playing football as long as I done played, I’ve seen so many formations and schemes. The back is flaring out that fast, that means that’s his hot. He’s going to the back first. If the back wasn’t his hot, the back would’ve waited to see if Julian was gonna rush versus the end flaring out. But he didn’t wait.” Both documentaries displayed the resiliency, brotherhood and resolve of a title contender. They also showcase (as did Hard Knocks), the Hawks’ fearless leader and strategist. Mike Macdonald’s affable and quirky demeanor with the media gives way to a laser-focused intensity on the gridiron. It’s a joy to experience. In the “Super Bowl Champions” piece, Macdonald delivers the now famous line: “We did not care. It’s always been about us and what we do.” Here’s to watching this new Seattle Seahawks team and how they run it forward, in an attempt to reach that generational mountaintop once again. No matter what, the 2025 team was special. It was about them, not their opponents, and both the Roku as well as the America’s Game documentaries highlight that.

full_text: Nov 10, 2024; Tampa, Florida, USA; San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle (85) and defensive end Nick Bosa (97) prior to the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con There was a very notable absentee from the 49ers’ opening practice this week ahead of Thursday’s Week 1 clash with the Los Angeles Rams. Defensive end Nick Bosa was not present at the section of practice open to the media in Melbourne as he continues to manage knee tendonitis related to his ACL reconstruction. However, the former Defensive Player of the Year was seen in uniform without pads later on, suggesting the 49ers are simply playing it safe with the man set to lead their pass rush on Thursday. Also absent was running back Christian McCaffrey, though given his likely workload and his injury history, a rest day for the 49ers’ most important skill-position player would be no surprise. A number of previously injured 49ers were back today: * Renardo Green * Romello Height * Jacob Cowing * Vederian Lowe * Gracen Halton * Luke Gifford No Nick Bosa. Christian McCaffrey was on hand but did not practice. He might be on a practice pitch count all season. — Matt Barrows (@mattbarrows) September 7, 2026 Tuesday and Wednesday will give a better indication of where Bosa is at ahead of the season opener, but there’s reason to be more confident about the status of tight end George Kittle. Kittle practiced on Monday, a clear sign that he is on track to play in Week 1, almost eight months to the day of the Achilles rupture he suffered in the 49ers’ playoff win over the Philadelphia Eagles last season. In short, the 49ers will likely have all their stars on offense for a potential shootout with the Rams, but questions linger around the most important player on one of the weakest areas of their defense.

title: 49ers announced 2026 team captains (spoiler: it’s the same as 2025)
summary: The San Francisco 49ers have their 2026 team captains. The same list as 2025. During his Sunday press conference in preparation for the 49ers’ Thursday game against the Los Angeles Rams, Kyle Shanahan gave the list of team captains: TE George KittleOT Trent WilliamsLB Fred WarnerQB Brock PurdyDE Nick BosaRB Christian McCaffreyFB Kyle JuszcykCB Deommodore […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 28: San Francisco 49ers captains look on during a coin toss prior to the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Levi's Stadium on September 28, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers have their 2026 team captains. The same list as 2025 . During his Sunday press conference in preparation for the 49ers’ Thursday game against the Los Angeles Rams, Kyle Shanahan gave the list of team captains: TE George Kittle OT Trent Williams LB Fred Warner QB Brock Purdy DE Nick Bosa RB Christian McCaffrey FB Kyle Juszcyk CB Deommodore Lenoir As said above, if that list seems familiar, that’s because it’s the same list as last season. The 49ers vote on who makes it as a captain, so this means the leadership pecking order in the locker room remains unchanged. The 49ers are a very talented roster, but the fact that the list remains the same as a year ago, with no new faces, probably won’t help the criticisms that the team is too “old.” The ’newest’ name on this list is Lenoir, whose ascension last year essentially filled the vacancy left by Deebo Samuel. While we can debate the roster’s age all we want, established veterans doing the heavy lifting means they have capable leadership. Hopefully Bosa can stay on the field to help the defensive line turn a corner. The same goes for Brock Purdy and George Kittle. With a rookie De’Zhaun Stribling impressing in the preseason, having Purdy and Kittle to look up to will be invaluable. At the same time, who would you bump off that list? Those names are the backbone of the 49ers, and if someone like Trent Williams wasn’t on there, that would be strange. We’re a long way removed from 2017, Shanahan’s first season, and a season he did the captains a bit differently. Rather than elect team captains for the season, captains were rotated game-by-game. So each game, a different set of players walked out for the coin toss. Having this list of captains isn’t surprising, and certainly isn’t concerning either; those names have a lot of experience hoisting the workload onto their shoulders and can help keep the rest of the team stabilized. That said, it’s really hard to think of any of those names not being a captain in 2027 because they were no longer on the team.

title: 49ers DL has a broken foot, hopes to return later in the season
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are preparing for their Week 1 contest against the Los Angeles Rams in Australia later this week, but they’ll be without one of their top rotational defensive linemen. Head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed that defensive end Sam Okuayinonu broke his foot, calling it a “bad injury.” The team is hoping he […]
full_text: Jan 5, 2025; Glendale, Arizona, USA; San Francisco 49ers defensive tackle Sam Okuayinonu (91) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The San Francisco 49ers are preparing for their Week 1 contest against the Los Angeles Rams in Australia later this week, but they’ll be without one of their top rotational defensive linemen. Head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed that defensive end Sam Okuayinonu broke his foot, calling it a “bad injury.” The team is hoping he can return later in the season, but the loss is a blow for the 49ers’ defensive line, which is already without Mykel Williams, who is starting the year on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list. With Okuayinonu out, the 49ers signed defensive end Khalid Kareem to the practice squad over the weekend. He could see the field as early as Week 1. Currently, the Niners have Keion White, Nick Bosa, Romello Height, and Kareem as the healthy defensive ends on the roster, while Osa Odighizuwa, Alfred Collins, C.J. West, Gracen Halton, and James Thompson Jr. are the healthy interior defensive linemen. Okuayinonu did not travel with the 49ers and was placed on Injured Reserve over the weekend. We’ll see now if he can return before the end of the season. The 28-year-old defensive lineman has been one of the success stories for the 49ers over the past few years, being a versatile lineman who could slide inside on passing downs. He had 39 tackles, three sacks, and a forced fumble last year. According to Matt Barrows, the injury occurred when Okuayinonu, who previously had a plate in his foot, was stepped on in practice last week. He’ll now have to have surgery on his foot and will likely miss a significant portion of the 2026 season.

title: Brayden Willis goes unclaimed; set to return to the practice squad
summary: The San Francisco 49ers waived tight end Brayden Willis Saturday to make room for long snapper Jon Weeks on the active roster. Per the NFL’s transaction wire, Willis went unclaimed. Willis showed positional versatility during the preseason, but he was also a 7th-rounder from ’23 with as many regular-season receptions since then as you and […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 20: San Francisco 49ers tight end Brayden Willis (9) walks off of the field after the NFL preseason game between the Los Angeles Chargers and the San Francisco 49ers on August 20, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers waived tight end Brayden Willis Saturday to make room for long snapper Jon Weeks on the active roster. Per the NFL’s transaction wire, Willis went unclaimed. Willis showed positional versatility during the preseason, but he was also a 7th-rounder from ’23 with as many regular-season receptions since then as you and I. That means the team can bring him back to the practice squad and potentially elevate him to the active roster for this upcoming week against the Rams. He’s expected to practice with the team after re-joining the practice squad, as he did not leave Australia, per Matt Maiocco. Willis’s best chance to contribute offensively is at fullback. During this past preseason, he lined up at fullback 15 times. Kyle Juszczyk recently returned to practice after breaking his finger. If Juszczyk can’t perform his usual duties or gets hurt again, Willis is his logical backup — assuming the team would have him on the active roster so he can play special teams. Juszczyk is entering the final year of his two-year contract . He’s 35. It makes you wonder if the 49ers want to keep Willis around to take over for Juszczyk if this ends up being Juice’s final year as a Niner. In my opinion, Willis offers more out of the backfield than as a tight end. That was likely part of the reason he was waived. Another reason, and unquestionably the most important, was that George Kittle is ready to go for Week 1. If that were not the case, the 49ers wouldn’t run the risk of waiving a tight end during their game week when they’re playing in Australia. The 49ers must be confident in what they’ve seen from Kittle. The masses will spend the next few days talking everything Rams, while we’re less than a year away from Kittle catching all nine of his targets from Mac Jones for four first downs, a touchdown, and 84 receiving yards. Not to mention Kittle being the greatest asset as a blocker in the running game. Whether he’s catching passes against the Rams weak link, their linebackers, or neutralizing their defensive line, Kittle on the field is one of the biggest net positives for any team. That’ll only increase with Mike Evans and Brock Purdy on the field. We’ll keep a close eye on how often the backup tight end duo of Luke Farrell and Jake Tonges spell Kittle, since it’ll be his first live action since George’s Achilles injury in the playoffs .

title: A slow start could sink the Buccaneers
summary: Football is back and for the Buccaneers it is a chance to get the sour taste of last year’s collapse out of their mouths. Sure football is a 17 game season and as last year showed, it doesn’t quite matter as much how you start, it’s how you finish. However, in this particular case with […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 28: Head coach Todd Bowles of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers against the Jacksonville Jaguars during a preseason game at EverBank Field on August 28, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Football is back and for the Buccaneers it is a chance to get the sour taste of last year’s collapse out of their mouths. Sure football is a 17 game season and as last year showed, it doesn’t quite matter as much how you start, it’s how you finish. However, in this particular case with this team, a fast start is critical. Slow starts have not been a thing for Tampa Bay since Todd Bowles became head coach. In fact, the Bucs have started 2-0 in every season under Bowles and began last year’s campaign 3-0. During Bowles’ four-year tenure as head coach, the Bucs record in games through the first six weeks of the season is 18-6. That is a very good pace and something Tampa Bay will need to try and replicate in 2026. The Bucs aren’t exactly starting off with the steepest of competition in the first six weeks either. Of the first six games played, only two of them will be against playoff teams from 2025 with those teams being the Green Bay Packers who come to town in week four and the Pittsburgh Steelers who will visit in week six. There is a real opportunity for Tampa Bay to come out of the gates out and they shouldn’t let it go to waste. Why is a fast start so important for this year in particular? It’s quite simple. Noise. After a brutal and embarrassing second half collapse in 2025 which saw the team start 6-2 only to finish 8-9 and miss the playoffs the Bucs decided to retain head Todd Bowles and instead made changes elsewhere along the coaching staff. Many fans were not pleased with the decision to keep Bowles, and they let their frustrations very clear. Not only did they keep the head coach who was not so popular, but just a few months later franchise legends Lavonte David and Mike Evans would depart with David retiring and Evans headed to San Francisco to join the 49ers. So not only did the team just suffer one of the worst collapses in franchise history, but they kept the head coach in place and then lost two of the most popular players and all-time franchise icons… yikes. Then the summer came and there were some uncomfortable conversations being had about Baker Mayfield’s status with the team beyond this year after the team and the quarterback could not get a long-term deal done before the deadline Mayfield had set. Mayfield was very vocal in expressing his frustrations in not getting a deal done and now enters 2026 in a contract year. So what would a slow start do to this team? It could cause a lot of unwanted drama. Let’s say the team starts the season 2-4 with some disappointing losses along the way, the conversations would immediately turn to “is Todd Bowles coaching for his job soon?” or “if this gets bad enough will they bench Baker Mayfield?” these questions are not something the Bucs want to be asked at any point this season because if they are being brought up, then that means a lot of jobs will be on the line and the team would look a lot different in 2027. It was a tough offseason for many fans after a disappointing end to the previous year but at the end of the day winning cures all and the Buccaneers have a golden opportunity in front of them to put up some wins early to give the fans something positive to talk about and look forward to each week rather than a weekly football soap opera.

title: The Athletic stupidly writes off Commanders’ season before it starts

The Commanders missed their opportunity to build a contender during Jayden Daniels’ rookie contract window. Daniels will be eligible for an extension next season and will likely reset the market. If he’s healthy, he can elevate this team as he did in his rookie season, but let’s be real, this isn’t a Super Bowl-worthy roster. [T]he Commanders should be identifying who they want to keep as building blocks for their next team build-out, and they will have to be more economical. To read more of this stupid article, CLICK HERE COMMANDERS COLLAPSE TALK GOES TOO FAR: National Panic Is Overblown Last Man Standig (paywall) Let’s talk about what’s right with the Commanders Daniels looked sharp. Get past the initial two camp practices when, per usual, the defense was a step ahead of the offense, and he cooked. Daniels’ accuracy was among the most consistent positives throughout camp, all while appearing increasingly comfortable within first-time coordinator David Blough’s offense. Daniels looked spry all summer, and there was nary a conversation over the offseason about lingering problems. We should also note his resilient, Gumby-like body when it comes to absorbing blows. Whatever else you think about the Commanders, their ceiling looks considerably different with No. 5 available. For more from Ben Standig, click here Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) How David Blough can help the Commanders run game In this post, we’re going to look at how Blough can help make things easier for the offensive line in the run game through various schematic tweaks. Running the ball effectively is one of the best ways to help mask any offensive line issues you may have, because it’s much easier for those lineman to work forward on run blocks than sit back and pass protect. But running the ball effectively isn’t always easy. The Commanders face some good interior defensive lineman early in the season and just calling a bunch of run plays on their own won’t work. Blough will have to have more up his sleeve. One of the first weapons he has in his arsenal is motion. Under Kliff Kingsbury, the Commanders opted against using much motion in order to get lined up quickly and be able to go up-tempo. But Blough is planning to slow things down a lot more, which opens up the ability to use more motion. Just using motion for the sake of using it adds nothing to an offense, but used correctly, it can really help out the offensive line. The Commanders are expected to transition to more of a zone-based run scheme this year under David Blough. @nick_akridge and I breaking down some film from the Commanders preseason game vs Miami to show some of the nuances of zone running pic.twitter.com/m2T5bmYigv — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) August 18, 2026 To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Wire Commanders WR has one word to describe offense vs. Eagles in Week 1 When Abraham asked, “What is this offense going to be like?” Lane quickly responded, “Yeah, it’s going to be explosive! We got a lot of explosive guys on the field. And Blough and the rest of the offensive side, they’ve been putting us in great positions to use our explosiveness. So, expect an explosive offense. I’m excited.” I caught up with Commanders second year WR Jaylin Lane after today's practice. About the David Blough offense that will be unleashed against the Eagles, Jaylin told me, "it's going to be explosive…I'm excited." pic.twitter.com/L7s9Ax5ZBk — Scott Abraham (@Scott7news) September 1, 2026 To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Final commanders rookie power rankings: Who rose most before Week 1? 3. EDGE Joshua Josephs — Previous: No. 2 Joshua Josephs has been the most consistent rookie riser on the roster since the pads came out. While he did technically “fall” on this list, it shouldn’t be viewed negatively; Styles merely passed him. Josephs was able to capitalize on injuries to players above him on the depth chart . The extra field time he saw in camp, joint practice sessions, and the preseason led to what defensive coordinator Daronte Jones loves to see out of his guys: disruption. What’s wild about Josephs’ rise over the course of camp is the fact that Washington specifically targeted, and spent a good portion of cap space on that exact position room. After the draft, many wondered if he’d even make the team with Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson added to the mix and Dorance Armstrong returning from injury . That led to the August question: could Josephs force his way onto the team? Which, of course, after his play on the field, turned into: how many regular-season snaps will the team give him now? To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Roundtable How Washington’s rookies fared this offseason & preseason Matt Gulbin is the one who may have been most discussed among the Commanders’ fanbase where the rookie arrived as a center, though drew reps at guard before Quinn moved him back exclusively to center over the final week of training camp. The sixth round pick proved to be one of two offensive line rookies on the 53-man roster alongside Tanoa Togiai, yet Gulbin allowed just two hurries through the first two games to clearly outplay Julian Good-Jones to earn the backup center job. “I think over the course of the summer and over the course of training camp, we saw development in Matt,” Newmark said. “We saw growth in Matt and really excited with where he’s at currently and what we project him to develop into.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) Bold NFL 2026 season predictions Washington Commanders: A rookie will star, but not the one most expect First-round linebacker Sonny Styles has given little reason to think he won’t have a solid rookie year with the Commanders. But third-round receiver Antonio Williams, an unheralded selection at No. 71, will be the team’s young breakout star of 2026. Williams, a 5-foot-11, 195-pound receiver out of Clemson, boasted a quiet confidence and a skill set that will make him a go-to target for Jayden Daniels and a key piece of the team’s future. Williams has the versatility to play inside and out, despite playing primarily in the slot in college. He also has the route-running polish of a veteran and a knack for making contested over-the-shoulder catches appear easy. Washington already has a third-round receiving gem in Terry McLaurin. Williams may be next. — Nicki Jhabvala To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Texas Longhorns WR Ryan Wingo should be on Commanders’ draft radar after dazzing Week 1 display Wingo finished with seven catches from eight targets for 121 receiving yards and one touchdown. While the standard he was facing wouldn’t exactly be classed as stellar, it was also a sign that the desired improvements have been made this offseason to become more influential. Simply put, this is a prospect the Commanders should be watching extremely closely from here on. Washington’s wide receiver room looks strong heading into the season. But as for the long term? It’s uncertain. Stefon Diggs, Dyami Brown, and Treylon Burks are all in contract years . Luke McCaffrey and Jaylin Lane have special-teams value but not much else right now. title: Commanders mailbag: Daronte Jones, David Blough, Adam Peters’ grand plan
summary: The NFL spends the entire summer building up to the regular season, with training camps and preseason games leading up to initial 53-man roster construction at the roster cut deadline.   Then you’ve got this relatively quiet week leading up to Labor Day, where nothing much outside a few mostly closed practices. Gone is the […]
full_text: The NFL spends the entire summer building up to the regular season, with training camps and preseason games leading up to initial 53-man roster construction at the roster cut deadline. Then you’ve got this relatively quiet week leading up to Labor Day, where nothing much outside a few mostly closed practices. Gone is the cutdown drama and all those practice video clips that are given too much stock. There’s a small dead period without roster moves or big news. We’re in it right now. Next week is officially Week 1 . In other words, go time. That makes this little lull a perfect time to discuss your questions and comments about what the Commanders have and what comes next. I asked for conversation topics and we got plenty. Let’s get right to them in this Commanders mailbag: I like the mystery to the coordinator plans. And I love that it’s hopefully going to be revealed in 3D Technicolor minimum 4K reality surprise the Iggles into getting embarrassed. And they need to reserve just enough surprises for Dallas. How this happens? No idea, not that it can’t happen, I just don’t know how it plays out. But there’s guys all over that D that should be able to add a few bumps to Hurts. — ComplainingIsAPayne The Commanders have played up the mystery element when talking about what we’ve seen schematically to this point, which is exactly what they should do heading into the 2026 campaign. We can point to Brian Flores and Mike Zimmer and others as Daronte Jones influences, but we’re not sure exactly how that will look. We can anticipate an attacking scheme with exotic looks when the Commanders blitz heavily or not. I think it’s fair to assume there will be plays where the pressure is the coverage and Washington tries to live in the offensive backfield. Jones should use mystery to his advantage, and then play off the Week 1 game tape in Week 2. With the schemes being implemented and the talent available, the Commanders should be a fun watch. Will this new offensive scheme commit to the run? Can the new defensive scheme stop the run? Last year the Bears created a blueprint to beat the Eagles which they did 24-15 — JayGrudenSucks I was at that game covering the Bears at the time, and it was a dominant showing to be sure. If you can run like the Bears did that day, you’re going to win a ton. There’s plenty we don’t know about how Commanders coordinator David Blough will ultimately call plays, but Ben Johnson’s influence is virtually guaranteed. That means a heavy reliance on the run game and playaction off of that. I would expect Blough to run a ton if its effective, using it as the foundation for everything else the Commanders do. Here’s a stark difference between the Bears’ roster assembly and what the Commanders did this offseason. Chicago gave eight-figure AAV deals to the entire interior offensive line. They invested heavily in Joe Thuney, Jonah Jackson and Drew Dalman. The Commanders spent elsewhere, and are trying to get by inside with Nick Allegretti and Chris Paul, alongside Sam Cosmi on the right. Washington has a first-round right tackle and spent heavy on Laremy Tunsil, who’s no longer available. Blough will have to adjust to that and play to the offense’s strength, which is at receiver and tight end. Is Washington’s strategy of turning over the roster 20-30% a year and signing veterans to one- and two-year deals going to become the way this team does business beyond just the first year or two of this front office? Unlike New England which started where we were in 2024 with a rookie quarterback and a questionable roster, they have made the commitments to go out and sign free agents LONG-TERM and garner some element of roster stability. Washington has avoided giving out any contracts that signal a player is going to be here for more than say 2 years, and I have never really seen an NFL team in the free agency era do that and be successful. — Ghost Rider I believe I’ve mentioned this before in the article comments but, for those unaware, I’m a huge salary-cap and roster construction nerd. Always have been. General manager Adam Peters’ current use of the salary cap – the Commanders are in a good space with it – follows the strategy of a team that A. has a franchise quarterback on a rookie deal who’s eligible for an extension soon. and B. hasn’t drafted well in the recent past. GMs love to hand out contract extensions to homegrown players. It’s a pat on the back for a smart draft pick and a reward for a player working well within an organizational culture. Problem is that the Commanders have no one to extend. They paid Sam Cosmi. Smart move. They invested in a young, presumably ascending free agent like Odafe Oweh (four years) and gave three-year deals to Leo Chenal and Chig Okonkwo. Everything they’ve done to this point is about preparing to absorb the Daniels extension and function well after that. You can generally keep the first year cap number of a massive deal low (thanks to a signing bonus), so Washington can afford to pay bigger salaries to free agents over the next few years. In the Patriots example, Drake Maye was in his second season, so they had three years to spend big on other positions. The Commanders lost a year in 2025, and are in a slightly different boat. Does the team increase its life insurance coverage for the players (and traveling fans) when playing in Philly? — via Eidolons Visiting fans have to pay a premium for hit-by-battery coverage, but it’s always worth it. Those guys love chucking AAs. But, buyer beware: Dressing up as Santa Claus automatically voids the emotional distress plan. Get booed at your own risk. Is DQ’s hat on correctly if he walks backwards? — DGOLD510 This was but one question in a list of awesomeness y’all should check out in the mailbag Feed post. And, to answer this question directly, yes. And I’d love to see it. Quinn supposedly wears the hat backwards to create a relaxed environment and to foster players being themselves. Stories have been written on it. Like, several, to my shock. As a fellow backwards hat guy, I dig it.

full_text: Dec 21, 2025; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Rachaad White (1) with the ball in the third quarter at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images | Bob Donnan-Imagn Images The Daily Slop – 6 September 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Week 1 is almost here! Make sure you download the SB Nation app so you’re ready next week for Commanders-Eagles! Apple: https://t.co/c0Vz4X8AsM Android: https://t.co/6rxS81SpUA — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) September 4, 2026 Articles ESPN Inside Commanders DC Daronte Jones’ unusual coaching journey BEFORE ARRIVING IN Washington, Jones had held 14 different jobs during his coaching career, from Division II to Division I-AA, high school, the Canadian Football League to multiple Division I stops and stints with three NFL teams. “Perseverance is the best word that describes him,” said Morgan State coach Damon Wilson, Jones’ boss at Bowie State. “He’s had to endure a lot of things to get to where he is.” THE COMMANDERS HAVE felt the results of Jones’ experiences. Commanders coach Dan Quinn said he has sat in on meetings run by Jones, listening to him ask questions of his position coaches — “What could have been done better in this scenario?” — almost like a teacher. “When you go through difficult circumstances, there’s a resiliency that gets developed,” Quinn said. “And one of the other things I love about him, there’s not one step that he’s missed in the coaching journey. He’s got remarkable teaching; he’s got perspective.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Rachaad White has everything riding on his one-year audition with the Commanders The dual-threat’s deal in Washington is for only one year and worth a paltry $2 million . The NFL made a clear statement to him last spring: after being supplanted by Bucky Irving in Tampa, he wasn’t in very high demand. In 2025, White saw his numbers decline across the board , with his fewest rushing yards since his rookie year and fewest targets, receptions, and receiving yards of any of his four NFL campaigns. But now he’s in a position where he has a clear role, because his backfield running mate Jacory Croskey-Merritt is not a pass-catcher. If all goes well for White, he could considerably raise his stock and earn himself a lot more money next time around . Playing a position where even the slightest falloff makes you damaged goods, it won’t be easy for him to re-establish himself. But it won’t be impossible either. The Commanders will rotate Croskey-Merritt and White, perhaps with some interludes from sixth-round rookie Kaytron Allen depending on the situation. Under Blough, who comes from a coaching tree that loves to establish the run, there should be plenty of chances for all of them to touch the ball. White should get the bulk of the third-down snaps, and it helps him that he already has a rapport with Daniels. In the best of worlds, he can play a D’Andre Swift-like role for Washington, where he and Croskey-Merritt complement each other and become the bread and butter of Blough’s offense. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Commanders’ 20-Kicker Search Now Rests on Undrafted Rookie Drew Stevens Washington has used seven different kickers since Dan Quinn took over as head coach of the Washington Commanders. 2025 is probably the best example, with Washington finishing 29th in the NFL in field-goal percentage (76.7) . Matt Gay was so bad that the team moved on; Moody actually provided a late-season spark, going 10-of-11 over the last six games. That spark didn’t prove to be enough for Washington to hand the job back to him in 2026, as the franchise wants to lock this position up long-term and get away from temporary solutions, so they brought in Stevens to compete with him . To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) NFL Hope-O-Meter 2026 results: Rams fans are feeling good; Browns backers? Not as much 28. Washington Commanders: 35.1 percent optimism Pessimist: The offensive line lost Tunsil, and we don’t have depth. If we are leaky again (looks likely), Daniels will be running for his life! Pessimist: Outside of Jayden Daniels, the roster just isn’t very talented. Optimist: Getting younger and faster on defense, upgrading the receiver room and changing the offensive scheme. This team rises and falls with the health of Daniels. If he’s healthy: playoff bound. If he isn’t: Peters and Quinn are both on the hot seat. Pessimist: If a blade of grass grows over five inches, our quarterback trips and is injured. Optimist: Jayden Daniels deserves a resurgence. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Ringer NFC East Preview Washington Commanders Reasons for Optimism The Commanders were 5-12 last season, but they had a lot of things working against them. Daniels wasn’t healthy and started just seven games. They were 31st in turnover EPA. They were 30th in AGL , which measures which teams were most hurt by injuries. And they were 1-5 in games decided by seven points or fewer. As mentioned above with the Eagles, turnover luck, injury luck, and performances in close games are not typically things that carry over from one year to the next. The 2025 Commanders got quite unlucky with those things. Perhaps the 2026 Commanders will land more around league average in those categories. If Daniels regains the magic from his rookie season, that will give Washington its most direct path to a playoff berth. Last year, he ranked 25th in EPA per pass play and 15th in success rate among 37 qualifying quarterbacks. The difference in the two numbers suggests that Daniels was slightly above average down to down, but he got dinged by turnovers and a lack of explosive plays. Like the Eagles, the Commanders appear to be implementing a massive offensive scheme change, going from Kliff Kingsbury to David Blough. Blough has just two years of coaching experience and will be calling plays for the first time. The expectation is that Washington will implement more under-center, play-action schemes, as opposed to Kingsbury’s shotgun, up-tempo spread attack. The scheme change on defense also appears to be significant. Quinn hired Daronte Jones from Minnesota, and he is expected to employ a creative Brian Flores–style attack with heavy blitzing to make up for roster deficiencies. Jones has an intriguing background, but like Blough, he has never been an NFL coordinator before. In addition to the scheme change, the Commanders overhauled their personnel, adding edge defenders Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson in free agency and drafting linebacker Sonny Styles seventh. If Jones proves to be a capable schemer, there are some pieces to work with here. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Podcasts & videos Take Command: The Paulsen’s see the needle pointing up for Washington Gearing Up For The Season With Quarterback Jayden Daniels | The Player’s Club NFC East links Blogging the Boys How the Cowboys season could go wrong For a defense that was as dreadful as it was last year, it’s a little strange to see so much optimism for this current group. The overhaul is real. Between the coaching staff and players, this is a completely different group, so drawing comparisons to the 2025 unit makes little sense. While the optimism is warranted, we must also understand that new defensive schemes don’t manifest into greatness overnight. There is an expected learning curve when a new coach shows up. A new philosophy with an influx of new components opens the door for communication breakdowns and blown assignments. title: NFL team previews 2026: Predictions, rankings, depth charts
summary: Here's everything you need to know for the 2026 regular season, including how all 32 NFL teams rank and key stats ahead of Week 1.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL season kicks off Wednesday with a Super Bowl rematch featuring the reigning champion  Seattle Seahawks hosting the New England Patriots  ( 8:20 p.m. ET, NBC ). Then, on Thursday, the NFL will have its first-ever regular-season game in Australia , where the Super Bowl-favorite  Los Angeles Rams will take on the San Francisco 49ers  ( 8:35 p.m. ET, Netflix ). 

 To welcome back football, we're previewing every single team in the league. Our NFL Nation reporters identified strengths and concerns for all 32 rosters, and then they laid out what would make 2026 a successful season. Analyst Matt Bowen gave a fantasy nugget for each team, analytics writer Seth Walder made 32 bold predictions, and ESPN Research provided QB stats to know.

 Plus, our Football Power Index predicted chances for every team to win its division, make the playoffs and more. The model even suggested best- and worst-case scenarios for all 32 teams, based on the 90th- and 10th-percentile outcomes across thousands of simulations, respectively.

 This is everything you need to know for the start of the season, which will conclude Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, for Super Bowl LXI on ESPN.

 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LV | LAC | LAR | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SEA 
 SF | TB | TEN | WSH 

 

 

 

 1. Los Angeles Rams 
 Chances to make the playoffs: 84.9% 
 Chances to win division: 50.4% 
 Projected wins: 11.3 
 Strength of schedule: Third hardest 
 2025 record: 12-5

 Biggest strength: The passing game. There are several options to choose from on this star-studded roster, but it's hard not to pick the reigning MVP. Quarterback Matthew Stafford is coming off the best season of his career and will again have one of the best receiver pairs in the NFL: Davante Adams and Puka Nacua . Last season, Adams led the league with 14 receiving touchdowns, and Nacua led the NFL with 129 catches. -- Sarah Barshop 

 Biggest concern: Offensive tackle. The Rams don't have much depth at tackle, which could matter if left tackle Alaric Jackson is suspended. The NFL is conducting its own investigation into an alleged incident of domestic violence by Jackson, who is not facing criminal prosecution because his case was assigned for diversion . Third-round pick Keagen Trost , who was expected to back up Jackson and Warren McClendon Jr ., left the preseason opener with a hamstring injury. Coach Sean McVay said he's hopeful Trost will return to start the season. -- Barshop 

 QB stat to know:  Stafford is coming off a career-high 46 passing touchdowns -- his third season with 40 or more passing scores. Those three seasons are tied for the most by any QB in NFL history along with Aaron Rodgers  and Tom Brady. However, Stafford has seen major regression following each season of 40 passing TDs -- including going from 41 to 20 in 2012 and going from 41 to 10 in 2022. -- ESPN Research 

 Best-case scenario for 2026, per FPI: 14-3 
 Worst-case scenario for 2026, per FPI: 9-8

 This season is a success if ...  the Rams win the Super Bowl. The Rams took steps to maximize the remaining time that Stafford wants to play, so expectations are sky-high for Los Angeles. -- Barshop 

 One key fantasy nugget: The Rams regularly isolate Adams in scoring position given his ability to win off the release. His 14 touchdown receptions on end zone throws last season were the second most in a season this century (Randy Moss had 16 in 2007). -- Bowen 

 Bold prediction for 2026: Tight end Terrance Ferguson will catch eight touchdown passes. I'm buying the hype here because it just makes too much sense. The Rams need a third pass catcher behind Nacua and Adams, and with a year of experience in the league after being a 2025 second-round pick, Ferguson could emerge as that guy. If either of those two receivers misses time, his ceiling could be even higher. -- Walder

 2. Buffalo Bills 
 Chances to make the playoffs: 84.1% 
 Chances to win division: 67.1% 
 Projected wins: 10.7 
 Strength of schedule: 14th easiest 
 2025 record: 12-5

 Biggest strength: Josh Allen . It's pretty simple. The Bills have an opportunity to win a Super Bowl once again this year, despite a first-time head coach, and that's because of who is playing quarterback. Allen, 30, is going into his ninth NFL season and has a new No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore . Breaking records has become commonplace for the 2024 MVP, and Allen gives the team a chance in every game. -- Alaina Getzenberg 

 Biggest concern: It is a transition year for the new defensive scheme. Coordinator Jim Leonhard has been open about the fact this year's defense will not fully look like his vision for the unit as it transitions from a 4-3 to 3-4 base. There is a mix of new players who fit the scheme specifically and carryovers from the previous regime. How the group comes together will go a long way in determining the unit's success. -- Getzenberg 

 QB stat to know:  Allen's dual-threat ability is unlike anything the NFL has seen. Allen already has 299 passing and rushing TDs combined in his first eight seasons, 40 more than the next-closest player ( Patrick Mahomes , 259). In fact, he already has the most through a player's first nine seasons (next closest: Peyton Manning, 288). -- ESPN Research 

 Best-case scenario for 2026, per FPI: 13-4 
 Worst-case scenario for 2026, per FPI: 8-9

 This season is a success if ...  the Bills reach the Super Bowl. Unfortunately for new coach Joe Brady, that's the bar. Maximizing Allen's tenure is the priority, and anything comparable to or less than what Sean McDermott accomplished won't make for a fully successful season. -- Getzenberg 

 One key fantasy nugget:  Allen gives fantasy managers a major boost when the Bills have the ball on the doorstep of the end zone. He converted 22 of 28 true goal-line carries (78.6%) over the past three seasons. -- Bowen 

 Bold prediction for 2026: Wide receiver Keon Coleman will record 750 or more receiving yards and at least five touchdowns -- both career highs. Earlier this offseason I thought there was a decent chance he'd be on a different team by now. But Coleman also hasn't been that bad in his first two years, posting a 49 overall score in ESPN's receiver score (just below average) and 1.6 yards per route run.
